1636.content: In focused interviews with 201 former opiate addicts located by snowball referral (half untreated, half treated), Waldorf found that once addicts decided to quit they had to leave the scene, break all ties with opiate users and build new interests, new social networks and new social identities; some did this alone and some through existing institutions. He describes six patterns of recovery, including conversion to religious, social or communal causes, retiring from the drug while keeping the lifestyle, and moving on to other drugs, usually alcohol, and concludes that 'maturing out' does not describe them all.
Among the six recovery patterns, Waldorf reports that some former addicts had used opiates in certain situations and changed when the situation changed.

1637.content: From in-depth interviews with 46 people formerly dependent on alcohol or drugs who recovered without treatment, the authors describe how the social capital they had built before their addiction and kept during it (their relationships and the resources those gave access to) aided their recovery.

1638.content: In the first Swiss study of spontaneous remission (1988), Klingemann screened for and found 60 remitters with practically no treatment, 30 from problem alcohol use and 30 from heroin. All but two of the heroin remitters had stopped completely, while 14 of the 30 alcohol remitters had cut down almost to abstinence. No selection bias was detected against clinic populations, survey data and police records. From life histories he describes three stages: the motivation to change, carrying out the decision, and maintenance together with negotiating a new identity or meaning in life.

1639.content: A methodological review of natural recovery studies published to the end of 1997 found 38 articles (40 samples) that reported recoveries without formal help separately from treated ones. Alcohol was studied most, heroin a distant second. For most studies, the description of who was sampled before and after recovery was seriously deficient. Low-risk drinking (78.6%) and limited drug use (46.2%) were commonly reported outcomes. The authors call for studies that describe what events and processes go with self-change, check respondents' accounts against other sources, re-interview later and require at least five years of recovery.

1640.content: A systematic review of controlled studies of drug-free therapeutic communities, in which people with addiction problems live together in a structured community, found 16 original studies (30 publications; 9 in prisons, 7 in the community). About two out of three studies showed significantly better substance use and legal outcomes for residents than controls at the first follow-up, five found better employment and five better psychological functioning. Length of stay and taking part in aftercare afterwards were consistent predictors of recovery status; posttreatment employment and older age also went with abstinence. Differences against controls usually shrank over time, and only three of six studies with longer follow-up showed lower illegal drug use two years on.

The review states that residents typically improve during the first months in a therapeutic community and keep that status until they leave, and that once they leave success rates tend to drop quickly, especially in the first month or months. In the studies reviewed, 25% to 55% of respondents had relapsed to drug use 12 to 18 months after leaving; one controlled prison study that followed people three years after release found relapse in 77% of the therapeutic community group and 94% of controls. The authors name re-entry into the community as a critical point, when not prepared (for example by aftercare) or when former residents go back to their old neighbourhoods, and report that combining the community with aftercare gave the best results.

1641.content: A Cochrane review of randomised trials of therapeutic communities (searches to March 2004) found seven trials, too different to pool. The authors found little evidence that therapeutic communities do better than other residential treatment, or that one type of community beats another. In two prison trials, a therapeutic community led to fewer reincarcerations 12 months after release than no treatment (RR 0.68) or a mental health treatment programme (RR 0.28). Methodological limits prevented firm conclusions.

1642.content: A systematic review of 12 studies covering 3,271 people in 61 therapeutic communities found that residents stayed on average a third of the planned time and that 9% to 56% completed. In all studies substance use fell during the stay, and relapse was frequent after leaving. Completing the programme was the strongest factor linked to abstinence at follow-up; comorbid psychiatric diagnoses as reported by the studies did not go with relapse or dropout.

1643.content: In 248 opioid addicts from San Antonio, Texas, followed for a mean of 20 years, 171 reported 465 moves away from San Antonio. They were voluntarily abstinent 54% of the time while living elsewhere and 12% of the time while living in San Antonio. One-year abstinence followed 17% of relocations, nearly three times the 6% after 1,654 treatment and correctional contacts, and 31% when treatment came before the move. The authors name drug availability, conditioned abstinence and peer modelling as possible explanations, and suggest relocation of patients should often be encouraged.
In the same cohort, when men who had been abstinent away from San Antonio returned to the city, they resumed opioid use within one month in 81% of cases.

1644.content: The California Civil Addict Program cohort: 581 men admitted in 1962 to 1964 to a compulsory treatment programme for heroin-dependent offenders, followed through interviews in 1974 to 1975, 1985 to 1986 and 1996 to 1997. By 1996 to 1997, 284 had died and 242 were interviewed (mean age 57.4). Of those interviewed, 20.7% tested positive for heroin, a further 9.5% refused a urine test and 14.0% were in custody; 40.5% reported heroin use in the past year. The authors conclude that heroin use patterns were remarkably stable for the group as a whole, and that for some heroin addiction had been lifelong.
In the same 33-year follow-up, long-term heroin abstinence went with less criminality, less illness, less psychological distress and higher employment.

1645.content: In 242 heroin users from the California Civil Addict Program followed for more than 30 years, those who reached stable recovery and those who did not did not differ in deviant behaviour or family and school problems earlier in life, and both groups had tried formal treatment and self-directed quitting, often many times.

In the same cohort, the men who had not recovered were more likely to use substances to cope with stress, to have spouses who also abused drugs, and to lack social support from people who did not use drugs. In the prospective analysis, stable recovery ten years later was predicted only by ethnicity, self-efficacy and psychological distress; the spouse and social support measures did not add to the prediction.

1646.content: In a prospective study of 132 adults entering a residential therapeutic community in regional Australia (mostly never married and not in full-time work), identification with substance-using groups fell and identification with the recovery community rose over the first weeks; 76% weakened their user identity in the first month. Sixty were followed up about seven months after leaving. After allowing for age, severity and identity at entry, the gap between recovery identity and user identity at follow-up accounted for 34% of the variance in drinks per drinking day, 41% in days abstinent from drinking, about 5% to 6% in days abstinent from other drugs, and 49% in life satisfaction.

The authors report that participants who still identified with their substance-using peers at follow-up had much poorer outcomes on every measure of substance use and life satisfaction, while those who kept their recovery social identity showed positive outcomes.

1647.content: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials of Housing First (rapid, permanent housing not conditional on abstinence, with case management or assertive community treatment) found four trials, all from North America and all at high risk of bias, in homeless adults selected for complex needs. Housing First participants spent more days housed (SMD 1.24) and were more likely to be housed at 18 to 24 months (RR 2.46), and had fewer emergency visits and hospitalisations. No clear difference in substance use was seen against usual care.

On substance use, the review reports that the Pathways Housing First trial found no significant difference in alcohol or drug use at 24 months; Padgett and colleagues reported a greater fall in heavy alcohol use over 48 months in the Housing First group with no clear difference in drug use; and pooling the age subgroups of the At Home/Chez Soi trial gave a very small difference in self-reported problematic substance use favouring Housing First (ratio of rate ratios 0.96, 95% CI 0.72 to 1.28), with both arms reporting fewer problems over time.

In the one trial with subgroup analyses (At Home/Chez Soi), participants housed together in dedicated buildings (the congregate model) improved more than those in scattered flats in mental health, quality of life and problematic substance use, among other outcomes.

1648.content: House mice (Mus musculus, C57BL/6) were given cocaine until they showed behavioural sensitisation or a conditioned place preference, while housed four to a standard small cage. They were then kept either in the standard cage or in an enriched cage (larger, with a running wheel, a small house and four to five toys changed weekly; same cagemates throughout). In standard cages sensitisation (about 200% of the response of cocaine-naive mice) and the place preference lasted 30 days. After 30 days of enrichment the sensitised mice responded to cocaine like cocaine-naive mice, the place preference was gone, and enrichment prevented cocaine from reinstating an extinguished place preference.

1649.content: Male Sprague-Dawley rats (Rattus norvegicus) self-administered intravenous cocaine for 10 days, 6 hours a day, while housed alone. They were then housed three to a cage for 30 days of forced abstinence, either in standard cages or in large enriched cages (house, running wheel, three floors with ramps, four toys changed weekly). Rats from enriched cages sought cocaine less in a 6-hour extinction session and showed less reinstatement of seeking triggered by cocaine-paired cues or by the stressor drug yohimbine.

In the same rats, enrichment did not reduce reinstatement of cocaine seeking triggered by an injection of cocaine itself. The authors tested whether this depended on dose of exposure or time in the enriched setting by running further groups with less cocaine (10 days of 3-hour sessions) and with 90 days of enrichment; cocaine-primed reinstatement was not reduced under any of these conditions.

1650.content: Sprague-Dawley rats (Rattus norvegicus) were raised from 21 days of age in an enriched condition (living with other rats plus novel objects), with other rats only, with objects only, or alone. As young adults they self-administered cocaine for 14 days in 1-hour (short access) or 6-hour (long access) daily sessions. At the low dose (0.1 mg/kg per infusion) only rats raised without other rats escalated their intake under long access. At the higher dose (0.5 mg/kg per infusion), intake escalated under long access in both enriched and isolated rats; the enriched rats escalated faster and reached the same intake as the isolated rats.

1651.content: Male Long-Evans rats (Rattus norvegicus) lived alone or in pairs from weaning, and were tested in chambers that let both partners self-administer at the same time. In 14 days of 6-hour sessions all groups escalated their cocaine intake, but rats paired with a partner that had no access to cocaine took less throughout. In 23-hour sessions every third day, rats with a partner without cocaine took less than rats with a partner that also had cocaine, at every dose tested.

1652.content: Among 137 consecutive opiate addicts who went through a 28-day inpatient detoxification programme in south London and were followed for a year, three died of an overdose within four months of discharge, and all three were among the 37 who had completed both the detoxification and the whole programme (the group the authors classed as having lost tolerance). None of the 43 who left before finishing detoxification died (Fisher's exact test, P = 0.02). All five who died in the year, of any cause, had gone back to heroin. Tolerance itself was not measured; the authors read the clustering as lost tolerance meeting resumed heroin use.

In the same follow-up, the five patients who died had, before admission, more often been living alone than the other patients (4 of 5 against 21 of 130; Fisher's exact test, P = 0.004), had been prescribed higher methadone doses (mean 51.0 mg against 29.2 mg) and had used heroin on fewer days in the month before admission (14.4 against 24.5). All five were men.

1653.content: Laboratory rats (Norway rat, Rattus norvegicus) trained for 10 days to press a lever for intravenous cocaine, each living alone in a test chamber, were then kept in that chamber with the lever withdrawn and the light off for 1, 2, 4, 7, 15, 29 or 60 days (seven groups). When the lever came back without cocaine, pressing in the presence of the cocaine-paired cues was lowest after 1 day and highest after 60 days, rising linearly over the two months. The authors note this rise took place while most of the brain adaptations of cocaine withdrawal are in decline, and conclude that cocaine seeking does not fade after the drug stops but grows, so that vulnerability lasts well beyond acute withdrawal.

1654.content: In a cross-sectional laboratory study at Stony Brook, New York (2007 to 2012), 76 adults who met DSM-IV criteria for cocaine dependence (current, or in partial or sustained remission) were grouped by self-reported abstinence: 2 days, 1 week, 1 month, 6 months and 1 year. An EEG brain response to cocaine pictures (the late positive potential, a marker of motivated attention) was higher at 1 month (1.26 microvolts) and 6 months (1.17) than at 2 days (0.17), 1 week (0.36) and 1 year (-0.27), an inverted U. The participants' own ratings went the other way: baseline craving on the Cocaine Craving Questionnaire fell from 26.05 at 2 days to 3.00 at 1 year, and wanting and liking after cocaine pictures fell steadily too. The authors did not detect incubation of reported craving.

1655.content: Eighty-six adult smokers (10 or more cigarettes a day) who were not seeking to quit were paid 30 US dollars a day to abstain for 7, 14 or 35 days, checked daily; about half of those who began did not complete. On the Tobacco Craving Questionnaire short form, craving set off by smoking cues rose with assigned abstinence (linear trend, effect size r = 0.28) and was higher in the 35-day than the 7-day group, while craving reported before the cues and daily withdrawal symptoms fell. Cue-induced craving did not fall on any measure. The effects were small, appeared on some measures only, and smoking cues moved no bodily measure (heart rate, blood pressure, cortisol).

1656.content: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 237 prospective studies (656 statistics, 51,788 people, 21,216 of whom met the studies' criteria for a confirmed substance use disorder diagnosis) found that cue exposure, bodily cue reactivity, cue-induced craving and reported craving measured at one time point went with later drug use or relapse: each one-unit rise more than doubled the odds (odds ratio 2.05, 95% CI 1.94 to 2.15). The association held across drug types, settings and time lags, including lags over 6 months (odds ratio 1.73); craving set off by cues was the strongest single indicator (a one-point rise more than tripled the odds). There was publication bias: trim-and-fill brought the pooled odds ratio to 1.31 in the abstract (1.03 in the discussion), and results varied between studies.

1657.content: Five adults who met DSM-IV criteria for methamphetamine dependence, enrolled in a California drug-court rehabilitation programme with regular drug screens, had PET scans of striatal dopamine transporters at about 3 months of abstinence and again at about 14 months. Transporter availability rose by 19% in the caudate and 16% in the putamen, and the rise was larger the longer the interval. Across groups, users at short abstinence were 26% (caudate) and 21% (putamen) below 11 controls, while users at about 15 months were 5% and 9% below, a difference that was no longer significant. Motor and memory tests showed only non-significant trends to improve, which the authors read as incomplete recovery of function.

In the original 12 users first scanned within 6 months of abstinence, the 7 who dropped out of the detoxification programme (whom the authors call most likely relapsed) had had lower dopamine transporter levels at that first scan than the 5 who stayed off the drug (putamen 1.40 against 1.74, p < 0.03; caudate trend, p < 0.07), and did worse on the pegboard and delayed recall tests. The authors give two readings: those who stayed off may have had less damage to start with, or the recovery itself may have helped them stay off.

1658.content: Ten healthy men in Montreal (mean age 25.8) took three single oral doses of dextroamphetamine (0.3 mg per kg) on days 1, 3 and 5 in the laboratory. PET scans with [11C]raclopride showed that 14 days and 365 days after the third dose, a test dose of amphetamine released more dopamine in the ventral striatum than the first dose had, spreading to the dorsal caudate and putamen, and produced a greater psychomotor response. Men who rated higher on novelty seeking and impulsivity showed more of this sensitization.

1659.content: A systematic review of 38 studies of people with chronic pain who were taking opioids found that rates of misuse, as the review defined it, averaged 21% to 29% across calculations, and rates of addiction averaged 8% to 12%. Single studies ranged from under 1% to 81%. Abuse was reported in only one study. Addiction rates were lower in studies that set out to count them as their main aim.

1660.content: A Cochrane review of 26 studies (25 case series or uncontrolled trial extensions and one trial comparing two opioids; 4,893 people with chronic non-cancer pain, mostly back pain, osteoarthritis or nerve pain) found signs of opioid addiction in 0.27% of participants (7 of 2,613) in the studies that reported it, or 0.14% if the studies that did not mention addiction had none. Most studies screened out people with a history of addiction or abuse, and all gave opioids under ongoing medical supervision; the authors say the rate does not apply to unselected patients.

1661.content: In US insurance claims (HealthCore, 2000 to 2005) for 568,640 adults with a new episode of chronic non-cancer pain and no opioid use or opioid use disorder diagnosis in the prior 6 months, a new diagnosis of opioid abuse or dependence in claims within the next year was recorded for 0.004% of those given no opioids and for 6.1% of those given high doses for 91 days or more. Against no opioids, the adjusted odds ratios were about 3 for any short course (low, medium or high dose) and 14.92, 28.69 and 122.45 for low, medium and high doses taken 91 days or more. The authors conclude that how long opioids were given mattered more than the daily dose.

In the same 568,640 people, those diagnosed in the year before the pain episode with one type of mental health condition (odds ratio 3.12) or two (5.71) had higher odds of a new opioid use disorder diagnosis than those with none, as did those diagnosed earlier with an alcohol use disorder (3.22) or with abuse of another drug (8.26).

1662.content: In US insurance claims for 2013 and 2014, 36,177 adults aged 18 to 64 who had filled no opioid prescription in the year before surgery filled one around a minor or major operation. About 6% (5.9% after minor and 6.5% after major surgery) were still filling opioid prescriptions 90 to 180 days later, against 0.4% of a comparison group without surgery.

The rate of continued opioid fills was about the same after minor operations (such as carpal tunnel release or gallbladder removal) as after major ones (such as colectomy or hysterectomy), although major surgery should bring more pain. Continued use went instead with conditions the patients had been diagnosed with: tobacco use, alcohol and other substance diagnoses, mood and anxiety diagnoses, and other pain conditions such as back pain and arthritis. In a 2019 correction the authors reported that these diagnoses had been counted from one year before to one year after surgery; after recalculation the significance of 5 characteristics changed and the overall conclusions stood.

1663.content: Dasgupta, Beletsky and Ciccarone argue that the US opioid crisis, though drug supply is a key factor, is fundamentally fuelled by economic and social upheaval, with opioids serving as a refuge from physical and psychological trauma, concentrated disadvantage, isolation and hopelessness. They call the prescribing-centred account a vector model that ignores where the demand for opioids comes from, and argue that cutting access alone offers illusory solutions.

The authors report that outpatient opioid prescriptions in the US fell 13% between 2012 and 2015 while the national overdose death rate rose 38% over the same years, and that people entering drug treatment were by then more likely to say they had started opioid use with heroin than with a prescription painkiller.

1664.content: Across US counties from 1999 to 2015, drug and opioid death rates rose more where the local economy declined, but the link was weak and mostly accounted for by confounding factors: in the preferred estimates economic change explained less than a tenth of the rise in deaths, and possibly none once plausible hidden differences between counties were allowed for. Death risk shifted between population groups in ways that fit the availability and cost of drugs, rising fastest for men and younger adults when illicit opioids replaced prescription ones.

1665.content: In 112 US manufacturing counties (mainly South and Midwest) that had a car assembly plant in 1999, the 29 counties whose plant closed were compared with the 83 whose plant stayed open (difference-in-differences, 1999 to 2016). Opioid overdose death rates started out similar (0.9 and 1.0 per 100,000). Five years after a closure, opioid overdose deaths among adults aged 18 to 65 were 8.6 per 100,000 higher in the affected counties (95% CI 2.6 to 14.6), 85% above the 12 per 100,000 in unaffected counties. The rise was largest among non-Hispanic white men aged 18 to 34 (20.1 per 100,000) and 35 to 65 (12.8), and showed for both prescription and illicit opioids.

1666.content: In 8,613 adults at a primary care clinic in California (the ACE Study), who reported in a survey on 10 categories of childhood abuse, neglect and household dysfunction and on their own drug use, each category went with 2 to 4 times the likelihood of starting illicit drugs early. Against people reporting none, those reporting 5 or more categories were 7 to 10 times more likely to report illicit drug use problems, addiction to illicit drugs and injecting drugs; the authors put the share of these problems attributable to the adverse experiences at 56%, 64% and 67%. The graded link held in four birth cohorts going back to 1900.

1667.content: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 37 studies (253,719 adults, general populations only) compared people reporting four or more adverse childhood experiences with people reporting none. Problematic drug use (injecting, or heroin or crack cocaine use) had the strongest link of the substance outcomes: pooled odds ratio 10.22 (95% CI 7.62 to 13.71) across 5 samples with low heterogeneity, against 2.20 for heavy drinking. Most included studies were cross-sectional with childhood experiences reported in retrospect.

A systematic review and meta-analysis of 37 studies (253,719 adults in general populations) compared people who reported four or more adverse childhood experiences with people who reported none, across 23 health outcomes. The group with four or more had higher odds of every outcome. The odds ratios were under 2 for physical inactivity, overweight or obesity and diabetes; 2 to 3 for smoking, heavy drinking, poor self-rated health, cancer, heart disease and respiratory disease; more than 3 to 6 for sexual risk taking, the outcomes the authors group as mental ill health, and problematic alcohol use; and more than 7 for problematic drug use and for violence against others and against oneself. Heterogeneity was considerable for almost half the outcomes.

1668.content: Lewis argues that the brain changes seen in addiction can be read within a learning framework, without reference to pathology or disease. Learning models, he writes, read addiction as a natural, context-sensitive response to hard circumstances, while the brain disease model reads the same learning as pathological brain change set off mainly by substance use. He points to repeated findings that adversity in childhood and adolescence and physical, economic or psychological trauma raise the chance of later addiction.

Lewis reports from cited studies that synaptic density in some prefrontal regions falls with the duration of drug use and that density in similar regions rises with weeks of abstinence, and that people who had met criteria for cocaine dependence and became abstinent no longer differed from controls in prefrontal inhibitory-control activation or task performance. He reads this as change limited to the period of habitual use, and as consistent with evidence that most people with addiction recover, most of them without treatment.

1669.content: Among Korean American adoptees placed by Holt International, who the author describes as quasi-randomly assigned to adoptive families, the standard behavioural genetics variance decomposition put the share of variation explained by the shared family environment at 14 percent for educational attainment, 35 percent for the selectivity of the college attended and 33 percent for drinking behaviour. The abstract gives no sample size.

In the same adoptee sample the author reports large effects on adoptees' education, income and health from assignment to parents with more education and to smaller families, and finds parental education and family size more strongly linked to adoptee outcomes than parental income or neighbourhood characteristics. The abstract gives these as effects without numbers.

1670.content: In the Colorado Adoption Project, a 20-year longitudinal adoption study of 245 adopted children with their biological and adoptive parents and 245 matched non-adoptive families, adopted children resembled their adoptive parents in cognitive ability slightly in early childhood and not at all in middle childhood or adolescence. Over the same years they came to resemble their biological parents, to the same degree as children and parents in the control families. The pattern was strongest for general cognitive ability and verbal ability and similar for spatial ability, speed of processing and recognition memory.

1671.content: In the Minnesota Study of Twins Reared Apart, more than 100 sets of identical and fraternal twins or triplets separated in infancy and reared apart were given a week of psychological and physiological assessment from 1979 on. On multiple measures of personality and temperament, occupational and leisure-time interests and social attitudes, identical twins reared apart were about as similar as identical twins reared together.

In the same study about 70 percent of the variance in IQ was associated with genetic variation, in line with earlier smaller studies of identical twins reared apart. The authors write that this evidence for strong heritability does not detract from the value or importance of parenting, education and other interventions.

1672.content: From the complete Swedish national register the authors found 436 male full-sibships in which one brother was reared by one or both biological parents and another by adoptive parents. At military conscription (age 18 to 20) the adopted brothers scored 4.41 IQ points higher (SE 0.75) than their home-reared brothers, and each step up on a 5-point scale of rearing parents' education went with 1.71 IQ points. In 2,341 male half-sibships adoption went with a gain of 3.18 points (SE 0.34).

1673.content: In Swedish national registers the authors found 666 full sibships and 2,596 half sibships in which at least one biological parent had been registered with a diagnosis of major depression and one sibling was reared at home while another was adopted away. Followed from age 15 to as late as 60, the adopted-away siblings were less often registered with a diagnosis of major depression: the risk was reduced by 23 percent in full sibships and by 19 percent in half sibships. The effect did not depend on the education of the adoptive parents relative to the biological ones.

In the same study the lower risk of being diagnosed with major depression among adopted-away siblings disappeared in both full and half sibships when an adoptive parent or a stepsibling had a registered depression diagnosis, or when the adoptive home was broken by a parent's death or a divorce before the adoptee was 15.

1674.content: Plomin and Daniels review twin, family and adoption studies of personality and report that in four adoption studies the average correlation between adoptive siblings reared together was .04 and between adoptive parents and adopted children .05. They conclude that environment shared by children in one family accounts for a negligible part of the environmental variance in personality, and report the same pattern for the psychopathology labels they review, and that environmental influences that differ between children in the same family (nonshared environment) explain perhaps 40 to 60 percent of total variance in these domains.

For IQ the same review reports that adoptive siblings still living at home correlate about .30, while a study of postadolescent adoptive siblings found -.03 and a study of 52 adoptive sibling pairs aged 9 to 15 found -.16, from which the authors conclude that shared family environment matters for IQ in childhood and fades to negligible importance by the end of early adolescence.

1675.content: Turkheimer and Waldron review the measured differences between siblings' environments (differential parenting, sibling interaction, peer groups, events) and find in a quantitative review that these measured nonshared environmental variables do not account for a substantial portion of the nonshared variance that twin and adoption studies attribute to environment. They note that when genetic similarity is controlled, siblings often appear no more alike than people picked at random.

1676.content: Harris examines the evidence on whether parents have important long-term effects on their child's personality and concludes that they do not. She proposes that socialization is specific to context and that outside the home it takes place in the peer groups of childhood and adolescence, where processes within and between groups, not one-to-one relationships, transmit culture and modify personality. She argues that the universality of children's groups explains why development is not derailed by wide variation in parental behaviour within and between societies.

1677.content: A systematic review of 55 independent twin and adoption studies of the heritability of measured environments (stressful life events, parenting as reported by the child and by the parent, family environment, social support, peer interactions and marital quality) found weighted heritabilities of 7 to 39 percent for the 35 measures examined by at least two studies, most between 15 and 35 percent, and 27 percent over all measures. By method the weighted heritability was 29 percent for self-report, 26 percent for informant report and 14 percent for direct observation.

1678.content: A meta-analysis of 32 children-as-twins studies of parenting (parents' behaviour toward each twin) estimated that the children's genes account for 23 percent of the variance in the parenting they receive, the shared environment for 43 percent and the nonshared environment for 34 percent. Assessment method, child age and the parenting dimension moderated these estimates.

1679.content: A systematic review of 89 genetically informative studies published 2014 to June 2020 (children-of-twins, adoption, sibling comparison, assisted conception, genetic nurture and polygenic score designs) found genetic transmission from parent to child for depression, criminal behaviour, educational attainment and substance use. After genetic effects were accounted for, several parental characteristics, among them parents' psychiatric traits and parenting behaviours such as harsh parenting, criticism and affection, were still associated with children's reported internalising and externalising problems, educational attainment, substance use and personality, which the authors read as environmental pathways.

Discussing the reviewed studies against the twin literature, the authors write that genes explain 40 to 80 percent of individual differences in internalising and externalising problems, that heritability of these rises with age while the influence of the shared family environment falls, and that the largest way parents influence their children's mental health is therefore through the genes they pass on. They add that the effect of any single parental environmental exposure is likely far lower than the heritability of the child's traits.

1680.content: A meta-analysis of 16 studies with 25,471 participants that measured childhood maltreatment both prospectively (records or reports in childhood) and retrospectively (adult recall) found poor agreement, Cohen kappa 0.19 (95% CI 0.14 to 0.24). On average 52 percent of people with prospective observations of maltreatment did not report it as adults, and 56 percent of adults who reported maltreatment had no matching prospective observation. Agreement was higher with interviews than questionnaires and was similar for records and reports.

1681.content: In the Dunedin cohort (New Zealand, N = 1,037), adverse childhood experiences recorded by study staff at ages 3 to 15 and recalled by the participants at 38 agreed moderately (r = .47, weighted kappa .31). Recalled adversity was more strongly associated with outcomes the participants rated themselves and more weakly with outcomes measured objectively (for example r .18 with self-rated poor physical health against r .07 with biomarker-indexed poor health, and r .40 with the authors' interview-based psychopathology score). Recalled adversity went with poor self-rated outcomes whether or not adversity had been recorded; people who recalled more than was recorded scored higher on neuroticism, and people who recalled less scored higher on agreeableness.

In the same cohort, adversity recorded in childhood but not recalled at 38 still went with poorer objectively measured physical and cognitive health in midlife. Associations of recorded adversity with adult outcomes were small and uniform (r .11 to .23), and remained for objective outcomes after controlling for recalled adversity; for self-rated outcomes they dropped to non-significance once recall was controlled.

1682.content: In two birth cohorts, the British E-Risk twin study (2,009 of 2,232 analysed, followed to 18) and the Dunedin study (918 of 1,037, followed to 45), prospectively measured ACE scores were associated with group differences in later health: in E-Risk each additional ACE raised the relative risk of any mental health problem, as assessed by the Diagnostic Interview Schedule, by 1.14 and of any physical health problem by 1.09. As individual predictors the scores were poor: area under the curve 0.58 for mental and 0.60 for physical health problems, where 0.50 is chance. Findings held in Dunedin with prospective and retrospective ACE measures.

1683.content: Fraley meta-analysed longitudinal studies of attachment security and fitted mathematical models of two accounts: a prototype account in which early representations are kept and keep shaping attachment, and a revisionist account in which new experience revises them. He found attachment security moderately stable across the first 19 years of life, with the pattern of stability best fitted by the prototype model.

1684.content: A meta-analysis of 127 papers covering 21,072 attachments to mothers and fathers and 225 time intervals from half a month to 29 years found an overall stability of attachment security of r = .39, a medium effect. Over intervals longer than 15 years there was no significant stability. Stability was higher over intervals under two years than over five years, with representational measures beyond infancy, and in middle-class samples than in at-risk samples; secure children at risk were less likely to stay secure and insecure children at risk most likely stayed insecure.

1685.content: In 551 twin pairs aged 15 from the Twins Early Development Study (UK), attachment assessed with the Child Attachment Interview correlated .42 in identical and .20 in fraternal twins on the Coherence scale. Model fitting gave about 40 percent heritability of attachment and a negligible shared-environment share; for secure against insecure classification, genes accounted for 35 percent (95% CI 22 to 48) and the nonshared environment for 65 percent. The authors note that earlier twin studies in infancy and the preschool years had found little genetic and strong shared-environment influence (52 percent shared in one infant study).

1686.content: Summarising their own meta-analyses, the authors report that early attachment security was associated with greater social competence with peers (d = 0.39), fewer externalizing problems (d = 0.31) and, more weakly, fewer internalizing symptoms (d = 0.15), and only slightly with negative temperament (d = 0.13). They describe the effects as modest, between Cohen's small and medium, and write that any simple notion that security determines children's peer interactions and aggression is likely incorrect.

1687.content: In 319 twin pairs aged 7 (114 identical, 205 fraternal) from the US National Collaborative Perinatal Project, a sample with many families near or below the poverty line, Wechsler IQ scores were modelled with genetic, shared and nonshared components allowed to vary with family socioeconomic status. In impoverished families the shared environment accounted for about 60 percent of IQ variance and genes for close to none; in affluent families the result was almost exactly the reverse.

1688.content: A meta-analysis of 43 effect sizes from 14 independent twin and sibling studies (24,926 pairs, about 50,000 people) tested whether genetic influence on intelligence and achievement test scores is smaller in poorer families. In the 8 US studies (10,831 pairs) the gene by socioeconomic status interaction was clear and moderate; in the 6 studies from Western Europe and Australia (14,095 pairs), where social policy gives more uniform access to education and health care, it was zero or reversed.

1689.content: Uchiyama, Spicer and Muthukrishna report that in the Polderman 2015 meta-analysis of essentially all twin studies published 1958 to 2012, 94 percent of twin pairs came from Western populations (the US, UK and Australia almost 60 percent, Nordic countries 25 percent), 4 percent from northeast Asia, and the rest of the world, the great majority of humans, only 2 percent. They argue that this narrow range of genes and cultural environments limits what heritability estimates can say about humans in general.

The authors review studies within countries over time, between countries and around policy changes showing that the heritability of educational attainment rises as educational opportunity becomes more equal, with some evidence in the other direction, and argue that heritability is a property of a society at a time: it rises when the environment is made more uniform and falls when access is unequal.

1690.content: In 1,018 pairs of female twins from a population-based registry (Virginia), the link between losing a parent before 17 and being diagnosed as an adult depended on the kind of loss. Separation from either parent went with a higher risk of being diagnosed with major depression and generalized anxiety disorder, and parental death did not; panic disorder diagnoses went with parental death and separation from the mother, phobia diagnoses with parental death, and eating disorder diagnoses with neither. Treating loss as a measured family environment in a twin model, the authors estimate that, if it is truly environmental, it accounts for 1.5 to 5.1 percent of the variance in liability to these diagnoses and 7.0 to 20.5 percent of their clustering in sisters.

1691.content: In the Virginia 30,000 children-of-twins sample (4,800 adult offspring, mean age 35.5, 22.1 percent with parents who divorced or separated), offspring of divorced parents scored higher on the authors' emotional problems measure (SCL items) than unrelated offspring of intact families (odds ratio 1.45). Comparing cousins whose identical-twin parents differed in divorce, the difference disappeared (odds ratio 0.94; risks 24.5 against 24.7 percent), which the authors read as shared genetic liability, so that offspring of divorced parents would have shown more depressive symptoms even had their parents not divorced.

In the same sample, offspring of divorced parents were about twice as likely to report ever being diagnosed or treated for an alcohol problem (odds ratio 2.10 against unrelated intact families). The association held among cousins whose identical-twin parents differed in divorce (odds ratio 2.03; risks 1.4 against 4.2 percent) and after measured characteristics of both parents were added (odds ratio 1.99), which the authors read as consistent with a causal effect of divorce on offspring substance use problems.

1692.content: English and Romanian Adoptees study, a natural experiment: children who spent from soon after birth up to 43 months in Romanian institutions under the Ceausescu regime and were then adopted into mostly advantaged UK families, compared with 52 UK adoptees who were never deprived, assessed at 6, 11 and 15 years and at 22 to 25 years. Adoptees with less than 6 months in an institution (67 at age 6, 50 in young adulthood) scored as low as the UK adoptees on most outcomes at most ages. Adoptees with more than 6 months in an institution (98 at age 6, 72 in young adulthood) had persistently higher rates of parent-reported symptoms in three domains the authors name autism spectrum disorder, disinhibited social engagement (over-friendliness with strangers) and inattention and overactivity, from age 6 through young adulthood (pooled p<0.0001 for all), although their adoptive families stayed as supportive as the others. Mental health service use from age 15 to 23 was reported for 43.1% of this group against 9.5% of the UK adoptees, and 36.1% against 14.3% were unemployed as young adults.

In the same study, the share of adoptees with an IQ below 80 in the group with more than 6 months in an institution was markedly higher than in the UK adoptees at age 6 (p=0.0001) and age 11 (p=0.0016) and fell to the UK level by age 22 to 25 (p=0.76). The authors read this as evidence of long-term plasticity: a deficit set up by early deprivation that years in an adoptive family removed.

In the same study, self-rated and parent-rated emotional symptoms (depressed mood, worry, social anxiety scored on the questionnaires) did not differ by deprivation at age 6, differed little at 11 and 15, and rose in young adulthood in the group with more than 6 months in an institution, to three to four times the rate of the other groups (self-rated, p=0.0005 against UK adoptees). Fifteen people (21%) of the most deprived group met the authors' criteria for no adverse outcome at any age. The authors offer two readings of the late rise: a developmental consequence of earlier problems, or a latent stress-system sensitisation from early deprivation that shows later.

1693.content: At age 4, 111 Romanian children adopted into the UK before age 2 after severe early privation were compared with 52 UK children adopted before 6 months. At UK entry about half of the Romanian children were below the third percentile for height, weight, head circumference and developmental quotient. By age 4, catch-up in growth and cognitive level looked nearly complete for those who arrived before 6 months of age; for those placed after 6 months it was large but incomplete, with a mean McCarthy General Cognitive Index of 92 against 109 for the UK adoptees. Age at entry to the UK was the strongest predictor of cognitive level at 4.

1694.content: Bucharest Early Intervention Project, a randomised trial: 136 abandoned children in all six Bucharest institutions for young children, enrolled at 6 to 31 months, were assigned by drawing names from a hat to stay in care as usual or to go to foster care created by the project. At about age 12, 110 were followed up and caregivers were interviewed with the DISC-IV by interviewers blind to group. The foster care group had fewer reported externalising symptoms than care as usual (mean count 1.73 against 2.89, difference 1.16, 95% CI 0.11 to 2.22, p=0.0255), while counts of internalising symptoms (0.85 against 1.00, p=0.57) and ADHD symptoms (4.24 against 3.76, p=0.58) did not differ. The authors conclude that early foster care slightly reduced the risk.

In the same follow-up, the 110 children who had ever been in an institution (both trial arms) had higher reported symptom counts than 49 Bucharest children never placed in an institution: internalising 0.93 against 0.45, externalising 2.31 against 0.65, ADHD symptoms 4.00 against 0.71. Within the foster care arm, children whose placement held (26) had fewer reported internalising and externalising symptoms than children whose placement was disrupted (28); the two groups had not differed on symptoms or IQ at 54 months.

1695.content: Bucharest Early Intervention Project, intention-to-treat follow-up of the randomised trial: 220 children (58 care as usual, 61 foster care, 101 never institutionalised) rated by teachers and caregivers on the MacArthur Health and Behavior Questionnaire at 8, 12 and 16 years, with a general factor (P) and specific internalising and externalising factors. At 8 both trial arms scored higher on P than never-institutionalised children and did not differ from each other. By 16 the foster care group scored lower on P than care as usual (mean 0.07 against 0.37), after a modest decline while care as usual stayed high, but still above the never-institutionalised group.

In the same trial, externalising scores (defiance, conduct, aggression) fell from 8 to 16 in the foster care group but not in care as usual, so that at 16 the foster care group scored lower than care as usual and no differently from never-institutionalised children. Internalising scores (low mood, worry, withdrawal), once the general factor was taken out, did not differ between any of the three groups at any age.

1696.content: Abstract only. In the Bucharest Early Intervention Project, 136 children living in Bucharest institutions, enrolled at 6 to 30 months, were randomised to continued institutional care or to project foster care, and caregivers of 52 and 59 of them were given structured psychiatric interviews at 54 months, alongside 59 never-institutionalised Bucharest children. Children with any history of institutional rearing met the interview criteria for more psychiatric disorders (53.2% against 22.0%). Children randomised to foster care were less often classified with internalising disorders than those kept in care as usual (22.0% against 44.2%); boys reported as more symptomatic than girls showed no drop in total symptoms after foster placement.

1697.content: Abstract only. A representative telephone sample of 2,181 people aged 18 to 45 in the Detroit area was interviewed about lifetime traumatic events, and PTSD by DSM-IV criteria was assessed for one event drawn at random from each person's list. The risk of meeting the criteria after a randomly chosen event was 9.2%, highest after assaultive violence (20.9%). Sudden unexpected death of a loved one, reported by 60% of the sample, carried a risk of 14.3% and was the event behind 31% of all cases. The authors state that earlier studies overestimated the risk by asking about the worst event a person had experienced.

1698.content: Abstract only. In the part II subsample of the US National Comorbidity Survey (5,877 people aged 15 to 54), modified DSM-III-R PTSD interview modules gave an estimated lifetime prevalence of meeting the criteria of 7.8%, higher in women and in the previously married. Survival analysis showed that more than a third of people with an index episode as scored by the interview did not recover even after many years.

1699.content: Abstract only. A meta-analysis of 20 laboratory fear-conditioning studies (453 people diagnosed with anxiety disorders, 455 healthy controls) found modest increases in learned fear and in fear during extinction among the patients. These differences did not appear in discrimination studies, where a danger cue and a safety cue are both shown; they came mainly from single-cue designs, where only a danger cue is shown and no holding back of fear to a safety cue is needed.

1700.content: A meta-analysis of 44 fear-conditioning studies published from 1920 to 2013 (about 963 people diagnosed with anxiety disorders, 1,222 controls; about half the studies included people diagnosed with PTSD). While fear was being learned, patients responded no more than controls to the danger cue (d = 0.067, P = .41) but more to the safety cue (d = 0.296, P < .001, 26 studies). Because the safety cues in these studies look like the danger cues, the authors read this as fear spreading to safe stimuli that resemble the danger cue. During extinction, patients kept responding more to the former danger cue (d = 0.352). Whether the patients were diagnosed with PTSD or another anxiety disorder did not account for the differences between studies.

1701.content: 71 male US combat veterans of Iraq and Afghanistan (61 analysed: 20 who met PTSD criteria on the CAPS interview, 21 with subthreshold scores, 20 trauma-exposed with low scores) learned in an fMRI scanner that one ring size came with a shock and another never did, and then saw rings of in-between sizes. Veterans who met the criteria showed fear that spread further along the rings resembling the danger ring: flatter generalisation gradients in rated risk and in activity of the anterior insula, ventral hippocampus, dorsolateral and dorsomedial prefrontal cortex and caudate. CAPS scores correlated with generalisation in the right anterior insula (r=0.34) and left ventral hippocampus (r=0.36), but not with generalisation in rated risk (r=0.15, p=0.24).

1702.content: Abstract only. A meta-analysis of 58 resting-baseline studies, 25 startle studies, 17 standardised trauma-cue studies and 22 personal trauma-script studies compared adults diagnosed with PTSD and adults not so diagnosed on heart rate, skin conductance, facial muscle activity and blood pressure. With no reminder present, at rest, people diagnosed with PTSD had higher heart rate (r = .18) and skin conductance (r = .08). To sudden loud tones that are no trauma reminder, they showed larger startle blinks (r = .13), higher heart rate (r = .23) and slower habituation of skin conductance (r = .21). With trauma reminders the differences were similar or larger: heart rate r = .27 for standard trauma cues, and with personal trauma scripts r = .21 to .34 for facial muscles, .22 for heart rate and .19 for skin conductance.

Abstract only. In the same meta-analysis, the most robust physiological correlates of being diagnosed with PTSD were slow habituation of skin conductance to repeated startling tones, facial muscle activity during personal trauma scripts, and heart rate in all study types, at rest included.

1703.content: Abstract only. Children with court-substantiated abuse or neglect in 1967 to 1971 in a Midwestern US county were matched on age, race, sex and approximate family class with children without such records and followed into young adulthood; 1,196 were interviewed with the NIMH Diagnostic Interview Schedule. Of those recorded as sexually abused 37.5%, of those physically abused 32.7% and of those neglected 30.6% met DSM-III-R criteria for lifetime PTSD; recorded victimisation was associated with higher lifetime and current risk, and with more symptoms after adjustment for family, individual and lifestyle covariates. The author concludes that victimisation is not a sufficient condition for meeting the PTSD criteria.

1704.content: In the E-Risk cohort (2,232 British twins followed from birth to 18 with 93% retention; 2,055 analysed), maltreatment up to age 12 was measured twice: prospectively from caregivers, researchers and clinicians at ages 5, 7, 10 and 12, and retrospectively with the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire at 18. The two overlapped little (all kappas 0.31 or below): only 27.6% of those with a prospective record reported the maltreatment at 18, and most who reported it at 18 had no prospective record.

In the same cohort, both kinds of report were associated with interview-assessed depression, anxiety, self-injury, alcohol or cannabis dependence and conduct disorder at 18, but recalled maltreatment gave the stronger associations, above all with depression and self-injury. When the two reports were entered together, the associations of recorded maltreatment with depression and self-injury often became non-significant or much smaller, while those of recalled maltreatment stayed strong; for alcohol or cannabis dependence and conduct disorder the two did not differ much. The authors conclude that maltreated people who recalled it had more affective problems than maltreated people who had forgotten it or did not disclose it.

1705.content: Cochrane review of 12 randomised trials (1,837 adults diagnosed with PTSD, all recruited in the United States, with most trials in military veterans) of present-centred therapy, a manualised therapy that does not go back to the event and works on current daily difficulties and coping, with therapist support. Against waiting list or minimal attention (3 trials, 290 people) it reduced clinician-rated symptom scores (SMD -0.84, 95% CI -1.10 to -0.59; moderate-quality evidence). Against trauma-focused CBT straight after treatment it did not meet the authors' non-inferiority margin of 10 CAPS points (mean difference 6.83, 95% CI 1.90 to 11.76; 6 trials, 607 people; low-quality evidence), but the gap shrank to 1.59 CAPS points at 6 months (906 people) and 1.22 at 12 months (485 people), neither significant.

In the same review, 10 trials (1,542 people) reported dropout: about 14% fewer people dropped out of present-centred therapy than out of trauma-focused CBT (risk difference -0.14, 95% CI -0.18 to -0.10; moderate-quality evidence).

1706.content: Abstract only. In laboratory rats (Rattus norvegicus), cross-fostering pups between mothers that differ in maternal care gave evidence that the mother's care sets the offspring's behavioural and hormonal response to stress, and that daughters pass the care style they received to their own young, a transmission across generations without a change in genes. An environmental manipulation in early life that changed a mother's care could in turn change the pattern passed to later generations.

1707.content: Long-Evans rat (Rattus norvegicus) pups were separated from the mother for 3 hours a day on days 1 to 14 (a loss of maternal care) or handled for 15 minutes a day, then from weaning (day 22) to day 70 housed either two to a standard cage or in groups of eight in large connected cages with burrows and regularly changed toys, and tested from day 110. Separated rats in standard housing had higher corticosterone responses to restraint (8 per group) and explored less and were slower to eat in a new place. Separated rats raised in the enriched housing did not differ from handled rats on any of these: the later environment fully reversed the effect of early separation on hormonal and behavioural responses to stress.

In the same experiment on rats (Rattus norvegicus), enrichment did not change the brain differences left by early separation: separated rats had lower glucocorticoid receptor gene expression in the hippocampus and higher CRF gene expression in the hypothalamus whether they had lived in standard or enriched housing (3 to 5 rats per group). The authors conclude that the later environment compensated for the early change rather than removing it, and state that under stable living conditions the separation effects endure over the lifespan.

1708.content: Abstract only. A Swedish national register cohort born 1973 to 1982 (862,554 people) was followed for hospital admissions and outpatient care with a recorded diagnosis of depression in 2006 to 2013. After adjustment for sociodemographic confounders, death of the mother from natural causes before 18 went with a hazard ratio for outpatient care for diagnosed depression of 1.19 (95% CI 1.02 to 1.40) in men and 1.15 (1.01 to 1.31) in women, with similar figures for death of the father; the authors call this a small increased risk. Death of a parent by suicide, accident or homicide carried higher ratios, up to 3.23 for hospital admission with diagnosed depression in men after losing a mother, and loss at preschool age carried more risk than loss as a teenager.

1709.content: Abstract only. In 7,188 twins from a population-based registry (Virginia) (5,070 from same-sex and 2,118 from opposite-sex pairs), first onsets of major depression and alcohol dependence by interview criteria were related to loss of a parent before 17, by death or by separation for other reasons. The raised risk of a first onset meeting the interview criteria for major depression was not constant: after a parent's death it returned to baseline within about 12 years, after separation within about 30 years, while the raised risk of alcohol dependence after separation did not change over time; the proportional-hazards model found no significant raised risk of alcohol dependence after a parent's death.

1710.content: In 2,605 adult male twins from the Virginia population-based registry, 7.1% reported a parent's death and 15.4% a separation (79% divorce) before age 17; the twins' reports agreed perfectly. Separation was associated with every interview-assessed outcome except phobia (odds ratios 1.45 to 2.03). A parent's death was associated only with phobia and alcohol dependence as classified by the interview, each at p < 0.05, and not with major depression. In the twin model, loss accounted for about 10% of the variance of each outcome, 2 to 11% for separation and 0 to 5% for death. Age at loss and time since loss showed no association with lifetime risk.

1711.content: Abstract only. In a community in the Okavango Delta of Botswana that mixes dry farming, foraging and herding, behavioural observation and household economic data on children were analysed with multiple regression. Children whose labour was in greater demand spent significantly less time playing, and, controlling for age and gender, children spent significantly more time in play activities related to the tasks of their own household's subsistence economy. The authors read this as consistent with play building adult competence.

1712.content: Abstract only. Brewer proposes an optimal distinctiveness model: social identity reconciles two opposing needs, for assimilation into a group and for differentiation from others. People avoid self-definitions that are either too personal or too inclusive and define themselves by membership of distinctive categories; identification and group loyalty are hypothesised to be strongest for groups that give both a sense of belonging and a sense of distinctiveness. An initial laboratory experiment supported the prediction that depersonalisation and group size interact in setting the strength of social identification.

1713.content: Two male rhesus macaques (Macaca mulatta) chose between two targets before a water reward that was big or small with equal chance. One target was followed by cues that told the size of the coming reward, the other to uninformative cues; the choice did not change the reward. After a few days both monkeys strongly preferred the informative target: monkey Z chose it about 80% of the time and monkey V close to 100%. In a second task where information always came before the reward, both preferred to get it immediately over after a delay, and switched colours when the cue meanings were reversed. The authors conclude that the monkeys treated information about rewards as a reward in itself.

In the same two rhesus macaques (Macaca mulatta), 47 presumed midbrain dopamine neurons that signalled the expected amount of water were recorded. The same neurons responded more to the target that promised advance information than to the target that promised none, and this neural preference tracked the behavioural one: monkey V, with the stronger behavioural preference, had the stronger neural preference (P = 0.02), and within monkey Z the neural preference was larger in sessions where the behavioural preference was stronger (rho = 0.44, P = 0.02). Behavioural preference for information did not correlate with the neurons' discrimination of water cues or water rewards.

1714.content: In four annual census surveys of the investment banking division of one large financial organisation, 345 bankers named 12,655 colleagues with whom they had frequent and substantial business contact in the past year. Only 24.7% of those relations were named again the next year, 10.1% two years on and 8.0% three years on; across all 22,709 relations at risk, three in four were gone the following year. Decay slowed with the age of the tie: of 883 relations named in each of the first three surveys, 47.1% were named again in the fourth, and for a tie that had lasted a decade the modelled yearly hazard was near zero. Decay was also slower between colleagues with a strong prior relation, in the same division, of high status, or linked through many third parties. Relations with colleagues who left the firm all decayed.

Burt's canvass of all longitudinal decay findings in Social Networks and Sociometry found few studies. Among them: of 162 intimates named in 1968 by 33 East Yorkers (Wellman and colleagues 1997), 27% were still named as intimates a decade later, 36.6% for family and 17.5% for others; of 254 people named for socialising by 42 women returning to college at midlife (Suitor and Keeton 1997), 36.6% were named again a year later and 23.2% ten years later; of 5,345 recognition citations among 152 men in a small college, 54% were seen again at the end of the freshman year.

1715.content: Abstract only. The authors argue that treating a diagnosed mental disorder as a latent variable that causes its symptoms runs into serious problems with comorbidity, and propose instead that comorbidity arises from direct relations between symptoms of different diagnostic labels. From an empirical symptom network for major depression and generalised anxiety, they argue that some paths through the symptoms are more likely than others, that those paths mostly run in one direction (from symptoms of one label to symptoms of the other), that symptoms shared by both labels play an important role, and that the boundaries between diagnostic categories are necessarily fuzzy.

1716.content: Abstract only. A meta-analysis of 115 randomised trials comparing 178 psychotherapies for adults with depression scores against a control condition, with eight quality criteria coded by two independent coders (participants met diagnostic criteria for a depressive disorder, a treatment manual, trained therapists, a check of treatment integrity, intention-to-treat analysis, at least 50 participants, independent randomisation, blinded outcome assessors). Only 11 studies (16 comparisons) met all eight. Their standardised mean effect size was d = 0.22, significantly smaller than the d = 0.74 of the other studies (p < 0.001), also when the comparison was limited to studies with care-as-usual or non-specific controls; heterogeneity among the high-quality studies was zero. The number needed to treat was 8 in the high-quality studies and 2 in the others. The authors conclude that the effects of psychotherapy for adult depression have been overestimated and, though significant, are much smaller than assumed.

1717.content: A meta-analysis of 98 studies that measured total energy expenditure (TEE) with doubly labelled water, covering 183 cohorts and 4,972 adults; 14 studies (21 cohorts, 483 people) came from low- or middle-development countries (Bolivia, Cameroon, China, Gambia, Guatemala, India, Jamaica, Nigeria, Siberian herders in Russia, South Africa, Swaziland). People in the lower-development countries were lighter (men 66.1 against 81.3 kg; BMI 22.7 against 26.0 in men and 24.3 against 26.6 in women), and their unadjusted TEE was about 1 MJ a day lower. In meta-regression, age and weight were associated with TEE, and development status was associated with neither TEE nor physical activity level (PAL, TEE over resting expenditure): men's PAL was 1.88 against 1.79 and women's 1.70 against 1.72. Results were the same when countries were grouped by OECD membership.

From the absence of a difference in energy expenditure, the authors infer that the higher mean BMI in high-development countries reflects energy intake more than energy expenditure, and cite two analyses by Swinburn and colleagues in which rising food intake was enough to account for the rise in US body weight since the 1970s.

1718.content: Abstract only. From a synthesis of psychodynamic, existential, arousal and cognitive theories, the authors argue that boredom is universally conceived as the aversive experience of wanting, but being unable, to engage in satisfying activity. They propose to define it through attention: boredom is the aversive state that occurs when a person cannot engage attention with the inner or outer information needed for satisfying activity, is focused on that failure, and attributes the aversive state to the environment.

1719.content: Abstract only. A review of nearly 200 studies of Hackman and Oldham's job characteristics model, with a meta-analysis of a large part of the data. Corrected correlations showed that job characteristics are related to both psychological and behavioural outcomes, and the results tended to support the critical psychological states as mediators between job characteristics and personal outcomes, though the pattern of correlations between job characteristics and those states was less supportive. Most cross-study variance came from statistical artifacts; true variance remained for the link between job characteristics and performance, which growth-need strength appeared to moderate.

1720.content: Using 1980 US census microdata and state differences in when laws (the mature minor doctrine, family planning statutes, a lower age of majority) gave young unmarried women legal access to the pill, Goldin and Katz report that the share of US-born women college graduates married before age 23 fell from 47.0% for those born 1940 to 1949, to 38.3% for those born 1950 to 1954, and to 26.8% for those born 1955 to 1957. In 1971 survey data, pill use among never-married 15 to 19 year olds was about 30% greater in states with lenient laws, and 40 to 45% greater among young college women. Adopting a non-restrictive birth control law for minors was associated with a modest but statistically significant 2 percentage point fall in the probability that a woman college graduate married before 23. Women's share of first-year law students rose from 10% in 1970 to 36% in 1980.

1721.content: Abstract only. A review of contrafreeloading: animals (for example rats pressing a lever) work for earned food even when identical free food can easily be had from a nearby dish, against the expectation of most learning, motivation and foraging theories that animals maximise reward over effort. After intensive training the behaviour may be explained by secondary reinforcement or unequal exposure to the two food sources, but it also occurs without prior training. Contrafreeloading declines as hunger rises and as the effort needed for the earned food rises, and has an inverted-U relation with how much stimulus change goes with the earned food.

Abstract only. The authors build a fuzzy logic model of the factors that set contrafreeloading, which reproduces earlier findings, and propose a functional explanation (the information primacy model): in changing environments animals work for earned food to update their estimate of a food source that is currently worse, because it may unpredictably become the best place to feed. On this reading contrafreeloading is adaptive under natural conditions.

1722.content: A review of national survey data from 1990 to 2015 in four English-speaking countries found that treatment rose steeply while the share of people meeting survey criteria for mood and anxiety disorders, or reporting their symptoms, did not fall. Australia: antidepressant use rose 352% from 1990 to 2002 and a further 95% from 2000 to 2011, yet 18% met criteria for an anxiety, affective or substance use disorder on the CIDI interview in 1997 and 20% in 2007. Canada: antidepressant use rose more than three-fold in the 1990s, and across eleven national surveys the prevalence of major depressive episodes, as scored by the survey interviews, showed no change from 1994 to 2012 (slope nearly exactly zero). England: antidepressant receipt nearly trebled from 1993 to 2000, while common mental disorders scored on the survey interview stood at 10.9% of men and 18.1% of women in 1993 and 11.8% and 18.9% in 2007. US: the share of adults aged 18 to 54 in treatment rose from 12.2% (1990 to 1992) to 20.1% (2001 to 2003), and the surveys reported no evidence of a fall in prevalence and some evidence of a rise.

Weighing reasons for the lack of improvement, the authors found no support for the idea that rising risk factors masked a fall from treatment (no national disaster, economic shock or decline in physical health that could plausibly push prevalence up in Australia, Canada or England; in the US, major stressors such as recession and hurricanes had no clear long-term effect found and physical health did not decline), little evidence on the idea that more people now report symptoms, and more support for the idea that much treatment falls short of guidelines and is poorly targeted. In Australia an estimated 39% of people meeting criteria for mood or anxiety disorders sought professional help, 26% received an evidence-based intervention and 16% minimally adequate treatment, and only 50% of people prescribed antidepressants took them for the recommended six months.

1723.content: Abstract only. A review built on 38 meta-analyses and 24 systematic reviews of shift work. The effect of shift work on sleep mainly concerns acute sleep loss around night shifts and early-morning shifts. Shift work is linked with accidents, type 2 diabetes (relative risk range 1.09 to 1.40), weight gain, coronary heart disease (relative risk 1.23), stroke (relative risk 1.05) and cancer (relative risk range 1.01 to 1.32), although the original studies showed mixed results. These links mirror those of insufficient sleep, and laboratory studies show that both shift work and sleep loss raise cardiometabolic stress and cognitive impairment. The authors say more research is needed on whether insufficient sleep is the path from shift work to the health effects.

1724.content: A review of interdisciplinary research on algorithms in organisations, framed by labour process theory. The authors find that employers use algorithms to direct workers by restricting and recommending, to evaluate them by recording and rating, and to discipline them by replacing and rewarding, and that algorithmic systems are more comprehensive, instantaneous, interactive and opaque than earlier workplace technology. Cases in the reviewed studies include a warehouse where a handheld scanner scored each worker's fine-grained behaviour in real time and alerted a manager when the score stayed low, trucking fleet systems recording speed, idling, braking and location, and ride-hail platforms where drivers with a low passenger rating and acceptance rate faced immediate deactivation. Workers resist individually and collectively through tactics the authors call algoactivism.

1725.content: In UK general practice records (GPRD, 170 practices that gave data throughout, 1993 to 2005), the authors report that antidepressant prescribing nearly doubled: the average number of prescriptions per patient rose from 2.8 in 1993 to 5.6 in 2004. The authors report that this rise did not come from more new cases diagnosed with depression, a lower threshold for treatment, a larger share of new cases given a drug, or longer first prescriptions; it came mainly from more patients on long-term medication. Chronic and intermittent prescribing together made up about 90 percent of all prescriptions, and the chronic group received on average 35 prescriptions per patient over five years.

Among 189,851 people in the GPRD diagnosed by their GP with a first episode of depression between 1993 and 2005, 79.4 percent received an antidepressant prescription in the first year after diagnosis, and this proportion stayed stable across all years. New cases diagnosed by GPs fell overall (men 7.83 to 5.97 and women 15.83 to 10.06 per 1000 patient years from 1993 to 2005), but rose among women aged 18 to 30 (23.8 per 1000 patient years in 1993 to a peak of 37.7 in 2001, then 26.4 in 2005).

1726.content: Mottron and colleagues propose an Enhanced Perceptual Functioning model of autism that gathers the main differences between autistic and non-autistic perception: locally oriented seeing and hearing, enhanced low-level discrimination, enhanced perception of simple static stimuli, diminished perception of complex movement, low-level processing that runs more independently of higher-order operations, and a different relation between perception and general intelligence. They suggest that increased perceptual expertise may lie behind the special abilities of savant autistic people and behind the spread of presentations within the authors' category of pervasive developmental disorders.

1727.content: A meta-analysis comparing people diagnosed with autism spectrum disorders and neurotypical people on four visuo-spatial tasks found that the autistic samples performed better on Block Design (d = 0.32) and on Figure Disembedding, finding a shape hidden in a larger figure (d = 0.26), with large heterogeneity the authors could not account for. No clear difference was found for Mental Rotation. On Navon tasks the samples diagnosed with autism showed a stronger preference for local detail (d = 0.35), with less clear evidence of performance differences.

1728.content: A systematic review searched 10 databases, screened 3892 citations and kept 38 qualitative studies (rated moderate to high quality) on how being diagnosed with a psychiatric condition in childhood or adolescence interacts with young people's self-concept and social identity. In the thematic synthesis, being diagnosed could threaten and devalue the young person's view of themselves, and could also help self-understanding, self-legitimation and self-enhancement. Socially, the authors report that a diagnosis could bring alienation, invalidation and stigma, and could also bring identification with others and acceptance.

1729.content: A review of empirical studies on how people use automated and decision-support systems concludes that automation complacency (failing to catch automation failures) arises when manual tasks compete with the automated task for attention, is found in both naive and expert participants and is not overcome by simple practice. Automation bias produces both omission errors (missing a problem the aid did not flag) and commission errors (following the aid's wrong advice) when aids are imperfect; it occurs in naive and expert participants, is not prevented by training or instructions, and affects decisions of individuals and of teams.

The review reports that in Mosier and colleagues' 1992 simulator study, when an automated electronic checklist recommended shutting down the wrong engine during a simulated engine fire, 75 percent of pilots followed the wrong recommendation without checking other indicators, against 25 percent of pilots using a paper checklist. In Mosier and colleagues' 1998 study with experienced commercial pilots, all pilots shut down an engine in response to a false fire alert from the automated system, and 67 percent reported afterwards having seen a further indication supporting the alert that was in fact absent.

The review reports a 1993 laboratory study by Parasuraman, Molloy and Singh in which participants monitored automated engine-failure detection while doing other flight tasks: they detected on average 33 percent of automation failures when the automation had been constantly reliable, against 82 percent when its reliability varied. When participants had only to watch the automation with no other task, detection was near perfect.

1730.content: In a Danish population-based register cohort of 1.89 million people, with years lived in each of five levels of urbanization during upbringing, the risk of being diagnosed with schizophrenia, as recorded in the Danish Psychiatric Central Register, rose with the number of years lived in more urban places. People who lived their first 15 years in the most urban category had 2.75 times the risk (95% CI 2.31 to 3.28). People who had moved to a more urban level than 5 years earlier had 1.40 times the risk (1.28 to 1.51), and those who had moved to a less urban level 0.82 times (0.77 to 0.88). Holding urbanicity at the 15th birthday fixed, risk also rose with urbanicity at birth. The authors conclude that continuous or repeated exposures during upbringing that are more frequent in urban areas may explain the association.

1731.content: In an online questionnaire completed by 1,829 New Zealand adults who had been prescribed antidepressants in the previous five years (52 percent reported taking them for more than three years), eight of the 20 adverse effects asked about were reported by more than half. The most frequent were sexual difficulties (62 percent) and feeling emotionally numb (60 percent); 52 percent reported feeling not like themselves, 42 percent a reduction in positive feelings, 39 percent caring less about others, 39 percent suicidality and 55 percent withdrawal effects.
