Total adverse effect scores were related to younger age, lower education and income and type of antidepressant, and not to the level of depression the respondents reported before taking them.

1732.content: Using genome-wide association summary statistics, the genetic correlation between being diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder and parent-rated social and communication difficulties (Social and Communication Disorders Checklist) in 5,628 eight-year-olds of the UK general population cohort ALSPAC was 0.27 for the PGC-ASD sample (5,305 cases, diagnosed mainly in the United States) and 0.30 for the independent Danish iPSYCH sample (7,783 cases, 11,359 controls). The authors read this as substantial, replicated overlap between the genetics of the diagnosis and typical variation in social and communication ability, at least as strong as the overlap between the autism diagnosis and the schizophrenia, bipolar or major depression diagnoses.

In the Simons Simplex Collection (2,497 children diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder and 1,861 unaffected siblings), the rate of damaging new (de novo) mutations rose linearly with lower adaptive functioning on the parent-rated Vineland scales in both the diagnosed children and their siblings. Diagnosed and undiagnosed children with the same Vineland score carried a highly similar de novo burden, and once Vineland score was controlled for, the link between de novo burden and diagnosis fell from p = 7.6e-15 to p = 0.05. The authors conclude that the categorical clinical threshold is largely arbitrary with regard to these social and communication impairments.

1733.content: In a two-page statement in the South African Medical Journal, three University of Cape Town clinicians (the authors) state that adrenal fatigue, promoted mainly in non-medical online publications as adrenal glands drained by repeated stress, has no confirmed diagnostic tests or special investigations and no ICD-10 code as a recognised clinical disorder. Citing the US Endocrine Society's warning and a systematic review, they conclude that until there is objective, reproducible clinical evidence, adrenal fatigue does not exist, and that patients should be investigated and managed for their symptoms, with true adrenal failure (Addison's disease) excluded.

The statement reports that of several thousand PubMed articles on adrenal fatigue, only 13 examined the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis; that the standard synthetic ACTH stimulation test, when used, showed a greater cortisol rise in people presumed to have fatigue than in healthy controls; that in one study two-thirds of participants showed no difference in salivary cortisol between fatigued people and controls; and that late-night cortisol, whole-day salivary cortisol and DHEAS gave inconsistent results. Supplements sold to support the adrenals (ashwagandha, rhodiola, liquorice root, ginseng, schizandra, maca) cost about ZAR 1,200 a month in South Africa with no objective benefit shown.

1734.content: Using a version of the Rejection Sensitivity Questionnaire adapted for clinical and non-clinical samples, the authors found that patients diagnosed with borderline personality disorder scored highest on rejection sensitivity (anxious expectation, ready perception and overreaction to rejection cues) and on borderline-specific thoughts, and differed significantly from every other group: several groups of patients with other diagnoses, including social anxiety disorder, and healthy controls. Rejection sensitivity scores correlated highly with the borderline-specific thoughts questionnaire.

1735.content: In individual participant data from 232 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of antidepressant monotherapy for major depressive disorder submitted to the US FDA between 1979 and 2016 (73,388 adult and child participants), scores converted to the 17-item Hamilton scale (HAMD17) improved by 9.8 points on drug and 8.0 on placebo: a mean difference of 1.75 points (95% CI 1.63 to 1.86), standardised mean difference about 0.23. The drug-placebo difference grew with greater baseline severity, and after controlling for baseline characteristics there was no trend in drug effect or placebo response over time.

A mixture model of individual responses fitted three groups: Large improvement (mean 16.0 points), Non-specific (8.9 points) and Minimal (1.7 points). Participants on a drug were more likely to have a Large response (24.5 percent against 9.6 percent on placebo; number needed to treat 6.7) and less likely to have a Minimal response (12.2 against 21.5 percent); most responses on drug (63.3 percent) and on placebo (68.9 percent) were Non-specific. The authors conclude that about 15 percent of participants have a substantial antidepressant effect beyond the placebo effect in trials.

1736.content: A Cochrane systematic review included 185 randomised trials (38 parallel-group trials with 5,111 participants and 147 cross-over trials with 7,134) comparing methylphenidate with placebo or no intervention in children and adolescents diagnosed with ADHD (average age 9.7, boys to girls 5 to 1, mostly high-income countries). Treatment lasted on average 75 days (1 to 425). All 185 trials were judged at high risk of bias. Methylphenidate may improve teacher-rated ADHD symptoms (SMD -0.77, 19 trials, 1,698 participants; about 9.6 points on the 72-point ADHD Rating Scale, where 6.6 points is the minimal relevant difference), teacher-rated general behaviour and parent-rated quality of life, with every one of these outcomes graded very low quality evidence. The authors say they cannot be certain of the size of the effects.

In the same review, 526 per 1000 children on methylphenidate had non-serious adverse events against 408 per 1000 in control groups (RR 1.29, 95% CI 1.10 to 1.51; 21 trials, 3,132 participants; very low quality). Children on methylphenidate had a 60 percent greater risk of sleep problems (RR 1.60; 13 trials) and a 266 percent greater risk of decreased appetite (RR 3.66; 16 trials). No increase in serious adverse events was found (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.44 to 2.22; 9 trials), within the short follow-up of the trials.

1737.content: In the MTA follow-up into early adulthood (about age 25, 16 years after children aged 7 to 9.9 were diagnosed with combined-type ADHD and enrolled), the authors grouped the diagnosed participants by their own pattern of stimulant use through childhood and adolescence: Consistent (n = 35), Inconsistent (n = 329) and Negligible (n = 112). On adult symptom severity (Conners Adult ADHD Rating Scale, parent and self ratings averaged), the comparisons between these medication subgroups were not significant. The diagnosed group as a whole still scored higher than local comparison classmates (d = 1.11).

In the same follow-up, with height measured by stadiometer at about age 25 and adjusted for sex and parents' height, participants with the Consistent or Inconsistent stimulant pattern were 2.55 cm shorter than those with the Negligible pattern (d = 0.42), and the Consistent subgroup was a further 2.36 cm shorter than the Inconsistent subgroup (d = 0.38); the gap between the extreme subgroups was 4.7 cm. The Negligible subgroup was taller than the population average (z = 0.43). Weight did not differ by medication pattern.

1738.content: Comparing FDA reviews of 74 registered trials of 12 antidepressants (12,564 patients) with the journal literature, the authors found that 31 percent of the trials, with 3,449 participants, were not published, and whether and how a trial was published was associated with its result. Of the trials the FDA viewed as positive, 37 were published and 1 was not. Of those the FDA viewed as negative or questionable, 22 were not published and 11 were published in a way that, in the authors' opinion, conveyed a positive outcome; only 3 were published as negative. In the journals 94 percent of trials appeared positive, against 51 percent in the FDA analysis, and the published effect size was larger by 11 to 69 percent per drug and by 32 percent overall.

1739.content: A review of 31 behavioural studies on creativity and ADHD found that most studies report more divergent thinking (producing many, varied and original ideas) in people with high ADHD symptom scores below the diagnostic threshold, and not in people diagnosed with ADHD. Among adults, five case-control studies compared formally diagnosed adults with controls: three found higher divergent thinking in the diagnosed group, all three by White and Shah (2006, 2011, 2016), and two did not (Barkley 1996, Boot 2017). The review found no evidence of better convergent thinking (finding the one right answer) in people diagnosed with ADHD or scoring high on its scales.

The same review reports that rates of creative abilities and achievements were high among both diagnosed (clinical) and high-scoring (subclinical) ADHD groups, and that across twelve studies of psychostimulant medication the drugs did not, overall, lower creativity scores.

1740.content: Two clinicians (a psychiatrist and a psychiatry resident) independently rated the 100 most popular TikTok videos about ADHD (on average over 2.8 million views each): 52 percent were classified as misleading, 27 percent as personal experience and 21 percent as useful (agreement 86 percent, kappa 0.78). Non-healthcare creators uploaded 49 of the 52 misleading videos; healthcare providers' videos were more often useful (63.6 against 15.7 percent), though 3 of their 11 were rated misleading. Personal experience videos drew the most views, likes and shares.

Of the 52 videos rated misleading, 37 (71 percent) presented symptoms found across many psychiatric diagnoses, including anxiety, low mood, anger, relationship conflict, dissociation and mood swings, as specific to ADHD, and none of the misleading videos advised viewers to seek an assessment before attributing these experiences to ADHD. Eight (15 percent) misrepresented the biology of the ADHD label, for example as a purely dopamine-deficient state, the authors report.

1741.content: A systematic review of studies published 2000 to 2013 included 214 publications from 199 investigations of 151,651 women in the first year after giving birth. Among psychosocial factors, the authors report that the strongest predictors of postpartum depression, as scored on questionnaires or diagnosed by interview, are severe life events, some forms of chronic strain, relationship quality, and support from the partner and from the woman's own mother. Among biological factors, the strongest are HPA-axis dysregulation, inflammatory processes and genetic vulnerabilities, each from small and often inconsistent literatures. The two literatures are largely separate and few studies integrate them.

On relationships, the review concludes that the quality of a woman's relationships around birth is associated with her risk of postpartum depression as scored or diagnosed in the studies: social support satisfaction, partner support and postpartum relationship satisfaction were protective, and high support need, anxious or ambivalent attachment, partner or family violence and substance abuse in the family went with greater vulnerability. A woman's partner and her own mother were the most critical relationships; evidence for friends and other family was mixed. Structural measures such as marital or partner status and network size showed little association beyond relationship quality.

Reviewing reproductive hormones, the authors conclude that the empirical evidence does not support a role for the fall in estrogen or progesterone after birth in the development of postpartum depressive symptoms; postpartum estrogen or progesterone levels were either unrelated to symptoms or related in the unexpected direction, with one exception for estriol. A small but fairly consistent literature links lower perinatal oxytocin to more symptoms. Studies of cortisol fairly consistently report null findings.

1742.content: In a 21-day ecological momentary assessment study of 31 US college-age tobacco users (mean age 21, from seven Georgia colleges), rating boredom, anxiety, happiness and cravings each on a ten-point scale in four four-hour windows a day, higher boredom was associated with using any tobacco product (OR 1.09 per point, 95% CI 1.01 to 1.18). Higher boredom was associated with cigarette smoking among women (OR 1.29) but not men, and with e-cigarette use among men (OR 1.16) but not women. Higher reported anxiety was associated with cigarette use; reported happiness showed no association.

1743.content: In a 7-day electronic diary study of 17 US adult smokers diagnosed with ADHD (870 smoking and 622 non-smoking entries), comparing moments just before a cigarette with non-smoking moments, participants were more likely to smoke when urge, negative affect, boredom (p = .004), stress, worry and restlessness were higher, and while drinking a caffeinated beverage (p < .0001) or alcohol. ADHD symptoms as scored in the diary were not raised before smoking. After smoking, urge, negative affect, stress, hunger and ADHD symptom scores fell, while boredom did not change significantly (1.69 before against 1.64 after, p = .144).

1744.content: Nowak, Tarnita and Wilson argue, from mathematical models, that inclusive fitness theory holds only under stringent assumptions (additive pairwise interactions, weak selection, special population structures) that they say are unlikely to hold in any real system, that where it does hold it gives the same answer as standard natural selection theory, and that it has no predictions of its own. They propose that close relatedness in eusocial colonies is better read as an outcome of eusociality than as what brought it about.

1745.content: In a reply signed by 137 authors, Abbot and colleagues answer Nowak et al. (2010): inclusive fitness theory rests on population genetics, needs none of the assumptions Nowak et al. name (pairwise interactions, weak selection, additivity), and is as general as natural selection itself, splitting selection into direct effects on the actor and indirect effects through relatives. They state that natural selection leads organisms to become adapted as if to maximise their inclusive fitness.

The reply reports that inclusive fitness theory has explained up to 96 percent of the variance in sex ratios in studies across species and 66 percent within species, against an average of 5.4 percent of variance explained in evolutionary and ecological studies, and that it explains why eusociality evolved only in monogamous lineages.

1746.content: In a large urban community sample (1,300 adults, two waves of data), the authors report that women felt they mattered to others substantially more than men did. Feeling one mattered went with lower depressive symptom scores among women, both at the same time and over time, and did not predict symptom scores among men; among men, mattering overlapped more with measures of social support.

1747.content: The authors set up 14 curated Tinder profiles (age set to 24) in London and New York, had software like every profile within 100 miles, and logged matches; they collected 230,000 male and 250,000 female profiles. Male test profiles matched with 0.6 percent of the users they liked, female test profiles with 10.5 percent. Even so, 86 percent of the matches that male profiles received came from other men. Female profiles passed 200 matches in the first hour; male profiles gained matches slowly. Overall the profiles drew 8,248 matches from men and 532 from women; 21 percent of matched women and 7 percent of matched men then sent a message.

In a survey of 131 heterosexual Tinder users (90 men, 41 women), 33 percent of men said they regularly liked most profiles they saw and no woman did; 93 percent of women said they liked only profiles they were attracted to. 59 percent of men estimated that 10 percent or fewer of their likes became matches, while 63 percent of women estimated that more than half of theirs did. 73 percent of respondents estimated that 10 percent or fewer of their matches ended in a meeting in person.

1748.content: Abstract only. In three lab studies with staged help from a confederate, people made to feel grateful put more effort into helping their benefactor, even when the help was unpleasant, and this differed from the effect of a general good mood; mediation analyses pointed to gratitude, rather than awareness of a norm to repay, as what moved the helping. Study 2 found that gratitude also raised help given to a stranger, and Study 3 that this spill-over vanished when people were made aware of what had caused the feeling.

1749.content: In a preregistered repeat of Bartlett and DeSteno's (2006) Study 1 with 152 Tilburg University psychology students (79 helped by a confederate, 73 controls), being helped raised reported gratitude and indebtedness but did not significantly raise the time people later spent helping the confederate (7.35 against 6.47 minutes), and neither gratitude nor indebtedness mediated helping. 90 percent of controls offered help without having been helped. The authors note that only four of the 91 studies in the Ma et al. (2017) meta-analysis measured direct paying back in time and effort.

1750.content: Abstract only. A meta-analysis of 252 effect sizes from 91 studies in 65 papers (18,342 participants) found a moderate positive correlation between gratitude and prosocial behaviour, r 0.374. The link was larger for paying back than for giving in general, and larger for direct paying back to the helper than for passing help on; larger for gratitude as a passing state than as a trait; larger for gratitude felt in response to someone's kindness than for general appreciation of life; and larger when gratitude was produced live (for example in economic games) than when people recalled a time they felt grateful.

1751.content: Abstract only. Reviewing several sets of research findings, the authors conclude that guilt arises from transactions between people (wrongs done and unfair gains), varies with the relationship, and is strongest, most common and most consistent in communal relationships built on mutual concern. They argue that guilt serves the relationship: it moves people to treat partners well and avoid wrongs, evens out inequities, lets less powerful partners get their way, and spreads emotional distress between the partners.

1752.content: In a double-blind, placebo-controlled within-subject study lasting about 49 days, five healthy adults each took caffeine (2.9 mg per kg, the amount in a double espresso) or placebo three hours before their usual bedtime, followed by three hours of dim (about 1.9 lux) or bright (about 3,000 lux) light, under constant laboratory conditions. Caffeine in dim light delayed the evening rise of melatonin by about 40 minutes more than placebo (Cohen's d 0.93), close to half the roughly 85 minute delay from bright light alone; bright light plus caffeine delayed it by about 105 minutes. Four of the five participants showed a delay with caffeine.

In human bone-cancer cells (U2OS) carrying clock-gene light reporters, constant exposure to caffeine lengthened the period of the cellular circadian clock in a dose-dependent way. Blocking experiments indicated that the effect ran through adenosine receptor signalling and cyclic AMP, and not through ryanodine receptors or phosphodiesterase.

1753.content: Two experiments tested Carver and Scheier's (1990) account that progress faster than needed makes people ease off a goal (coasting) and turn to other goals (shifting). In a word-recognition task with a bonus for a set number of accurate and of fast answers, people got randomly assigned feedback halfway. In experiment 1 (173 online workers), feedback of being ahead on accuracy was followed by more errors, and on speed by slower answers, with effort moving to the other goal; being ahead also raised mood. In experiment 2 (223 university students), being ahead on accuracy was again followed by more errors and faster answers, and the effect disappeared in people given a plan to ignore their feelings, which points to the feeling of progress as what eased the effort.

1754.content: In a two-sample Mendelian randomisation study among adults of European ancestry (genetic summary data on 611,583 people: accelerometer-measured activity in 91,084 and self-reported activity in 377,234 UK Biobank participants, and major depressive disorder diagnoses in 143,265 Psychiatric Genomics Consortium participants), genetically predicted higher accelerometer-measured activity went with lower odds of a major depressive disorder diagnosis (odds ratio 0.74 per standard deviation of mean acceleration, 95% CI 0.59 to 0.92). Genetic liability to that diagnosis did not predict measured activity, and self-reported activity showed no significant link in either direction.

1755.content: Opening paragraph only. Coppen proposes that biochemical changes are the most important cause of what he labels affective disorders (depression and mania), while granting that the weight of evidence is by no means conclusive and that some psychiatrists of the time denied biochemistry any causal place. On his account, a biochemical cause implies changes in the brain that must be restored to normal before the patient improves; psychological and environmental events may set off and maintain those biochemical events, but he proposes to postpone study of how environment and biochemistry interact until the biochemistry is clearer.

1757.content: Abstract only. Group size rises with relative neocortex volume across non-human primates, and Dunbar reports that this regression predicts a group size for modern humans very similar to that of hunter-gatherer and traditional horticulturalist societies, with similar group sizes in other contemporary and historical societies. In Old World monkeys and apes, grooming time rises in a straight line with group size; holding human-sized groups together by grooming alone would take an intolerable share of the day, so he proposes that language evolved as a more efficient way to bond large groups.

Abstract only. Dunbar reports that the sizes of human conversation groups and other small interacting groups fit the predicted efficiency of talk compared with grooming as a way of bonding, and that about 60 percent of conversation time is spent on relationships and personal experiences. He proposes that language let people learn how others in the group behave faster than they could by watching them directly.

1758.content: Abstract only. In a review of the built environment and mental health, Evans concludes that high-rise housing is harmful to the psychological well-being of women with young children; that poor-quality housing appears to raise psychological distress, though methodological problems prevent clear conclusions; that household crowding (people per room) and loud outside noise such as airports raise psychological distress without producing serious mental illness, in the review's words; and that too little daylight is reliably associated with more reported depressive symptoms. He adds that the built environment acts indirectly through personal control, supportive relationships and recovery from stress, and that poor conditions concentrate among the poor and ethnic minorities.

1759.content: Abstract only. Using US survey data on happiness and state changes in cigarette excise taxes, and comparing people with a high predicted propensity to smoke against others (to remove other differences between states and years), the authors find consistent evidence that higher cigarette taxes went with more reported happiness among likely smokers. Canadian survey data with independent well-being questions and larger tax changes show the same pattern, and the pattern appears for cigarette taxes and not for other excise taxes. The authors conclude that the welfare effects of cigarette taxes are more complex than simple rational economic models predict.

1760.content: Abstract only. Across 40 European countries and regions from 1990 to 2011, using the staggered introduction of smoking bans and estimating each person's propensity to smoke, the authors find that higher cigarette prices lowered the life satisfaction of likely smokers.

Abstract only. In the same 40-country data, smoking bans were barely related to life satisfaction overall but raised the life satisfaction of smokers who said they would like to quit. The authors read this as consistent with cue-triggered models of addiction and with bans working as self-control devices.

1761.content: In a preregistered audit of Twitter in February 2023, 806 US users had the first 10 tweets of their engagement-ranked timeline compared with the 10 latest tweets from accounts they follow (the chronological timeline). Readers reported that the engagement-ranked tweets were more partisan (0.24 SD), more hostile to their political out-group (0.24 SD) and expressed more anger (0.47 SD), sadness and anxiety; among political tweets, anger was the emotion amplified most (0.75 SD). After reading the engagement-ranked tweets, readers reported feeling worse about their political out-group (-0.17 SD) and feeling more anger (0.27 SD), sadness, anxiety and happiness.

The same 806 users were asked of each tweet whether they wanted to see tweets like it. Overall they rated the engagement-ranked tweets slightly higher than the chronological ones (0.06 SD), but they rated the political tweets chosen by the engagement ranking lower than the political tweets in their chronological timeline (-0.18 SD). The authors note that Twitter's internal tests found the engagement ranking increases time spent on the platform, and read the gap as the algorithm serving what users engage with and not what they say they want, most of all for political content.

1762.content: In three studies of single heterosexual adults aged 18 to 30 (315 and 305 Amazon Mechanical Turk workers rating pictures of hypothetical, slightly above-average-looking partners; 158 Dutch students rating pictures of real, available fellow participants), pictures were shown one by one in random order in a Tinder-like task. The chance of accepting a partner fell with each further picture, by on average 27% from the first to the last option, and the fall went together with falling satisfaction with the pictures and a falling sense of one's own dating success. Among the Dutch women, the chance of a real match also fell over the task (by about 70%); among men this fall was not significant.

1763.content: In the How Couples Meet and Stay Together survey (2009; a nationally representative US panel of 4,002 adults, 3,009 with a spouse or partner), almost no heterosexual couples who met in 1990 or before had met online; the share rose steeply from 1995 to 2005 and reached about 22% for couples who met in 2007 to 2009, making the internet the third most common way of meeting after friends and about level with bars and restaurants. For same-sex couples the share was above 60% in 2008 and 2009. Meeting through family fell from 25% of heterosexual couples who met in 1940 to under 10% of those who met in 2007 to 2009, and 74% of couples who met online had been perfect strangers with no previous social tie.

1764.content: Among 8,400 young adults aged 24 to 32 in the US Add Health cohort (Wave IV, 2007 to 2008), those reporting high household debt relative to their assets reported higher perceived stress, scored higher on a 5-item CES-D depressive symptom scale and reported worse general health, with adjustment for socioeconomic status, health and depressive symptom scores measured years earlier in adolescence and early adulthood. Those who said they would still be in debt after selling all they own had higher measured diastolic blood pressure (about 1.3% above the mean in the fully adjusted model); the debt-to-asset ratio calculated from reported amounts was not related to blood pressure.

1765.content: Across about 126,000 news stories tweeted by about 3 million people more than 4.5 million times on Twitter from 2006 to 2017, stories that six independent fact-checking organizations rated false spread farther, faster, deeper and more broadly than stories rated true, in all categories and most of all for political news. False stories were more novel than true ones and drew replies expressing fear, disgust and surprise; automated accounts spread true and false news at the same rate, so the authors conclude that humans, not bots, spread false news more.

1766.content: Smartphone accelerometer step counts from 717,527 users of one iPhone activity-tracking app in 111 countries (68 million days, July 2013 to December 2014) averaged 4,961 steps a day (SD 2,684) over an average recorded span of 14 hours a day. Across the 46 countries with at least 1,000 users, the spread of activity within a country (a Gini coefficient of steps) tracked the share of obese people (from reported height and weight) more closely than average steps did (r 0.79), lower activity among women accounted for 43% of that spread, and more walkable US cities (69 cities) had more steps across all age, sex and weight groups and a smaller gap between women and men.

1767.content: In a short theoretical review, Anselme notes that across many animal species, an animal given a choice between a certain and an uncertain reward tends to prefer the uncertain option even when its net gain is lower, and responds more strongly to reward-related cues when rewards are uncertain, which runs against basic reinforcement principles and optimal foraging theory. He argues that unpredictability and deprivation, whether physiological or psychological, both raise the motivation to seek valuable things, as a way of compensating for an organism's difficulty in predicting important events.

1768.content: Reviewing the experiments that compared a bright screen with a dim screen, a filtered screen or a printed book before sleep (lab and home studies; teenagers, adults, athletes and people with insomnia), Bauducco and colleagues report that the bright screen lengthened the time to fall asleep by only minutes, at most 9.9 minutes (after five evenings of e-reader use) and in several studies not at all, while melatonin suppression was consistent across studies. They read this as an uncoupling of pre-sleep melatonin from the time taken to fall asleep, and note that daylight exposure earlier in the day lessens the effect of evening light.

In studies that let adolescents play a novel videogame without a set bedtime, self-chosen bedtimes on a school night were up to 1 hour 15 minutes later, and some kept playing past midnight even when told they would be woken at 7:00. Bauducco and colleagues contrast this with bright-light and arousal effects on sleep onset of at most 9.9 and 8.5 minutes, and conclude that time taken from sleep by device use (displacement) and night-time interruptions by phones can each cut sleep opportunity by an hour or more. They also propose a reverse path, in which sleep problems come first and devices are used to fill time or regulate emotion before sleep.

1769.content: Ethnic Fijian schoolgirls in Nadroga, Fiji were surveyed in two separate samples: 63 girls in 1995, within a month of television arriving in the area, and 65 girls in 1998, after three years of it. The share scoring above 20 on a modified 26-item Eating Attitudes Test (EAT-26, a self-report scale) rose from 12.7% to 29.2%, and the share reporting self-induced vomiting to control weight rose from 0% to 11.3%; reported binge eating did not change (7.9% and 4.6%). In 1998, 69% reported having dieted to lose weight, which the authors' earlier fieldwork had found rare in traditional Fijian culture, 74% reported feeling too big or fat at least some of the time, and 77% of those interviewed said television had influenced their own body image.

1770.content: Active Facebook users were surveyed about how many people saw their posts (589 about one specific recent post, 542 about their audience in general) and their answers were compared with Facebook's logs of who actually viewed the posts. For a specific post the median guess was 20 friends against a median actual audience of 78, so the median estimate was 27% of the true audience, an underestimate by a factor of about four; for the general monthly audience the underestimate was about threefold. In logs of about 220,000 users' posts over one month, friend count, likes and comments varied widely and gave little indication of how many people saw a post, and users typically reached 61% of their friends each month.

1771.content: Study 1 compared 22 major lottery winners with 22 controls and with 29 people paralysed in accidents who had been interviewed earlier. The lottery winners were not happier than the controls and took significantly less pleasure from a series of everyday events. Study 2 found that this was not explained by prior differences between people who do and do not buy lottery tickets, or by interviews that did or did not make the lottery salient. The accident victims also showed a contrast effect, by idealizing their past, which did not help their present happiness.

1772.content: In an online survey of 328 college students in romantic relationships, attachment style was related both to relational uncertainty and to electronic surveillance of the partner on Facebook, with students classed as preoccupied or fearful reporting the highest levels of both. Relational uncertainty itself was not related to how much they monitored their partner on Facebook.

1773.content: Among 34,192 California Seventh-day Adventists (75% of those eligible) followed from 1976 to 1988 with mortality traced through state death records and the National Death Index, life expectancy at age 30 was 7.28 years higher in men (95% CI 6.59 to 7.97) and 4.42 years higher in women (3.96 to 4.88) than in other white Californians, perhaps the highest of any formally described population. Within the cohort, common combinations of diet, exercise, body mass index, past smoking and hormone replacement therapy (in women) were associated with differences of up to 10 years of life expectancy; each factor alone, from high-risk to low-risk, was associated with 1.06 to 2.74 years.

1774.content: Twitter has kept a randomly chosen control group on a reverse-chronological home timeline since it introduced personalized ranking in 2016 (by June 2020, 58 million accounts were in the experiment, 20% of them in control). Comparing reach in the two groups, tweets by elected legislators in seven countries reached a larger audience on the ranked timeline for every party, in some cases more than three times the audience on chronological timelines. In six of the seven countries the mainstream right was amplified more than the mainstream left, and among 6.2 million US news articles right-leaning sources were amplified more; far-left and far-right parties were generally amplified less than moderate ones.

1775.content: In two speed-dating studies, romantically unattached participants rated themselves on more than 100 measures of traits and preferences that earlier research tied to mate selection, then had a 4-minute speed date with each opposite-sex participant at their event. Random forest models using these measures accounted for 4% to 18% of how much a person desired others in general (actor variance) and 7% to 27% of how much a person was desired by others (partner variance), but could not account for desire for a specific partner beyond these (relationship variance) with any combination of traits and preferences reported before the dates.

1776.content: Thirty-seven young adults aged 21 to 29 (mostly in the London area, also France and Germany) wore first-person video cameras for at least three days, giving 200 hours of footage and 1,130 smartphone interactions (34 participants in the numerical analysis). Interactions lasted 64 seconds on average, but half lasted 23 seconds or less, and the median gap between them was 137 seconds (mean 290 seconds), about one minute of use every five minutes; one interaction in six was a lock-screen check of about 5 seconds. Only 11% of interactions began with a notification the user perceived, and only 15.6% of the brief lock-screen checks did; in interviews, participants described picking up the phone as automatic and habitual.

1777.content: Among the Meriam of Mer island (Torres Strait, Australia), 32 men and women were each asked to name three 'best turtle hunters'. Three men, the ones the authors had observed most often leading hunts, received 38 of the 96 nominations (39.6%), out of a pool of 90 or more males aged 16 and older. Feast-goers could name the hunt leader who provided the turtle years after a feast, but lumped the other crew members together as 'the boys'.

Meriam turtle hunts in the hunting season (April to October) were all made to supply a previously arranged public feast, attended on average by 174.9 people (range 49 to 343, 54 feasts). Hunters kept no share of the turtle and paid for the fuel, so their own return was negative (-1,086 kcal per hour); the authors report that a hunter who failed to bring turtle lost standing, since every feast-goer would notice. In the nesting season, hunted turtles kept for households were shared to more households (7.5 on average) than collected turtles (4.6).

1778.content: In a laboratory experiment with first-year economics students at Tilburg University and the University of Amsterdam (30 pairs per treatment), dictators who were told the family name of the recipient gave about 50 percent more than dictators who were not. In the name treatment 43 percent (13 of 30) gave at least half the pie against 20 percent (6 of 30) without names, and 27 percent gave nothing against 43 percent. In the ultimatum game the recipient's name made no significant difference to offers.

1779.content: Reviewing historical accounts and archaeology of mobile foragers (mainly North America, Australia and Pleistocene Europe), Boyd and Richerson report that foragers hunted communally in groups of hundreds: caribou hunts in which Inuit and Athabaskan speakers herded animals into lakes or corrals could employ hundreds of people, and in 1771 Thomas Hearne saw 350 to 600 people using one driveline; on the Great Plains about 200 bison were stampeded into a ravine and killed in a single event 8,500 years ago. Foragers also built and maintained shared drivelines, nets and fish weirs.

Boyd and Richerson argue from historical accounts of foragers who lived among other foragers and outside state control that forager conflict ran on all scales, from small raids to battles with hundreds of warriors on each side, killed many people, and was larger between ethnolinguistic or tribal groups (typically 500 to a few thousand people) than within them. They report Burch's record of 77 raids and battles among the Inupiaq of northwest Alaska in the first half of the 19th century, in a region of 10 'nations' averaging 470 people; raiding parties travelled 80 to 300 km, and one party of 350 to 400 men attacked a village of about 600.

The same review argues that small-scale foraging societies made peace, formed alliances and traded across group lines. In northern California, wholly occupied by foragers until the mid 19th century, disputes inside and between groups were settled by negotiated compensation with a mediator, fighting usually stopped after one or a few casualties, traders could visit other tribes' villages to meet their trade partners, and goods such as obsidian and shell beads moved long distances by relay trade.

1780.content: Burch, from field work in north Alaska in 1960 to 1967 and older accounts, reports that the Inupiaq held two annual summer trade fairs (Colville River mouth and Kotzebue Sound) that drew people from all of north Alaska and sometimes from Siberia, southwest Alaska and the Mackenzie delta. The fairs were one of the very few settings in the traditional society where complete strangers could meet peacefully, and the main chance for trading partners from different regions to meet, often the only time in the year.

In traditional Inupiaq society, Burch reports, the trading partnership was a demanding lifelong non-kin bond set up by a gift and the term 'my trading partner'. One or two partners were all the average person could manage, while a boat owner (umialiq) might have five or six. By the 1960s partnerships carried less and the range ran from zero to a dozen or more, and people with more than three or four partners seldom did more than send small gifts every few years.

1781.content: Combining household balance sheets for 39 countries and wealth-distribution data for 20 countries (59 percent of the world's people, 75 percent of its wealth), with imputation for the rest, the authors estimate that in 2000 the richest 10 percent of the world's 3.7 billion adults owned 70.7 percent of household wealth, the richest 1 percent 31.6 percent, and the poorer half 3.7 percent. The global wealth Gini coefficient was 0.802 at purchasing-power parity, higher than the 0.642 Gini for world income they cite.

Within countries in the same estimate, wealth was always more unequal than income: wealth Gini coefficients ran from 0.547 for Japan to 0.784 for Brazil and 0.801 for the USA, and 0.803 for Switzerland, while most income Gini coefficients lie between 0.3 and 0.5. The median share of the richest 10 percent in the core national data was 51 percent.

1782.content: In an experience-sampling study, 309 Dutch adults (aged 18 to 75) answered four phone surveys a day for 10 days in 2018 and reported 5,284 episodes of sending or receiving gossip (talk about an absent third party). Of these, 68.4 percent were face-to-face, 74.9 percent came from first-hand experience and 73.7 percent were between two people. About six in ten episodes were relevant to judging the person's trustworthiness (60.6 percent), warmth (61.0), competence (59.2) or dominance (61.1), and 14.8 percent were about the person breaking a social norm.

In the same Dutch sample, 31.5 percent of gossip was rated neutral, 35.9 percent negative and 32.6 percent positive; gossip portraying the person negatively was only slightly more frequent than neutral or positive gossip. Participants valued their gossip partner more than the person gossiped about (relationship value 71.3 against 47.5 on a 0 to 100 index).

Listeners in the Dutch sample believed nearly all the gossip they received (mean 6.37 on a 1 to 7 scale; 63.0 percent rated it definitely true). They believed it slightly less when the sender and the target had conflicting interests; the number of sources and the number of times they had heard it were not associated with belief. When gossip about a person in their own network portrayed that person as trustworthy (335 cases), the value they placed on the relationship rose and they reported more intention to help and less to avoid the person.

1783.content: Reviewing research on animals and people, Hart proposes that the behaviour seen at the onset of febrile infections (lethargy, loss of appetite and less grooming, with what he lists as depression) is an organized, evolved strategy that supports fever in fighting viral and bacterial infection, rather than a maladaptive response or mere weakness. He describes the sick individual as at a life-or-death point, with its behaviour an all-out effort to overcome the disease.

1784.content: In repeated public-goods experiments with 1,120 university undergraduates in 16 participant pools across the world (among them Boston, Copenhagen, St. Gallen, Seoul, Minsk, Riyadh, Athens and Muscat), people could pay to punish group members after seeing their contributions. Punishment of free riders differed only weakly between pools, while punishment of people who had contributed as much or more than the punisher ('antisocial punishment') differed strongly: very little in some pools, and in others as harsh as the punishment of free riders.

In the same 16-pool experiment, average contributions with punishment ranged from 90 percent of the endowment in the most cooperative pool to 29 percent in the least, and pools with more antisocial punishment had lower cooperation. Across pools, mean antisocial punishment was strongly associated with a weaker response of low contributors to being punished (Spearman r = -0.87, 16 pools), and the authors report weak norms of civic cooperation and weak rule of law in a country as significant correlates of antisocial punishment.

1785.content: In a between-subjects vignette experiment, 346 University of California Santa Barbara students read that a coworker had been seen 'hitting on' her boss at a party. Belief rose with the number of named coworkers who each said they had seen it: mean believability 4.81 with one gossiper, 5.40 with two, 6.69 with three and 6.97 with four (about 31 per condition), 45 percent higher with four than with one. Adding benign alternative explanations slightly lowered belief (4.71 against 5.09).

In a second vignette experiment (99 students), a rival's report was believed least when a second person only repeated what the rival had said (mean 4.82 on a 1 to 10 scale), more when the second witness was the rival's close friend (5.55), and most when the second witness was independent (6.26). In a third (151 German students), gossip that a coworker had been arrested for shoplifting was believed less when the gossiper was competing with her for a promotion (4.86 against 5.76). Simple repetition of celebrity gossip (187 students) raised belief only slightly, and only among the few who found it uninteresting.

1786.content: In a brain-scanning study, 19 Caltech students read 40 trivia questions and rated their curiosity about each answer; curiosity while reading the question went with activity in the caudate, a striatal region earlier tied to anticipated reward. In a follow-up behavioural study (10 students spending limited tokens, 20 spending waiting time), students were more likely to pay a scarce token or wait up to 25 seconds to see an answer when they were more curious about it.

In a second experiment, 16 Caltech students rated their curiosity about trivia answers; 12 came back 11 to 16 days later for a surprise recall test. For questions they had first guessed wrongly, they recalled the correct answer better the more curious they had been, with differences between high, middle and low curiosity items all significant. In the scanner, curiosity raised activity in memory-related regions when the guess had been wrong.

1787.content: In a third-party punishment game played for about a day's wage in 12 societies (foragers, horticulturalists, pastoralists and city dwellers in Africa, the Pacific and South America), a third player could pay to reduce the earnings of a player who shared little with another. The minimum offer that escaped punishment was higher in societies with larger local groups (rank correlation 0.685, 12 societies) and larger ethnic groups (0.727, 11 societies), with or without control for region. The Hadza foragers of Tanzania, living in camps of about 33 people, had one of the lowest minimum offers (5.65 percent of the stake, or 0 when players who probably misunderstood the game were excluded).

1788.content: In laboratory experiments that alternated rounds of a public-goods game with rounds of an indirect-reciprocity game (in which a player's giving record decides whether others give to them), the need to keep a good reputation held contributions to the public good at an unexpectedly high level. When no indirect-reciprocity rounds were expected, contributions dropped quickly to zero, and alternating the games gave all players higher profits.

1789.content: In a randomised experiment, 52 US university students either assembled a plain black IKEA storage box or inspected a ready-made one and then bid for it with real money. Builders bid more ($0.78 against $0.48) and liked the box more. In a second experiment (106 people), students who folded an origami crane or frog bid 23 cents for their own creation, while other people offered 5 cents for it and 27 cents for figures made by experts.

In further experiments the higher valuation held only when the work was completed. Participants who built a small Lego set bid more for their own set than for a partner's, but after building and then taking it apart the difference was no longer significant. Participants who fully assembled an IKEA box bid $1.46 for it, against $0.59 from those allowed to complete only half the steps. The effect held for people who rated themselves low as well as high on liking do-it-yourself work.

1790.content: In a brain-scanning study at UCLA, 23 women whose mother or sister had died of breast cancer in the previous five years (11 diagnosed by structured interview with complicated grief, 12 without) viewed photos of the dead person and words from their own account of the death. Both groups showed activity in pain-related regions; only the women diagnosed with complicated grief showed activity in the nucleus accumbens, a reward region, while the others showed reduced activity there. Accumbens activity rose with self-reported yearning for the dead person (r = 0.42) and did not track time since the death, age or general mood.

1791.content: In a randomized field experiment on eBay, an established dealer with a very high reputation sold matched pairs of lots of vintage postcards under his own seller identity and under new seller identities that he also ran. Buyers were willing to pay 8.1 percent more of the selling price under the established identity. In a second experiment comparing new sellers with and without negative feedback, one or two negative ratings did not change what buyers were willing to pay.

1792.content: Estimating US household wealth by capitalizing income reported on tax returns, matched to the national household balance sheets, Saez and Zucman find that the share of wealth held by the top 1 percent of families rose steadily from the late 1970s to 42 percent in 2012, and the share of the top 0.1 percent from 7 percent in 1978 to 22 percent in 2012, close to its level in 1929.

In the same series, the share of US household wealth held by the bottom 90 percent of families rose from 20 percent in the 1920s to 35 percent in the mid-1980s and then fell to about 23 percent in 2012. In 2012 the bottom 90 percent (144 million families, $84,000 on average) owned about as much as the top 0.1 percent (160,700 families with net assets above $20 million), each about 22 percent of the total.

1793.content: Re-estimating US top wealth from tax data while allowing returns to differ within asset classes (the rich earn higher returns on their interest-bearing assets), Smith, Zidar and Zwick find that from 1989 to 2016 the top 1 percent wealth share rose by 6.6 percentage points to 33.7 percent, the top 0.1 percent by 4.6 points to 15.7 percent, and the top 0.01 percent by 2.9 points to 7.1 percent. They conclude that wealth inequality is high and has risen substantially.

1794.content: Merker reviews comparative neurology, experimental psychology, neurophysiology and clinical data and argues that a highly conserved upper brainstem system, from the roof of the midbrain to the basal diencephalon, performs a late step in action control and supports conscious function, and that it keeps working without cortical input. He offers this as an account of the purposive, goal-directed behaviour of mammals after experimental removal of the cortex and of the evidence that children born without a cortex are conscious.

1795.content: An online survey of 108 primary caregivers of children born with hydranencephaly (almost no cerebral cortex), recruited through a parent support group, asked 106 questions on the child's responsiveness to the surroundings, emotional reactivity, mood and agency. A conservative measure of agreement among the answers gave a common portrait of the children's responsiveness and expressive behaviour, which the authors judge incompatible on several counts with the unconsciousness of the vegetative state.

1796.content: A systematic review of 659 published papers (peer-reviewed studies, editorials and commentaries) on parents and children sharing a sleeping surface covered its correlates (such as socioeconomic and cultural factors) and its purported risks and outcomes (such as sudden infant death syndrome and sleep problems). The authors found general design limitations and a lack of convincing evidence, which in their view rule out strong generalisations about harm or benefit.

From 98 eligible studies the authors drew a world heat-map of how common parent-child bed-sharing is, and call for more research in the societies where bed-sharing is the norm, bringing anthropology, psychology and paediatrics together on how nightly closeness to parents bears on children's development.

1797.content: In a two-wave yearly survey of 164 students in grades 6 to 9 (aged 11 to 15 at the start, 56% girls) in one western Canadian school district, cross-lagged structural models tested mattering to mother, father and friends against reported depressive symptoms and problem behaviours. Significant cross-lagged links appeared only between mattering to friends and depressive symptoms and problem behaviours; with one exception, mattering to parents showed no direct link with well-being over time. The authors conclude that mattering may not be as strongly protective of adolescent well-being as previously suggested.

1798.content: Among 197 UK community adults (mean age 40, recruited online through Prolific) who completed the General Mattering Scale, the Anti-Mattering Scale and a short form of the CES-D depression scale three times, three weeks apart, mattering correlated strongly and negatively, and feelings of not mattering strongly and positively, with depressive symptom scores at every wave. In the random-intercept model the between-person correlation was -0.73 for mattering and 0.82 for not mattering with depressive symptom scores, while within-person cross-lagged effects were mostly not significant; the authors find tentative support only for depressive symptoms being followed by more feelings of not mattering.

1799.content: Among Meriam men of Mer (Murray Island), Torres Strait, Australia, who fish, hunt turtle and collect shellfish (once also full-time gardeners, now also buying store food), turtle hunters (50 men with age-specific data) had higher cumulative reproductive success than nonhunters (48) in every five-year age class, significantly so at ages 20 to 24 and 25 to 29. Projected over ages 15 to 49, the expected lifetime reproductive success was about 2.4 times that of nonhunters for turtle hunters and about 2.8 times for hunt leaders. Men known as outstanding fishermen, dancers, political leaders or "popular with the ladies" showed no such difference.

Meriam turtle hunters averaged more mates (women with whom they had surviving offspring: 0.76 against 0.46 for other men aged 15 and over), a difference that held after controlling for age, and more co-resident sexual partners; their partners, though not their mates, were significantly younger. Hunters' mates also received more nominations as the hardest-working women on the island.

Among Meriam men aged 30 and over, the share who had fathered no child was 0.20 for turtle hunters, 0.41 for nonhunters and 0.17 for hunt leaders; a survival analysis of time to first birth showed a significantly shorter wait for hunters (54) than for nonhunters (59).

1800.content: Among 44 Shuar forager-horticulturalist children (mean age 8.1) in a roadless community in Amazonian Ecuador, doubly labelled water showed total daily energy expenditure (adjusted mean 1738 kcal) indistinguishable from 40 US and UK children (1811 kcal), although Shuar children were about 25% more physically active by accelerometry and had about 20% higher resting energy expenditure (1255 against 1042 kcal), which rose with their immunoglobulin G level.

The authors propose that, within a constrained daily energy budget, trade-offs between competing tasks such as immune activity, physical activity and growth shape how children develop, and that for populations in the developing world high physical and immune activity may leave less energy for growth even when food is not short. They read the mismatch between lifestyle and total expenditure as support for the position that changes in diet, more than in physical activity, underlie the rise in obesity.

1801.content: Actigraphy, sleep diaries, written questions and interviews with adolescents in three Mexican settings (Mexico City 50, a Totonac farming town in Puebla 51, a Maya subsistence village in Campeche 44) found that solitary sleep predominated in Mexico City (72%), while in the Maya village 89% shared their sleeping quarters with household members; in Puebla 33% slept alone and 67% shared with adults, children or both. Urban adolescents slept in rooms built to buffer sound, light and temperature; rural adolescents slept in shared quarters with less buffering.

1802.content: In beagles (Canis lupus familiaris) moved from enriched, spacious outdoor group housing to six weeks of solitary housing in small indoor kennels, the dogs showed lower postures and lasting rises in self-grooming, paw lifting and vocalising, with incidents of eating faeces and repetitive behaviour, which the authors read as signs of chronic stress. When challenged outside the kennel, the restricted dogs showed more excitement, aggression and uncertainty, and males behaved more dominantly and aggressively towards other dogs.

1803.content: Comparing 72 dogs (Canis lupus familiaris) kept for a year or more under four housing conditions, privately owned dogs had the lowest urinary cortisol to creatinine ratios, and dogs kept individually in kennels of 1.7 square metres (with daytime outdoor kennels of 3.6 square metres) had the highest; cortisol ratios differed significantly between the owned dogs and each kennel group. When undisturbed, the dogs in the most austere housing showed high levels of locomotion, nosing, urinating and paw lifting, and after a slamming door or a researcher's presence they showed body shaking, yawning, ambivalent postures and displacement behaviours.

1804.content: A Bayesian meta-analysis of reproductive skew (inequality in number of surviving offspring, adjusted for unequal time at risk) in 90 human populations and 49 other mammal species found lower male skew and smaller sex differences in skew in humans than in most other mammals, though humans fall within the mammalian range. In the 14 polygynous human populations male skew was much lower than in 41 polygynous non-human mammals, and female skew somewhat higher.

Across the 90 human populations, male and female reproductive skew and the sex difference in skew were more or less the same across foraging, horticultural, (agro)pastoral, agricultural and market-based populations. Among the 25 forager populations, 10 had normative monogamy, 13 tolerated but rare polygyny and 2 normative polygyny.

1805.content: A dated species-level phylogeny of nearly all living mammals found that net per-lineage diversification rates barely changed across the Cretaceous/Tertiary boundary; rates instead spiked with the origins of the present placental superorders and orders about 93 million years ago, then fell and stayed low until rising again in the Eocene and Oligocene.

1806.content: Using linked Danish birth cohort and register data and a fuzzy regression-discontinuity design built on the rule that Danish children enter kindergarten in the calendar year they turn six, the authors find that a one-year delay in kindergarten entry cut parent-reported inattention/hyperactivity scores on the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire at age 7 by 0.73 standard deviations; the effect was identified mainly for girls and persisted at age 11.

1807.content: When the Seattle School District moved secondary school start from 07:50 to 08:45, wrist actigraphy of sophomores in the same science class at two high schools (94 students in spring 2016, 84 in spring 2017) showed a 44-minute later median wake time on school days and no significant change in sleep onset, giving a 34-minute longer median school-night sleep. Social jet lag fell, daytime sleepiness fell, median grades were 4.5% higher, and one of the two schools had fewer first-period absences and tardies.

1808.content: In the Uppsala multigenerational cohort (about 14,000 people born at Uppsala University Hospital, Sweden, 1915 to 1929, followed with their descendants in national registers to 2009), lower parental fertility and higher parental socioeconomic position went with better school marks, more university entry and higher family income in descendants across the generations studied, with the largest gains where both coincided. Low fertility and high socioeconomic position did not go with more descendants: higher parental position had no effect on the number of children of the cohort members' children and went with fewer children among their grandchildren by 2009, mostly through later childbearing in high-status lineages.

In the same cohort, each extra child of the cohort members (mean 1.7 children) went with more grandchildren, great-grandchildren and total estimated fitness in an essentially straight line across the whole range of family sizes, in both high and low status lineages, with no inverted U and no levelling off at the high end; the authors conclude that the number of children that would maximise long-term descendants lies far above the observed mean.

1809.content: In a within-subjects laboratory study, 16 healthy adolescents (mean age 17.4, 56% female) used a bright tablet screen (80 lux), a dim screen (1 lux) and a short-wavelength-filtered screen (f.lux, 50 lux) for one hour before their usual bedtime. Bright against dim screens produced significant but small differences in reaction-task speed (23 ms) and accuracy (13%), which the authors judge of minimal clinical significance, and no significant effects on sleep onset latency, slow rolling eye movements or slow-wave and REM minutes in the first two sleep cycles; chronotype did not interact with the conditions.

1810.content: Surveys of children in the same English schools (five areas, urban to rural) in 1971, 1990 and 2010, and of their parents in 1990 and 2010, found that the share of primary school children whose parents allowed them to travel home from school alone fell from 86% in 1971 to 35% in 1990 and 25% in 2010. The fall came from younger children: among 7 and 8 year olds it went from 80% in 1971 to 19% in 1990 and 6% in 2010, while for secondary school children it changed little between 1990 and 2010.

1811.content: Two longitudinal samples of children in child care (72 and 106) were followed from infancy through preschool. Attachment to mother (Strange Situation, reunion behaviour at 4, Attachment Q-Set) tended to be stable. The quality of the child's relationship with a child care teacher (Attachment Q-Set) was stable when the teacher stayed the same; when the teacher changed it tended to be unstable until about 30 months of age, and after 30 months it was stable whether or not the teacher changed. Relationships with mother and with teacher did not match.

1812.content: Jensen and colleagues, writing in the journal of the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, argue that through an evolutionary lens some conditions labelled mental disorders are better seen as adaptive responses to early environments, or as brain function tuned to some environments at the cost of a poorer fit to others. Taking the traits the DSM labels attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (inattention, impulsivity, motor hyperactivity), they argue these may be adaptive depending on the nature of the child's environment, and that this reframing has treatment implications.

1813.content: Among the Hadza hunter-gatherers of Tanzania, 350 stool samples from 188 people in two camps over 12 months (five sub-seasons) showed that the gut microbiome reconfigures with the seasons and returns: Dry-season samples from two successive years could not be told apart, while both differed from the Wet season. Many Bacteroidetes units (70.2%) disappeared between the 2013 Late-Dry and 2014 Early-Wet sub-seasons, and 78.2% of those reappeared later. The Wet-season community carried a less diverse set of carbohydrate-digesting enzymes than the Dry-season community.

Set against gut-microbiome data from 18 populations in 16 countries (26 cohorts), the communities lined up along one axis that tracked modernization. Families common in the Hadza and other traditional groups (Spirochaetaceae, Succinivibrionaceae) were rare or undetected in industrialized guts, Prevotellaceae averaged 29.8% in traditional populations against 7.6% in industrialized ones, and the taxa most seasonally volatile in the Hadza were the ones that separate industrialized from traditional populations. The authors read this as some microbial lineages having declined in modernized populations, with a diet low in plant-derived complex carbohydrates as one likely factor among several.

1814.content: Among 98 Old Order Amish adults aged 18 to 75 in a farming community in southern Ontario, who use no cars or electrical appliances, pedometers worn for 7 days counted an average of 18,425 steps a day for men and 14,196 for women. Men reported 10.0 hours a week of vigorous activity, 42.8 of moderate activity and 12.0 of walking; women 3.4, 39.2 and 5.7 hours. 25% of the men and 27% of the women had a BMI of 25 or more, and 0% of the men and 9% of the women a BMI of 30 or more.

1815.content: Cordain and colleagues review how food staples and processing introduced in the Neolithic and Industrial periods changed seven nutritional characteristics of ancestral hominin diets: glycemic load, fatty acid composition, macronutrient composition, micronutrient density, acid-base balance, the sodium-potassium ratio and fiber content. They argue that these changes, about 10,000 years old or younger, came too recently for the human genome to adjust, and that the clash may underlie many chronic diseases of Western populations.

1816.content: Crittenden reviews ethnographic reports, Paleolithic rock art and evidence from non-human primates on honey and bee larvae, and argues that early hominins likely raided beehives with Oldowan stone tools and that honey and larvae supplied significant energy alongside meat and plant foods, possibly helping to fuel the enlarging hominin brain.

1817.content: In the US REGARDS cohort, 7,985 black and white adults aged 45 or older wore a hip accelerometer for up to 7 days and were followed for a median 4.0 years (340 deaths). Sedentary time took up 77.4% of waking wear time (about 12.3 hours a day). After adjustment for moderate-to-vigorous activity and cardiovascular risk factors, the top quartile of total sedentary time carried a hazard ratio for death of 2.63 against the bottom quartile, and the top quartile of mean sedentary bout length (12.4 minutes or more per bout) a hazard ratio of 1.96. Mortality risk rose sharply at about 10 minutes per bout, and people high on both total time and bout length had the highest risk (HR 2.00).

In the same cohort, the share of sedentary time spent in bouts shorter than 30 minutes was linked to a lower mortality risk even after accounting for time spent in bouts of 60 minutes or more, and more, longer and more intense breaks in sedentary time were each linked to lower all-cause mortality.

1818.content: Dunbar reviews social grooming in primates, including humans, as a bonding mechanism that bears on lifetime reproductive fitness, and argues that the neuroendocrine pathways are unresolved: alongside the oxytocin account there is equally good but often ignored evidence for a role of endorphins, and the two neuropeptide families may play different roles in bonding in primates and non-primates.

1819.content: Gleeson and colleagues review how exercise lowers inflammation. They state that regular exercise lowers the risk of chronic metabolic and cardiorespiratory disease partly through anti-inflammatory effects, which may work through less visceral fat (and so less release of adipokines) and through an anti-inflammatory environment set up by each bout of exercise. The same effects are likely behind the suppressed immunity that makes elite athletes more prone to infections.

1820.content: Pooling 358 population-based surveys from 168 countries with 1.9 million participants, WHO authors estimate that 27.5% of adults worldwide in 2016 did not reach 150 minutes of moderate or 75 minutes of vigorous activity a week (23.4% of men, 31.7% of women), with no significant change since 2001 (28.5%). The share was more than twice as high in high-income countries (36.8%) as in low-income countries (16.2%), and it rose in high-income countries from 31.6% in 2001.

1821.content: Groups of 11 to 13 people ate 240 kcal (1000 kJ) servings of 38 common foods and rated fullness every 15 minutes for 2 hours. Taking white bread as 100%, boiled potatoes scored highest at 323% and croissants lowest at 47%, a sevenfold range at equal calories. Fullness scores rose with serving weight (r = 0.66), protein (r = 0.37), fibre (r = 0.46) and water content (r = 0.64), and fell with fat content (r = -0.43) and with how palatable people rated the food (r = -0.64).

Across the 38 foods, fullness per calorie ran opposite to palatability: the foods people rated tastier scored lower on the satiety index (r = -0.64), while foods with more fibre, water and protein scored higher.

1822.content: Among Tsimane forager-horticulturalists in lowland Bolivia, production-and-sharing interviews with 1,254 people in 8 communities (2005 to 2010, mean 14 months) showed net food flowing down the generations. Grandmothers gave a mean net of 117 kcal a day to their grandchildren, peaking at 176 in their 40s; grandfathers gave a mean net of 223 kcal a day, peaking at 337 in their 60s and still significant into their 70s. Fathers gave offspring a mean net of 1,107 kcal a day (peak 1,737 in their 30s), mothers 177 (peak 1,042). Grandchildren under 12 received 90 more kcal a day from grandparents when their mother was absent.

Between Tsimane households, older families made net food transfers to closely related younger families, and the amount rose with the number of unproductive mouths in the receiving family and fell with those in the giving family. Need alone, without kinship, did not produce significant net transfers (p > 0.12); the largest flows ran between parents and the families of their adult children.

1823.content: Jakubiak and Feeney propose a model in which receiving affectionate touch from close others promotes relational, psychological and physical well-being in adults, along two paths: by reducing stress and independently of stress, through relational-cognitive changes and neurobiological changes. They note that while touch is known to promote well-being in infancy, its effects in adult close relationships had been largely unexplored, and they review the existing adult studies and set out a research agenda.

1824.content: In male Wistar rats (Rattus norvegicus), all with free chow, extended access (18 to 23 hours a day for 40 days) to a cafeteria diet of bacon, sausage, cheesecake, pound cake, frosting and chocolate led to almost twice the daily calorie intake of chow-only or 1-hour-access rats, with only about 5% of calories from chow, marked weight gain, and steadily rising brain-stimulation reward thresholds, a sign of reduced reward responsiveness. Striatal dopamine D2 receptor levels fell in these rats, and across groups heavier rats had lower D2 receptor levels.

Rats with extended cafeteria-diet access kept eating palatable food when a light previously paired with foot shock was shown, while chow-only and restricted-access rats cut their intake (compulsive-like eating in the authors' terms). Knocking down striatal D2 receptors with a lentivirus made reward thresholds rise almost at once on extended access and made food intake insensitive to the shock cue after only 14 days of access, without changing total calorie intake or weight gain.

1825.content: Among Tsimane forager-horticulturalists of the Bolivian Amazon, 2,496 24-hour dietary recalls from 78 villages (2010 to 2015) showed a high-energy diet (about 2,736 kcal a day for men and 2,422 for women), 64% of calories from complex carbohydrates and low fat (40 to 46 g a day). Calories came from 26 cultivated crops (61.9%, mostly plantain, rice, manioc and corn), 43 species of fish (15.6%), 32 species of wild game (6.1%), domestic meat (7.5%), wild fruit and vegetables (0.7%) and market foods (8.1%).

Over the 5.5 years of the study, Tsimane total energy and carbohydrate intake rose, and the sugar and cooking oil households acquired (bought, given or traded) rose the most, by 15.8 g and 4.9 ml per person a day from 2010 to 2015, alongside rising BMI, body fat and share overweight. The neighbouring Moseten, closely related but more integrated into Bolivian markets, acquired more than twice the sugar (65.3 against 19.0 g a day) and five times the oil (45.7 against 8.5 ml a day) of the Tsimane, ate more market and domestic foods and less wild fish and game, and took in 653 fewer kcal a day.

1826.content: Using genome-wide data from 230 West Eurasians who lived between 6500 and 1000 BCE, merged with present-day Europeans (617 samples, about 1.08 million SNPs), the authors ran the first scan for selection with ancient DNA and found twelve genome-wide significant signals, at loci tied to diet, skin pigmentation and immunity, plus two separate episodes of selection on height. The strongest was the lactase-persistence variant, which reached appreciable frequency in Europe only in the last four thousand years; others sat near FADS1 and DHCR7 (fatty acid and vitamin D metabolism), SLC45A2 (light skin), the TLR1-TLR6-TLR10 cluster and the MHC (immunity).

For most of the twelve selected loci, allele frequencies in present-day Europeans lie outside the range of any ancient population sampled, so Europeans of about four thousand years ago differed in some important traits from Europeans today despite similar overall ancestry.

1827.content: McGlone, Wessberg and Olausson review evidence that touch carries two inputs to the brain: the well-known discriminative one and an affective one. They propose that a class of low-threshold mechanosensitive C fibres in hairy skin (C-tactile afferents) are the neurobiological substrate for the affective and rewarding properties of touch.

1828.content: In the SUN cohort, 8,451 middle-aged Spanish university graduates who were not overweight or obese at the start were followed for a median 8.9 years; 1,939 became overweight or obese. Ultra-processed food intake was measured at baseline with a 136-item food-frequency survey. After adjustment for confounders, people in the highest quarter of ultra-processed food intake had a 26% higher hazard of becoming overweight or obese than those in the lowest quarter (HR 1.26, 95% CI 1.10 to 1.45).

1829.content: Among 103 Tsimane forager-horticulturalist men in four villages of lowland Bolivia, men ranked by half their male co-villagers as having more political influence had lower first-morning urinary cortisol (standardised beta -0.27 after controlling for age, body mass index and income), and cortisol was 0.51 standard deviations lower in the top than in the bottom influence quartile. The number of men who named a man as a regular food, labour and conflict-support partner partly carried the link (a 33% reduction in the influence effect when partners were added). In one village measured in 2005 and 2009, among 19 men who lost influence, the greater the loss the higher their cortisol at the end.

In the same Tsimane men, more influential men were less likely to have a respiratory infection found by visiting physicians (odds ratio 0.73, 166 men, 456 observations; 16% of all men had one, 13% of men in the top influence quartile), and among men who lost influence between 2005 and 2009 a smaller loss went with lower odds of respiratory infection. Influence was not associated with C-reactive protein, sedimentation rate, lymphocyte count, intestinal parasites, skin infection or cardiovascular findings. Income from sporadic wage labour and sales was associated with higher cortisol independent of influence, age and body mass index.

1830.content: Arnsten reviews human and animal work showing that even mild acute uncontrollable stress rapidly impairs prefrontal functions such as working memory and flexible thinking, while it spares or strengthens amygdala-based emotional learning and basal-ganglia habits. People who felt in control of a stressor (even falsely) were often not impaired, while those who felt out of control were. In rats, inescapable shock impaired attention but escapable shock did not. The mechanism is high catecholamine release (noradrenaline and dopamine) driven by the amygdala, which weakens prefrontal network firing.

Chronic stress in rats reduces dendrite length, branching and spine density of prefrontal layer II/III neurons, beginning after about one week (possibly after one exposure), while amygdala dendrites expand under the same stress. Arnsten concludes that chronic stress weakens the structures that give negative feedback on the stress response and strengthens those that drive it. The prefrontal dendritic changes gradually reverse when the stress stops.

1831.content: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 124 randomised and observational studies (through April 2014) compared kangaroo mother care (mostly skin-to-skin contact on the mother's chest) with conventional care. Among low birthweight newborns, kangaroo care was associated with 36% lower mortality (relative risk 0.64), lower risk of sepsis (0.53), hypothermia (0.22), hypoglycaemia (0.12) and hospital readmission (0.42), and more exclusive breastfeeding (1.50). Newborns in kangaroo care had slower breathing, higher oxygen saturation and temperature, more head growth and lower pain scores.

In the same meta-analysis, eleven studies promoting 22 or more hours of skin-to-skin contact per day showed lower mortality with kangaroo care (relative risk 0.64), while there was no association in the one study promoting 4 to 8 hours a day. In the two studies of newborns of all birth weights, kangaroo care did not change mortality (relative risk 1.04). Standardised cortisol levels did not differ significantly between kangaroo care and control groups (3 studies).

1832.content: In 6,956 New York Times articles that appeared on the paper's home page over about three months (2008), articles scored by blind coders as evoking more anger, anxiety or awe were more likely to make the most e-mailed list, while articles evoking more sadness were less likely, controlling for how long and how prominently each article was featured, timing, author fame, and how useful, interesting or surprising it was. A one standard deviation rise in anger raised the odds of making the list by 34%, about the same as 2.9 extra hours as the lead story; a one standard deviation rise in awe raised them by 30%. Positive articles overall were more shared than negative ones.
