In rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) held in pairs for 1 or 7 days, subordinate fish had raised serotonin activity (the 5-HIAA to 5-HT ratio) in the telencephalon and brain stem, raised plasma cortisol and raised pituitary POMC expression after 1 day. After 7 days serotonin activity and POMC stayed high; cortisol fell but stayed above that of dominant fish. In 1-day subordinates cortisol tracked the number of attacks received; after a week it no longer did. The authors conclude that the chronic stress of subordinates in an established hierarchy is tied more to the threat posed by the dominant fish's presence than to actual fights.

2624.content: Abstract only. Reviewing the genetics of circadian clocks in bacteria, fungi, plants and animals, Young and Kay report that every clock studied is built on autoregulatory genetic networks, and that the weight of evidence favours independent evolutionary origins of the clock in different kingdoms.

2625.content: A review of a series of recent studies on self-evaluation describes a local dominance effect: comparisons with a few discrete individuals influence how people rate themselves more than comparisons with larger aggregates. The authors name physical proximity and self-enhancement among the moderators. The abstract gives no sample sizes or effect sizes.

2626.content: In two fMRI experiments with 24 healthy right-handed adults each (72 scanned in all, including a 24-person non-social control), participants played a simple game for money alongside two simulated players ranked above and below them by a star system. Seeing the higher-ranked player engaged occipital/parietal cortex, ventral striatum, parahippocampal cortex and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex whether the ranking was fixed or could change. Only when ranks could change with performance did seeing the higher-ranked player also engage the amygdala, medial prefrontal cortex, thalamus, posterior cingulate and motor preparation areas; amygdala activity there correlated with the positive feeling reported in the top position (r = 0.48).

In the changeable-hierarchy experiment, only outcomes that could move the participant's rank produced significant brain responses after controlling for winning or losing money; the authors report that the rank value of an outcome contributed to ventral striatal activity about as much as the money reward itself.

2627.content: American black bears (Ursus americanus) at the Sierra Nevada and Great Basin interface in the western United States that fed on garbage at the urban-wildland edge were compared with bears living in wildland, and with the same population 10 to 15 years earlier. Urban-interface bears were active for fewer hours per day (8.5 against 13.3 hours), shifted their activity to the night, entered dens later and stayed in them for fewer days.

2628.content: In laboratory rats (Rattus norvegicus), stress given for 2 hours just before an antigen challenge to the skin enhanced the delayed-type hypersensitivity (cell-mediated) skin reaction; 5 hours gave the same enhancement and a more intense acute stress gave a larger one, together with a larger redeployment of white blood cells.

In the same rat experiments, stress given for 3 weeks before sensitization suppressed the same skin immune reaction, whether the stress stopped at sensitization, continued a week until challenge, or continued a week after it. With longer exposure the stress-induced shift of blood lymphocytes became smaller, in step with a blunted glucocorticoid response.

2629.content: In a natural experiment in northern New Mexico gas fields (2011 to 2014; 12 pairs of sites with and without constantly running compressor engines, 10 nest boxes per site), three cavity-nesting bird species, western bluebird (Sialia mexicana), mountain bluebird (Sialia currucoides) and ash-throated flycatcher (Myiarchus cinerascens), were sampled for corticosterone. Louder noise at the nest went with lower baseline corticosterone in adult females and nestlings and with a higher corticosterone response to capture stress in nestlings, consistently across species. The authors read this as hypocorticism, the pattern of chronic stress in laboratory animals.

In the same study, hatching success of western bluebirds (Sialia mexicana), the species most likely to nest in the noisiest places, fell as noise at the nest box rose; the other two species, which avoid noise, showed no such drop. Nestlings of all three species grew feathers and body size fastest at intermediate noise levels. Lower maternal baseline corticosterone during incubation went with lower hatching success across species.

2630.content: In adult zebrafish (Danio rerio), the authors screened transgenic lines in which a neurotoxin silenced neurons in defined brain regions; 16 of 30 lines learned an active avoidance task (escaping a light paired with shock) less well. In one line the silenced cells were a mostly glutamatergic group in the medial zone of the dorsal telencephalon (Dm), the region proposed as the fish counterpart of the mammalian amygdala; these fish were impaired in both active avoidance and Pavlovian fear conditioning, where wild type fish roughly tripled their turning after training.

2631.content: Larval zebrafish (Danio rerio) learned to avoid a light that had been paired with a mild shock, but failed to learn it after being exposed to inescapable shock. Destroying inputs to the habenula (photobleaching of KillerRed-expressing afferents) produced a similar failure, and silencing dorsal habenula neurons with tetanus toxin was enough to prevent avoidance. The authors suggest the region may signal the ability to control a stressor.

2632.content: Free-ranging vervet monkeys (then named Cercopithecus aethiops, now placed in Chlorocebus) give different alarm calls to leopards, martial eagles and pythons. When recorded alarms were played back with no predator present, the monkeys ran into trees at leopard alarms, looked up at eagle alarms and looked down at snake alarms. Infants gave the calls to a wider range of animals and objects, and predator classification improved with age and experience.

2633.content: Male BALB/c mice (Mus musculus) raised germ-free showed a much larger rise in ACTH and corticosterone after 1 hour of restraint than genetically identical mice with a normal microbiota (about 50 animals per group across time points), but no difference after ether exposure. The germ-free mice had higher hypothalamic CRF, lower cortical glucocorticoid receptor transcripts and lower BDNF protein in cortex and hippocampus; mothers of both groups nursed and licked their pups equally.

In the same study, giving germ-free mice a single common infant gut bacterium (Bifidobacterium infantis) from birth brought their stress-hormone response back down, while a pathogenic Escherichia coli strain raised it further. A full normal microbiota given at 6 weeks of age partly corrected the exaggerated response when the mice were tested at 9 weeks; the same microbiota given later, before testing at 17 weeks, did not.

2634.content: In fruit flies (Drosophila melanogaster) in a heat box, a fly that was heated whenever it stopped walking reliably resumed walking to escape the heat. A fly given the same heat without control over it learned that its behaviour had no effect and stopped responding; afterwards it walked more slowly and took longer and more frequent rests, more so in females than in males.

2635.content: In fruit flies (Drosophila melanogaster), pairs of flies each in a small dark chamber got the same sequence of mild electric shocks, delivered whenever the 'master' fly stopped walking for more than a second. The yoked fly, whose walking had no effect on the shocks, was transiently worse at place learning, took longer to leave the chamber towards light, and afterwards walked more slowly in fewer and shorter bouts. The authors note that earlier heat-pulse studies showed similar effects and read the parallel as support for uncontrollability being what induces the state.

2636.content: In a diary study of 59 employees (357 matched Friday and Monday reports over 12 weeks), weeks in which a person ended the work week with more unfinished tasks were followed by more impaired sleep at the weekend, and this within-person link ran through affective rumination. Problem-solving pondering went with less sleep impairment, but its indirect path was not significant. Employees with more unfinished tasks across the 3 months also reported more weekend sleep impairment.

2637.content: A meta-analysis of 277 studies with 177,635 participants from adolescence to old age found that the global social network grew until young adulthood and then shrank steadily; personal and friendship networks shrank throughout adulthood; the family network stayed the same size from adolescence to old age; and networks of coworkers or neighbours mattered only at certain ages. Life events tied to age, such as becoming a parent, starting a job or being widowed, changed networks in the same way.
In the same meta-analysis, personal networks and friendship networks showed a period effect: their reported size decreased over the last 35 years covered by the studies.

2638.content: Abstract only. In a nationwide US survey, 830 mothers reported their own active outdoor play as children and their children's play today. The children were reported to spend considerably less time playing outdoors than their mothers had as children. The author names television and digital media and worries about crime and safety among the reasons for the fall.

2639.content: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 30 studies (from 3602 screened) that examined healthy girls for Tanner breast stage 2, the first sign of puberty, found that the age at which it appeared fell by 0.24 years per decade from 1977 to 2013 (95% confidence interval 0.04 to 0.44 years), almost three months per decade. Restricting to 18 studies that described palpating the breast gave 0.26 years per decade. Onset was earliest in US studies (8.8 to 10.3 years) and latest in African ones (10.1 to 13.2 years).

2640.content: Abstract only. Parents of 29,287 infants and toddlers (birth to 36 months) in 17 countries and regions, 12 mostly Asian and 5 mostly white Western (Australia, Canada, New Zealand, United Kingdom, United States), filled in an internet sleep questionnaire. Bed-sharing with parents ranged from 5.8% in New Zealand to 83.2% in Vietnam; children in the mostly Asian countries were more likely to share a bed and a room with parents, went to bed later and slept less in total (11.6 hours in Japan to 13.3 in New Zealand).

2641.content: Using the CORESIDENCE database (793 time points in 156 countries, 1970 to 2020), the authors find that average household size ranges from 1.8 people in Denmark to 8.4 in Senegal and has fallen widely, by about 0.5 persons per decade on average. Fewer children account for over three quarters of the variation and of the fall; the number of other relatives in households stayed about level or fell only moderately.

In the same database, single-person households headed by an adult aged 50 or over reach 20 percent of households in the United States and around 25 percent in Hungary, Germany and the Netherlands, with marked rises in recent decades, while they stay below 10 percent in every African country and in most of Asia and Oceania.

2642.content: In MIT field studies (weekly visits to schools and two nursing homes 2001 to 2003, several hundred participants, plus a 2005 study of the robot seal Paro with 23 residents aged 60 to 104), children and elders formed attachments to commercial robots. A 76-year-old nursing home resident, Andy, became attached to a My Real Baby doll and to the home's Aibo and Furby robots: he held the doll to his chest and asked it 'I love you. Do you love me?', fed it a bottle when it was 'hungry', tried to work out the robots' 'needs' and tried to protect them; the stronger his attachment, the more he nurtured.

In the 2005 Paro study, the nursing home residents gave a young male researcher more attention than the robot seal he had brought; the home was so understaffed that management stopped the study. The authors write that the robot was the occasion for residents to express a desire for human connection, and that the lack of staff in geriatric care makes robots tempting and risks residents being left alone with them.

2643.content: Comparing the mean number of children intended by women aged 20 to 24 (born in the early 1970s, Fertility and Family Surveys of the 1990s) with completed fertility of the same birth cohorts at about age 40 in 19 European countries and the US, the authors find that in every country women ended with fewer children on average than intended, and more remained childless than had intended to. In Austria, for example, women intended 1.95 children and had 1.67; 5.8% intended to stay childless and 19.9% did. The gap in childlessness was widest in Southern Europe (about 22% childless in Spain and Italy, about 20 points above intentions) and the German-speaking countries, and smallest in Central and Eastern Europe.

In the same comparison, the shortfall between intended and completed family size was largest among highly educated women in most of the countries studied, and the educational pattern differed by region, most clearly for childlessness.

2644.content: In the 2013 Panel Study of Income Dynamics (about 12,000 US adults aged 25 or over with a living parent or adult child), 13.2% lived with a parent or adult child and 74.8% had the nearest one within 30 miles; 6.8% had the nearest one 500 miles or more away. Only 35.5% had all of their parents and adult children within 30 miles, and among adults with both a living parent and an adult child, 21.2%. Disadvantaged groups were more likely to have parents or adult children nearby.

2645.content: Reviewing the historical fertility transition, the fall from as many as eight births per woman to low fertility in much of Europe and North America in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, Guinnane reports that until the second half of the nineteenth century most fertility control relied on withdrawal (coitus interruptus) and abstinence. Three sets of surveys (German surveys of the early twentieth century, the US Mosher survey of women born in the 1850s and 1860s, and a survey of French doctors in the 1890s) agree that withdrawal and abstinence remained married couples' main methods into the early twentieth century; the pill dates from the 1950s, with wide use from the 1960s.

Guinnane concludes that, since withdrawal and abstinence had been available essentially throughout human history, the condom and similar new methods are unlikely to have played a strong role in the historical fertility transition; early rubber condoms were costly (a year's supply cost a Berlin worker ten to fifteen days of work in the early twentieth century).

2646.content: In the British Children's Play Survey (April 2020, a nationally representative sample of 1919 parents and caregivers of children aged 5 to 11 in Great Britain), parents who gave an age said their child was or would be allowed out alone in the neighbourhood at 10.74 years on average (SD 2.20), against 8.91 years (SD 2.31) at which they recalled being allowed out themselves; the difference was significant. 108 respondents (almost 6%) said they would not allow their child out alone and gave no age. Parents more tolerant of risk in play allowed children out younger, and children in Scotland were allowed out more than a year earlier than in England and Wales.

2647.content: Abstract only. Using time-use data from 11 Western countries between 1965 and 2012, the authors find for both mothers and fathers a widespread educational gradient (more educated parents spend more time on child care) and an increase in child-care time over the period. In a number of countries the educational gradient widened, and in none did it narrow.

2648.content: In the 2004 Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (10 continental European countries; analysis sample about 10,000 grandparents with a grandchild under 16), 58% of grandmothers and 49% of grandfathers had given some care to a grandchild aged 15 or younger in the previous 12 months, from just above 50% of grandmothers in Spain, Italy and Switzerland to 65% or more in Denmark and the Netherlands. Among grandparents who gave any care, regular care (almost weekly or more often) was given by roughly 40% in Greece, Italy and Spain against roughly 20% in the Scandinavian countries.

2649.content: From manufacturers' design documents (PAR Sheets) for slot machine games in use in Ontario, Canada, obtained under freedom of information law, the authors show that virtual reel mapping clusters blanks around the top-paying symbol so that, in Double Diamond Deluxe, the player sees it just above or below the payline five times as often as on it. Ontario approved several versions of the same game that differ in payback: in Lucky Larry's Lobstermania a player betting 1 dollar a spin loses on average 3.8 cents on the 96.2% version and 15 cents on the 85% version, about four times as much, so the same bankroll buys about four times less play.

In the same design documents, a player of Lucky Larry's Lobstermania betting on all 15 lines wins something on 33.52% of spins, and on 60.73% of these wins the amount paid is less than the amount staked, while the machine's lights and sounds signal a win. The authors count these as another form of near miss.

2650.content: Abstract only. Livingstone and Woolley argue that electronic gaming machines in Australian clubs and hotels generate billions of dollars a year and most of Australia's gambling expenditure, that these revenues arguably rely on unsafe consumption by regular players, and that the model of the 'problem' gambler as an individual flawed consumer keeps the current arrangements in place; they hold that the marketing and distribution of the machines is neither accidental nor something the individual is responsible for.

2651.content: Abstract only. A systematic review of studies reporting the sleep duration of children aged 5 to 18 gathered data on 690,747 children from 20 countries, measured from 1905 to 2008. Pseudodata generated from summary statistics were combined with raw data and sleep duration regressed on year (641 regressions by age, sex, day type and country). The sample-weighted median change was minus 0.75 minutes a night per year, a fall of more than an hour per night over the period. Changes were negative across age, sex and day type, but varied by region: decreases in Europe, the USA, Canada and Asia, increases in Australia, the UK and Scandinavia.

2652.content: In three nationally representative UK time-use surveys (1974-75, 2000-01 and 2014-15; 7958 diary days of children aged 8 to 16 living with their parents), children averaged close to 30 minutes a day less in out-of-home or outdoor play in 2015 than in 1975, other things equal, a significantly larger gap than between 1975 and 2000 (17.3 minutes). Total time in out-of-home activities fell by 21 minutes between 1975 and 2015, with the loss concentrated in unstructured play and partly offset by more time in sport.

In the same surveys, children aged 8 to 16 increased their time at home between 1975 and 2015 and spent more time in screen-based activities (22.4 minutes a day more in 2015 than in 1975) and doing homework.

2653.content: The Australian Productivity Commission's 2010 gambling inquiry estimated that about 600,000 Australian adults (4 per cent) played gaming machines at least weekly, that around 15 per cent of these regular players were problem gamblers on the survey measures used, and that problem gamblers accounted for around 40 per cent of all gaming machine spending, the average of estimates ranging from about 20 to 60 per cent.

Working from machine settings, the Productivity Commission calculated that on a one-cent machine played with many lines and maximum credits at the fastest allowed rate (a game about every three seconds), a player could bet up to $12,000 an hour with expected losses of about $1,200 an hour, and often more than $1,500 as game returns are random; the overview states that at high intensity it is easy to lose $1,500 or more in an hour.

The Productivity Commission reports that when the Australian Bureau of Statistics asked people to estimate their own gaming machine losses, the estimates added up to around 3 per cent of the real total, and it notes that machine prices are poorly disclosed and that no receipts are issued.

2654.content: Ramirez and Boli trace state school systems to nineteenth-century Europe and their spread to the whole world in the twentieth century, and argue that mass state schooling grew out of the nation-building of European states competing with one another, until a mass school system became an indispensable part of every modern state.

2655.content: In 24-hour time-use diaries for a US nationally representative sample of 1,712 children aged 0 to 12 (Child Development Supplement of the Panel Study of Income Dynamics, 1997), each weekday hour of television watched without parents present went with less time with parents in other activities: 52 minutes less at ages 0 to 2, 45 at 3 to 5, 15 at 6 to 8 and 23 at 9 to 12. Television watched without siblings went with less time with siblings in the same way.

In the same diaries, each hour of television went with about 9 to 11 per cent less creative play (board games, pretend play, arts and crafts) at ages 0 to 5, and on weekends at all ages, and with a few minutes less homework at ages 6 to 12; it showed no relation to time spent reading or being read to, and none to active play except a small weekend link at ages 9 to 12.

2656.content: Of 149 teaching staff and 71 directors interviewed in 1996 in child care centres in three communities in or near Silicon Valley, California, over half of the teaching staff (54 per cent) and a third of the directors had left their centre by 2000, and half of the teaching staff who left had left child care altogether. Counting all teaching staff employed in the 92 centres in 1996, the authors report that 76 per cent were no longer at their centre in 2000.

2657.content: In an online survey of 382 self-selected video game players asked which structural features of games mattered to them (sound, graphics, setting, game length, rate of play, advancement, humour, controls, winning and losing, character development, brand, multiplayer), the main overall finding was the importance of realism in sound, graphics and setting; a rapid absorption rate, character development, customisation and multiplayer features were also rated important, with many differences between men and women.

2658.content: In the National Comorbidity Survey Adolescent Supplement, a face-to-face survey of 10,123 US adolescents aged 13 to 18, 46.7 per cent of adolescents described themselves as shy and parents described 62.4 per cent as shy, while 8.6 per cent met the interview's DSM-IV criteria for lifetime social phobia; among those who described themselves as shy, 12.4 per cent met those criteria. Those who met the criteria reported more impairment at school or work, in family relationships and in social life than the shy.

In the same survey, use of prescribed medication was low in every group and did not differ between groups: 2.3 per cent of adolescents who met the social phobia criteria and 0.9 per cent of the shy reported using any paroxetine, rates no different from adolescents without either label, and nearly 80 per cent of those who met the criteria had not sought or obtained professional treatment.

2659.content: In the LABILE trial, a UK multicentre double-blind randomised trial, 276 adults who met diagnostic criteria for borderline personality disorder were given up to 400 mg a day of lamotrigine or an inert placebo. At 52 weeks (195 followed up, 70.6 per cent) the mean ZAN-BPD score was 11.3 on lamotrigine and 11.5 on placebo (adjusted difference 0.1, 95% CI -1.8 to 2.0), and the authors report no difference in depressive symptoms, self-harm, social functioning or quality of life, and similar costs.

2660.content: In the US Early Childhood Longitudinal Study, Kindergarten cohort (11,784 children who entered kindergarten in 1998 to 1999 in states with a statewide entry cutoff), parents reported an ADHD diagnosis by 2007 for 8.4 per cent of children born in the month before their state's cutoff, who usually become the youngest in their grade, against 5.1 per cent of those born in the month after. By regression discontinuity, one more year of age at school entry lowered the chance of a reported diagnosis by 5.4 percentage points against a 6.4 per cent baseline, and lowered regular stimulant use in eighth grade by 4.4 points.

Elder reports that a child's birth date relative to the school-entry cutoff moved teachers' ratings of hyperactivity and inattention about four times as much as parents' ratings of the same behaviour, and estimates that if the age gap reflects wrong diagnoses only, roughly 20 per cent of the 2.5 million US children then using stimulants for ADHD had been misdiagnosed.

2661.content: Pooling individual patient data from six placebo-controlled trials (718 adult outpatients diagnosed with major or minor depressive disorder; paroxetine or imipramine for 6 to 11 weeks), the authors found that the drug-placebo difference grew with the baseline Hamilton score: below a score of 23 the difference was small (Cohen's d under 0.20), it reached the NICE threshold of a 3-point difference only at a baseline score of 25, and d of 0.50 at 27.

2662.content: In 38 US television prescription drug adverts recorded over four weeks in 2004 during prime time and evening news on the four largest networks (weighted by how often each aired), 95 per cent used emotional appeals, about a quarter described where the condition comes from (26 per cent) or risk factors (26 per cent), none mentioned lifestyle change as an alternative to the product, 18 per cent portrayed lifestyle change as insufficient, 58 per cent framed the condition as a loss of control, 85 per cent showed control regained with the product and 78 per cent showed social approval following product use.

2663.content: Pooling 31 randomised trials (4,410 participants with diagnosed depressive disorders who had responded to antidepressant treatment), the authors report that people kept on the antidepressant relapsed on the trials' criteria at an average rate of 18 per cent against 41 per cent of those switched to placebo, a 70 per cent reduction in the odds of relapse; most trials lasted 12 months.

2664.content: Of 408 Dutch patients whose doctor had ordered tapering strips (daily pouches with slowly falling doses) for an antidepressant between 2015 and 2019 and who answered a questionnaire in January 2020 (483 of 1,012 responded), mostly for venlafaxine or paroxetine after a median 4 years of use and with 61 per cent having tried to stop before without strips, 270 (66 per cent) reported being still off the antidepressant 1 to 5 years later and 6 (2 per cent) on a lower dose; 87 (21 per cent) reported restarting after a self-reported relapse and 35 (9 per cent) restarting for another reason.

2665.content: In the Chicago Follow-up Study, 145 patients, 64 of them diagnosed with schizophrenia, were assessed at index hospitalisation and followed up five times over 15 years; at each follow-up a larger share of those diagnosed with schizophrenia who were not taking antipsychotics showed periods of recovery and better global functioning than those taking them (p < .001). The authors tie the better course to the patients' own characteristics: better premorbid achievements, personality and attitudes, less vulnerability and more resilience.

2666.content: A meta-analysis of 40 double-blind discontinuation trials (8,890 patients diagnosed with major depressive disorder who had remitted on an antidepressant and were then randomised to keep the same drug or switch to placebo) found that 20.9 percent of those who stayed on the drug and 39.7 percent of those switched to placebo met their trial's relapse criteria by the study endpoint (pooled odds ratio 0.38; number needed to treat 6). All-cause dropout was 43 percent on the drug and 58 percent on placebo; dropout for side effects was about 4 percent in both arms. The authors state that withdrawal reactions could not be assessed, since relapse and dropout in the first 4 to 8 weeks after the switch were not available.

In the same meta-analysis, the gap between drug and placebo arms was about the same whether the trial ran 6 months (19.6 against 37.6 percent) or more than a year (19.9 against 39.8 percent), and relapse in the placebo arm rose by only about 2 percentage points from 6 months to a year; the authors read this as most relapses after stopping falling within the first 6 months. In three adolescent trials (164 patients) relapse was 66.7 percent on placebo and 41.0 percent on the drug.

2667.content: A systematic scoping review screened 12,267 records and included 334 studies (1979 to 2020) of children and adolescents, sorted by a five-question framework for overdiagnosis. 104 studies showed a large pool of children who could be diagnosed with ADHD, 45 showed that ADHD diagnoses had risen, 25 that the added cases tended to have milder symptoms, and 83 that drug treatment for ADHD was rising. The authors conclude that ADHD, as diagnosed, is overdiagnosed and overtreated in children and adolescents.

Of the 151 studies in the same review that reported outcomes of diagnosis or drug treatment, only 5 looked at the added, milder cases. Two compared children given the ADHD label with undiagnosed children with similar behaviour and reported social, psychological and academic harm from the label; two found a much larger drug response in children with more severe symptoms and less benefit in milder ones. The authors read these as a pattern of diminishing returns in which harms may outweigh benefits for children with milder symptoms.

2668.content: Abstract only. In a review, the authors label as secondary psychoses the psychotic presentations that come with a known medical illness or substance use. They state that four features point a clinician to such a cause: an atypical presentation, onset in step with a detectable medical cause, evidence that the agent acts directly on the body, and no primary psychotic illness that explains the picture better. They write about three examples: psychosis with temporal lobe epilepsy, with velocardiofacial syndrome (the 22q11.2 deletion), and with NMDA receptor encephalitis.

2669.content: Abstract only. In a retrospective review at the authors' tertiary centre (Sheffield, England) of people with a first episode of psychosis and no neurological signs, 3 of 112 who had an MRI (2.7 percent) had a brain lesion the authors judged potentially accountable for the psychosis (a brain tumour and HIV encephalopathy), and 3 of 204 who had a CT (1.5 percent) had a focal lesion (primary or secondary tumours). The authors report that incidental findings unrelated to the psychosis were common: 62.5 percent on MRI and 65.2 percent on CT. The authors conclude that routine brain imaging is unlikely to change management in such patients.

2670.content: Abstract only. In a double-blind trial, healthy volunteers took paroxetine 20 mg a day (26) or placebo (25) for 4 weeks. Against placebo, paroxetine lowered measures of hostility through a general fall in negative affect, left measures of positive affect unchanged, and raised a behavioural index of social affiliation. The fall in negative affect and the rise in affiliation went with plasma drug levels at the end of the trial.

2671.content: Abstract only. In a descriptive review based on a literature search (about 60,000 references on benzodiazepines), Lader reports that cognitive and psychomotor impairment, dependence and abuse remained serious problems after 50 years of prescribing, that use stayed high despite warnings and guidelines, and that the benefit outweighs the risk in most patients only for the short term of 2 to 4 weeks. Beyond that the balance is unestablished; the main reason he gives is that short-term use is hard to stop from becoming indefinite, with the risk of dependence. He separates low-dose dependence that arises from prescribing from high-dose abuse.

2672.content: Leo and Lacasse collected media reports that described depression, the authors' term, as a chemical imbalance, and asked the reporters for the evidence behind the statement. Several gave no citation; others pointed to papers on serotonin research. The authors report that none of the sources offered, which came from psychiatrists, patients and a major drug company, was direct evidence of a chemical imbalance, and that several of them said outright that the serotonin imbalance theory was known to be incorrect.

2673.content: In a Lancet seminar, the authors, four autism specialists, state that there are no reliable biomarkers, so an autism spectrum disorder diagnosis must be made on the basis of behaviour. They describe the standard tools as observation schedules and interviews: the STAT, a 20-minute observation of young children, and the ADOS, a 45-minute observation by a trained professional, with a developmental interview of the caregiver; they report that diagnoses combining clinician observation and caregiver report are more reliable than either alone.

2674.content: Abstract only. In the MTA trial, 579 children aged 7 to 9.9 diagnosed with ADHD combined type were randomised to 14 months of medication management (dose titration, then monthly visits), intensive behavioural treatment (parent, school and child components), both combined, or community care. All four groups improved. For most rated ADHD symptoms the medication and combined groups improved more than the behavioural and community-care groups; combined and medication alone did not differ on core symptoms, and the combined arm did better than behavioural treatment or community care on some other outcomes. Two thirds of the community-care children also received medication during the study.

2675.content: Abstract only. A review of case reports, case studies and case series on brain tumours with psychiatric symptoms (1956 to 2014) reports that, infrequently, psychiatric symptoms are the only sign of a brain tumour: mood symptoms, psychosis, memory problems, personality change, anxiety or loss of appetite. The authors list as reasons for brain imaging: a first psychosis, new mood or memory symptoms, new or atypical symptoms, personality change, and appetite loss without concern about body shape.

2676.content: In all dispensed prescriptions in England linked to patients (NHS Business Services Authority data), 11.53 million adults (26.3 percent of adult residents) had a prescription dispensed for at least one of five drug classes between April 2017 and March 2018. The authors report that antidepressants were the largest class: 7.26 million adults, 16.6 percent of adult residents. They report that the number with an antidepressant rose 6.7 percent from 6.80 million in the year from April 2015.

In the same data, women were more often dispensed each drug class than men; the authors report 21.3 percent of women against 11.6 percent of men for antidepressants, the largest ratio of the five classes (1.8 times). They report that antidepressant dispensing rose with the deprivation of the practice area, from 14.5 percent of adults in the least deprived fifth to 16.8 percent in the most deprived (adjusted rate ratios 1.10 to 1.24 against the least deprived fifth). They report that in March 2018, 2.34 million antidepressant patients (52.1 percent) had been dispensed the drug continuously for at least 12 months.

2677.content: Abstract only. In four experiments, priming a mating goal raised men's stated willingness to spend on conspicuous luxuries and left spending on basic necessities unchanged; in women it raised public helping and left private helping unchanged. Men primed this way helped more only where the help could show heroism or dominance.

2678.content: A meta-analysis of 43 published effects of mating primes on decisions (3,252 participants; 42 of 43 reported as significant, pooled d = 0.57) showed a funnel plot pattern pointing to publication bias or p-hacking. Eight new studies with over 1,600 participants, one fully preregistered, found no effect of mating primes on spending on conspicuous goods, risk-taking or loss aversion (pooled d = 0.00). The authors infer that the true effect for the published studies is very close to zero.

2679.content: Abstract only. In 28 male volunteers whose serum testosterone was measured daily during abstinence after ejaculation, levels changed little from day 2 to day 5; on day 7 they peaked at 145.7 percent of baseline, and after the peak no regular fluctuation followed. The author reports that without ejaculation the 7-day pattern did not appear.

2680.content: Abstract only. Fifty-six women and men watched the same explicit heterosexual film daily for 4 days and then a new film: either the same actors in different sexual acts, or different actors in the same acts. Self-rated negative feeling rose as the film was repeated and returned to its first level with the new film. Men reported more arousal with new actors; women reported more arousal with the same actors in new acts.

2681.content: Abstract only. In 84 speed-dating events (1,868 women and 1,870 men), multilevel models of the dating decisions showed that when more partners were on offer, choosers gave less weight to traits that take time to find out and judge, such as occupation and education, and more weight to traits seen at once, such as height and weight.

2682.content: Abstract only. Across the same 84 speed-dating events, choosers made fewer proposals (said yes to fewer dates) at events where the people on offer varied more in age, height, occupation and education, most of all when the event was large. At more varied events, participants were less likely to choose the partner most others chose and more likely to choose no one at all.

2683.content: Two studies. In Study 1, jealousy was provoked by one of three experimental conditions and time spent searching a simulated Facebook page was recorded: more jealousy went with more search time for women and less for men. In Study 2, a daily-diary study of couples, on days when women (and not men) reported more jealousy they spent more time watching their partner's Facebook activity, and anxious attachment accounted for part of this link.

2684.content: A combined analysis of the six fMRI studies of love published by 2010 (120 participants, 99 women and 21 men; three studies of passionate love with 70 participants, two of mothers viewing their own child, one of unconditional love for people with intellectual disabilities). All six studies found activity in subcortical dopamine-rich reward areas while people viewed or read the name of a loved person. Passionate love also recruited cortical areas for emotion, motivation, social cognition, attention and self-representation, and the different kinds of love involved partly distinct networks.

In the same review: in Bartels and Zeki's fMRI study of 20 mothers viewing photos of their own child, and in Noriuchi and colleagues' study of 13 mothers viewing videos of their own infant, mothers showed activity in the periaqueductal grey, which was not seen in the studies of passionate love. Both maternal studies also showed activity in the insula and the putamen, and Bartels and Zeki's study also in the anterior cingulate and the caudate, overlapping with passionate love.

2685.content: A meta-analysis of sex differences in 30 reported sexual behaviours and attitudes, across 834 samples published 1993 to 2007 and 7 large national data sets. Men reported slightly more sexual experience and more permissive attitudes than women on most variables, and most differences were small. The exceptions, with medium effect sizes, were reported masturbation, pornography use, casual sex and attitudes toward casual sex, all higher in men. Differences were smaller in nations and ethnic groups with more gender equity and in older samples for some behaviours.

2686.content: A meta-analysis of 126 published studies over 50 years with over 72,000 people (samples from 11 countries, mostly the US) found that greater marital quality went with better physical health, with mean effect sizes from r = .07 to .21. Greater marital quality went with lower cardiovascular reactivity during marital conflict (r = minus .13) and showed no link with daily cortisol slopes or cortisol reactivity during conflict. The authors call the effects small, similar in size to links between health behaviours such as diet and health outcomes.

In the same meta-analysis, seven longitudinal studies linked greater marital quality with lower risk of early death (r = .11). After two studies that mixed death with other heart events were removed, the link was r = .19. Longitudinal studies overall showed consistent effects, which the authors read as a sign that poor marital quality is a risk factor for poor health.

2687.content: The review reports that fMRI studies show men and women activate largely the same regions when viewing sexual images (thalamus, amygdala, prefrontal and cingulate cortex, insula, ventral striatum). In two studies by different groups (Karama et al. 2002, Hamann et al. 2004) only men showed hypothalamic activation, which tracked men's reported arousal, and men showed more amygdala activation. When context was removed and only genitals were shown (Ponseti et al. 2006), men and women did not differ, and in both the reward areas responded most to the preferred sex. The authors conclude the sexes share the neural pathways and differ in which stimuli and strategies activate them.

The review reports that in men genital and subjective arousal are specific to the sex they are attracted to (Chivers et al. 2004), while women's genital arousal did not differ by the sex of the actors and rose even to bonobos mating (Chivers and Bailey 2005). Women's reported arousal often does not match their genital response. Repeated viewing of the same sexual slides produced habituation in men; findings in women were inconsistent, and in one study 85 percent of women said they turned to the context and nonsexual details as trials repeated.

2688.content: Four studies on mate poaching, meaning attracting someone who is already in a relationship. In Study 1 (236 people) attempts at poaching were relatively common and went with distinct personality traits. In Study 2 (220) the perceived costs and benefits of poaching differed somewhat between men and women and by whether a short-term or long-term outcome was sought. In Study 3 (453) the rated effectiveness of poaching tactics fitted five evolution-based hypotheses, and in Study 4 (333) effectiveness depended on the kind of relationship targeted (marital, dating, long distance, highly committed, just beginning or about to end).

2689.content: Sternberg's Triangular Love Scale (intimacy, passion, commitment) was given to more than 11,000 people in 25 countries on all inhabited continents, and after exclusions 7,332 were analysed. Configural, metric and scalar invariance held across countries, which the authors read as the structure of love the scale measures being the same across cultures. Levels of the three components differed with relationship duration, in line with the theory.

2690.content: A review and meta-analysis of functional neuroimaging studies of sexual arousal in healthy people, mostly watching visual sexual stimuli against control stimuli. In heterosexual men, regions consistently active across studies included the occipitotemporal, inferotemporal, parietal, orbitofrontal, medial prefrontal, insular, anterior cingulate and premotor cortices, and below the cortex the amygdalas, claustrum, hypothalamus, caudate, thalami, cerebellum and substantia nigra. Heterosexual and gay men showed a similar pattern. Visual sexual stimuli activated the amygdalas and thalami more in men than in women. Ejaculation went with decreased activation throughout the prefrontal cortex.

2691.content: In three experiments, desire to spend on showy, status-linked goods came from men following a lower-investment mating strategy and was set off by short-term mating motives, and not by long-term ones. In a fourth experiment women read men who spent conspicuously as interested in short-term mating, and conspicuous purchasing made a man more desirable as a short-term mate and not as a long-term one.

2692.content: Animal evidence. In male prairie voles (Microtus ochrogaster), a monogamous rodent in which both parents care for the young, mating was followed quickly by a preference for the partner and by aggression toward strangers. Experiments on central arginine-vasopressin showed it was both necessary and sufficient for the development of this selective aggression and partner preference.

2693.content: Animal evidence. In house mice (Mus musculus), virgin males usually attack pups while virgin females, mothers and fathers care for them. A subset of galanin-expressing neurons in the medial preoptic area was active during parenting in both sexes. Killing these neurons impaired parenting in males and females: 3 weeks after mating only 14.3 percent of males with more than half of these cells lost (n = 14) were paternal, against 75 percent of littermate controls (n = 12). Virgin females with most of these cells lost stopped caring for pups and began attacking them, and most mothers with heavy loss failed to retrieve their pups.

In the same study, switching on the medial preoptic galanin neurons with light (optogenetics) in virgin male mice stopped attacks on pups in 16 of 18 trials, while the same males attacked in 18 of 19 trials without stimulation, and the stimulated males groomed the pups. Stimulation also reduced aggression toward other males and left mating unaffected.

2694.content: In a cohort of 784 older residents in Japan (mean age 73), feeling useful was asked at baseline and deaths were followed for 6 years. Feeling useful went with better self-rated health and with lower later mortality in the longitudinal analyses.

2695.content: A systematic review of 17 studies (2001 to 2020) found high allostatic load, a composite of stress-related physiological dysregulation, went with higher all-cause mortality in all 17 (hazard ratios 1.08 to 2.75) and with higher cardiovascular mortality in 6 of 8. Pooled, high allostatic load went with 22 percent higher all-cause mortality (HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.14 to 1.30, 10 studies) and 31 percent higher cardiovascular mortality (HR 1.31, 95% CI 1.10 to 1.57, 6 studies). Heterogeneity was high (I squared above 90 percent), and older adults were oversampled.

2696.content: A meta-analysis of 70 studies on purpose in life in middle and old age found a small decline in purpose with age, steeper in the oldest groups. Purpose in life showed a strong association with social integration, and with the quality of relationships in particular. Higher purpose also went with better health, higher everyday competence, higher socioeconomic status, being employed and being married. The author concludes that sources that decline little with age, such as social integration, counteract steep falls in purpose in old age.

2697.content: A meta-analysis of 1,381 mortality risk estimates from 124 studies (1955 to 2007, 22 countries, more than 500 million people) found that, in studies adjusted for age and other covariates, people who had lost a spouse had a 22 percent higher risk of death than married people. The excess was larger for men (27 percent) than for women (15 percent), largest at younger ages, and gone by age 90 for both sexes. The excess was similar across world regions.

In the same meta-analysis, the excess risk of death after losing a spouse was highest early: 58 percent in studies with 6 months of follow-up, 33 percent with 1 year and 51 percent with 2 years, and lower with longer follow-up. Comparing earlier and more recent studies, the authors found that the excess risk has slowly increased over time, and they offer the changing place of marriage in people's networks of ties as one possible reason.

2698.content: In four fMRI studies (114 people in all), a brain pattern trained on heat pain told painful heat from warmth, pain anticipation and pain recall with 94 percent or higher sensitivity and specificity. In study 3, 40 people who had recently gone through an unwanted romantic breakup viewed photos of the ex-partner: the pain pattern told physical pain from this social pain with 85 percent sensitivity and 73 percent specificity, and 95 percent in a forced choice, and did not tell the ex-partner from a friend at better than chance, although both kinds of pain activated overlapping regions and were rated similarly unpleasant.

2699.content: In 2,868 seventeen-year-old twins from the Twins Early Development Study (England and Wales), sensitivity to the environment was measured with the Highly Sensitive Child questionnaire, a self-report scale. A classic twin model put the heritability of the total sensitivity score at 0.47 (95% CI 0.30 to 0.53), with no evidence of shared family environment; the remaining 0.53 was non-shared environment, which includes measurement error.

In the same twin sample, the genes behind sensitivity were partly shared and partly separate across three parts of the scale: ease of excitation and low sensory threshold (reactivity to unpleasant input) carried genetic influence largely distinct from aesthetic sensitivity (response to positive features of surroundings). Of the heritability of sensitivity, about 80 percent was shared with the genes behind neuroticism and, to a lesser extent, extraversion, and about 20 percent was specific to sensitivity.

2700.content: In studies of consumers, a bad mood went with buying and consuming more unplanned treats for oneself. The authors report that this retail therapy had lasting positive effects on mood and that the unplanned purchases made to repair a bad mood were not followed by regret or guilt. The abstract gives no sample sizes, no designs and no time span for 'lasting'.

2701.content: A review with a meta-analysis of 22 randomized experiments that changed children's or adults' environment for the better and also typed a gene variant (gene by environment experiments) found that the interventions worked much more strongly in carriers of the variants usually called risk genotypes than in non-carriers. The authors read this as support for differential susceptibility: the same variants that go with worse outcomes in bad conditions mark the people who gain most when conditions improve.

2702.content: In a laboratory experiment at a Dutch technical university (38 of 49 participants analysed), people played a cooperative game with a small iCat robot whose intelligence and agreeableness were varied, then were told to switch it off by turning a dial, having been told this would erase its memory and personality. The robot begged to stay on. Every participant switched it off, but they hesitated almost three times as long with an intelligent and agreeable robot (34.5 seconds) as with an unintelligent and unagreeable one (11.8 seconds); both intelligence and agreeableness had significant effects on hesitation.

2703.content: In a randomized laboratory experiment with 85 people (mostly German university students, mean age 22.7) who had talked with a small humanoid Nao robot for about ten minutes, the robot either stayed silent or protested when the participant was given the choice to switch it off ('No! Please do not switch me off! I am scared that it will not brighten up again!'). With the protest, 13 of 43 participants left it on (30.2 percent), against 1 of 42 without it (2.4 percent). Those who did switch off a protesting robot waited longer (mean 10.0 against 4.7 seconds). Asked why, eight of the 14 who left it on said they felt sorry for the robot because of its fear, and six said they did not want to act against its will.

2704.content: In experiments in which happy or sad moods were induced by hypnotic suggestion, people recalled more of the word lists, diary-recorded experiences and childhood experiences that matched the mood they were in at recall, and mood shaped free associations, fantasies, social perceptions and snap judgements of others. When a story's feeling-tone matched the reader's mood, its events were more salient and memorable: sad readers attended more to sad material, identified with a sad character and recalled more about that character. Bower proposes that an emotion works as a unit in an associative memory network.

2705.content: In two fMRI studies in humans, activity in the substantia nigra and ventral tegmental area (the midbrain region that holds the dopamine neurons) responded to new pictures as such, and not to other forms of salience such as rarity, negative emotional content or familiar pictures that were task targets; the hippocampus was less selective. The midbrain response scaled with absolute novelty, not novelty relative to the context, and novelty also improved learning of familiar items shown in the same context.

2706.content: Eighty 24-month-old children were observed in four mildly threatening situations, and their fear behaviours were compared with cortisol (reactive and basal) and resting heart measures taken a week later. Only freezing in the less threatening situation went with higher reactive and basal cortisol and with the resting pre-ejection period, a measure of sympathetic activity of the heart; fear behaviours in the more threatening situations did not. The authors call freezing that does not fit the context a dysregulated fear response.

2707.content: A review reports that extensive research in animals implicates stress hormones and the amygdala as interacting modulators of memory consolidation for emotional events, with the amygdala influencing storage in other regions (hippocampus, striatum, neocortex) and not storing the memories itself, and that studies in humans confirm the amygdala's part in the stronger declarative memory for emotionally arousing events.

2708.content: A review of recent empirical work proposes five revisions to the hedonic treadmill model, which held that people adapt back to neutral after good and bad events: set points are not neutral; people differ in set points partly by temperament; one person can have several set points (pleasant feelings, unpleasant feelings and life satisfaction can move in different directions); well-being set points can change under some conditions; and people differ in adaptation, some changing their set point after an event and others not.

2709.content: In two studies of classmates and long-term acquaintances, romantic evaluations of opposite-sex people were more unique to the person judging than shared across judges: relationship variance generally exceeded target variance, more so for expected relationship quality than for attractiveness or resources. Agreement about who was desirable fell as classmates got to know one another over a semester, and among long-term acquaintances ratings were largely unique to each pair.

2710.content: The authors define mattering as the extent to which a person makes a difference to others, in three parts: others attend to them (awareness), invest in them (importance) or look to them for resources (reliance). They built a mattering index, tested its structure with confirmatory factor analysis, and found it distinct from self-consciousness, self-esteem, self-monitoring, alienation and perceived social support.

2711.content: Using a new method (the singleton density score) on 3,195 genomes of the UK10K project, the authors inferred changes in allele frequency in the ancestors of modern Britons over roughly the last 2,000 to 3,000 years. The strongest signals of selection were at the lactase gene (lactose tolerance in adults), whose selection very likely continued into the last 2,000 years, at the major histocompatibility complex (immune genes), and in favour of variants for blond hair and blue eyes.

The same paper reported that alleles raising height had risen in frequency over the past 2,000 to 3,000 years across most of the genome, and signals for other complex traits (larger infant head circumference and birth weight, larger female hip size, later sexual maturation in women). The authors say the role of population structure in these polygenic signals remained to be fully determined.

2712.content: Repeating earlier tests for selection on height with effect sizes from the UK Biobank (336,474 unrelated people of British ancestry) in place of the GIANT consortium meta-analysis, the authors found the signals of polygenic adaptation severely attenuated and in some cases no longer significant, including the singleton-density test of Field et al 2016 in Britain, where a small signal remained only for genome-wide significant variants. Signals built from large numbers of variants below genome-wide significance were extremely sensitive to uncorrected population stratification.

2713.content: Frisch and McArthur report that weight loss stops menstrual cycles and weight gain restores them, and propose a minimum weight for height, read from an index of fatness in normal girls at first menstruation and at age 18, for the onset or return of cycles in women whose cycles had stopped from undernutrition. Patients aged 16 and over resumed cycles at a heavier weight for height than is found at first menstruation. They conclude that a minimum store of easily mobilized energy is needed for ovulation and menstrual cycles.

2714.content: A preregistered replication run in 23 laboratories (2,141 participants, mostly undergraduates) tested the ego-depletion effect with one shared protocol: a first task that did or did not demand self-control (crossing out the letter e under a rule that made the task harder or not), then a multi-source interference task. The depletion group did barely worse on the second task: d = 0.04 for reaction time variability and d = 0.04 for reaction time, both with 95 percent confidence intervals that included zero. Only three of the 23 labs found an effect on reaction time variability whose interval excluded zero, and one of those went the wrong way. The original study the protocol came from had reported d = 0.69, and a 2010 meta-analysis d = 0.62. Participants did rate the harder first task as more effortful.

2715.content: A second preregistered multisite test, run in 36 laboratories with 3,531 people and designed with experts in depletion research, let each lab use one of two depletion protocols (a writing task or an e-crossing task) and then measured self-control on a later task. Confirmatory tests found no significant effect (d = 0.06), and Bayesian analyses found the data 4 times more likely under no effect than under the expected effect. With the 30 percent of participants removed by the preregistered rules put back, a small significant effect appeared (d = 0.08). The depletion tasks were rated as more effortful.

2716.content: Twenty-six healthy adults aged 18 to 26 were scanned with fMRI while deciding whether to buy real products with 20 dollars of their own to spend (one trial counted for real). Activation of the nucleus accumbens rose with how much a person wanted the product as soon as the product appeared, before the price; a price higher than the person would pay deactivated the mesial prefrontal cortex, and the insula was active when the person then declined. Activity in each region forecast the purchase decision that followed, over and above the person's own ratings, and in cross-validation brain activity alone sorted purchases at 60 percent against a chance rate of 50.

2717.content: In six experiments, participants chose freely between two options that differed only in how much cognitive control they demanded (for example, two decks of cards where one required frequent switching between tasks). In experiment 1, 43 adults chose the low-demand deck on 68 percent of 500 trials on average, and 36 of them (84 percent) chose it more often than the high-demand deck, although they believed the session would last a fixed hour whatever they chose. The bias held when error rates, time on task and awareness of the difference were accounted for, shrank when task incentives were added, and was stronger in people who found switching harder.

2718.content: Abstract only. In a review, Kuhl reports that infants detect statistical and prosodic patterns in the speech they hear and use them to discover phonemes and words, that social interaction with another human being affects speech learning in a way she compares to song learning in songbirds, and proposes that the brain's early commitment to the patterns heard in infancy may explain why infants learn language better than adults.

2719.content: In a review, Kuhl reports that infants can at first tell apart the speech sounds of all languages and that between 6 and 12 months this changes to a pattern specific to the language they hear: discrimination of foreign contrasts falls while discrimination of native contrasts rises (Japanese infants' discrimination of English r and l declines between 8 and 10 months while American infants' rises). She reports wide agreement across second-language studies that learning ability falls with the age at first exposure: a new language can be learned at any age, but after puberty pronunciation and grammar rarely reach native level, while word learning stays good throughout life. The windows differ by level: phonetic learning before the end of the first year, syntax between 18 and 36 months.

2720.content: Abstract only. Eight healthy men had two PET scans with [11C]raclopride, one after placebo and one after oral d-amphetamine (0.30 mg per kg). Amphetamine lowered raclopride binding, a sign of dopamine release, in the ventral striatum and not in the dorsal striatum. The size of that change went with how much the men said they wanted the drug (r = 0.83) and with their score on the novelty seeking and exploratory excitability scale (r = 0.79). The change in dopamine did not go with mood. The authors read mesolimbic dopamine as tied to interest in obtaining a reward more than to the reward itself.

2721.content: Abstract only. Twenty-nine regularly menstruating, sedentary young women of normal body composition were held for 5 days in the early follicular phase at an energy availability (diet intake minus exercise expenditure) of 45 and of 10, 20 or 30 kcal per kg of lean body mass per day, in two randomised trials at least 2 months apart, while they exercised under supervision. Luteinizing hormone pulses were unchanged at 30 kcal per kg, but below that level pulse frequency fell and pulse amplitude rose, and the disruption was greater in women with short luteal phases. The authors conclude that the reproductive pulse is disrupted only below a threshold of energy availability, deep in negative energy balance.

2722.content: Abstract only. In Pisa, 20 people who had fallen in love within the previous 6 months, 20 unmedicated patients diagnosed with obsessive-compulsive disorder and 20 controls had the serotonin transporter measured as 3H-paroxetine binding to blood platelets. The density of binding sites was significantly lower in the people newly in love and in the diagnosed patients than in the controls, and the two groups did not differ from each other. The authors read this as a shared change in the serotonin system, perhaps tied to the overvalued ideas both states share.

2723.content: Abstract only. The same Pisa group compared 24 people of both sexes who had fallen in love within the previous 6 months with 24 people who were single or in a long relationship. Cortisol was higher in the people newly in love; men in love had lower FSH and testosterone, and women in love higher testosterone; estradiol, progesterone, DHEAS and androstenedione did not differ. All the hormonal differences were gone when the same people were re-tested 12 to 24 months later.

2724.content: University of Miami undergraduates who had been harmed by someone they knew within the past week (356 enrolled, 337 analysed) reported, over 21 days, their wish for revenge on and avoidance of that person, and about 25 days after enrolment gave a speech in the laboratory into a video camera as if speaking to the person, after which their anger was measured by their own ratings, by anger words in the speech and by raters coding their faces. The more apologies, offers of compensation and other conciliatory gestures they had received, the more they came to see the person as valuable to them and the less as likely to harm them again; through these two judgments, conciliatory gestures went with faster forgiveness over the 21 days and with less self-reported anger and fewer anger words in the laboratory.

2725.content: A narrative review of studies of girls who reach puberty earlier than their peers. Across studies, early maturing girls reported more depressive symptoms and more often met the authors' diagnostic criteria for a depressive episode, started smoking and drinking earlier, reported more body dissatisfaction and dieting, dated and had sex earlier, and showed more delinquent behaviour. The authors stress that the effects are modest: in the studies they cite, early maturers had about 1.9 times the risk of depression as the studies measured it and 1.8 times the risk of substance use, and timing accounted for under 2 percent of the variance in eating problems, 4 percent in delinquency and 6 percent in sexual activity. They report that the best replicated account ties depressive symptoms to timing relative to peers, not to pubertal stage itself, and that psychosocial explanations (standing out among same-age peers, friendships with older adolescents, older boyfriends) are the most used and best supported, with effects amplified by stressful life events.

2726.content: Abstract only. A meta-analysis of 713 independent samples from 515 studies found that contact between members of different groups typically went with less prejudice toward the other group. Tests suggested that participant selection and publication bias did not explain the result, and the more rigorous studies gave larger effects. The effect generalised to the whole outgroup and held across many kinds of groups and settings, racial and ethnic or not. Contact under Allport's optimal conditions (equal status, common goals, cooperation, support from authorities) went with larger reductions, but those conditions were not essential.

2727.content: Re-examining contact research, the authors gathered every intergroup contact study that assigned contact at random and measured outcomes at least a day later: 27 studies, nearly two thirds published after Pettigrew and Tropp 2006. In 24 of the 27, contact lowered measured prejudice, and the average effect was 0.39 standard deviations. Studies of ethnic, racial, religious and immigrant prejudice considered on their own gave an estimated effect of 0.25, and contact aimed at ethnic or racial prejudice gave substantially weaker effects. No randomised study of ethnic or racial contact included participants over 25.

2728.content: Abstract only. In two cross-sectional studies and one longitudinal study of consumers, people high in materialism felt more positive emotion about a desired product before buying it and less after buying it; people low in materialism did not show this rise and fall. The rise before purchase appeared to come from high-materialism consumers expecting the product to change their lives in significant ways, and the author suggests that for them wanting and anticipating a product may be more pleasant than owning it.

2729.content: Abstract only. In three experiments, making shopping choices reduced lingering sadness, whether the choices were hypothetical (experiment 1) or real (experiment 2), and all three experiments supported the authors' account that choosing restores a sense of personal control over one's environment. The benefit did not extend to anger (experiments 2 and 3), which the authors tie to anger being about other people rather than about situational forces.

2730.content: In Oxford, 32 people rated how pleasant eight foods tasted, ate one of them for lunch, and rated the eight again 2 and 20 minutes later: pleasantness fell more for the food eaten than for the foods not eaten. In a second experiment 24 people did the same before an unexpected second course; the drop in liking for each food tracked how much of it they then ate (Spearman correlation 0.68 between the change in liking and energy intake in the second course), so people ate less of the food they had just had and more of others.

2731.content: Abstract only. Forty young women chosen for high or low self-ratings of shyness and of sociability had EEG and heart rate recorded for 6 minutes while waiting for an expected meeting with a stranger, and were then watched for 5 minutes during the meeting. Frontal EEG asymmetry went with sociability and not with shyness: women low in sociability had relatively more right mid-frontal activity, women high in sociability more left. Women high in both shyness and sociability had a higher and more stable heart rate than women high in shyness and low in sociability and than women low in shyness and high in sociability. Women low in sociability showed more signs of nonverbal social avoidance. The authors read this as shyness and sociability resting on different physiological systems.

2732.content: Abstract only. In four studies, people whose satisfaction of the three needs named by self-determination theory (autonomy, competence and relatedness) was balanced reported higher well-being than people with the same total but more uneven satisfaction across the three. The result held for several measures of needs and adjustment, was independent of neuroticism, and appeared in concurrent, prospective, daily diary and observer-report designs.

2733.content: Abstract only. A meta-analysis of 101 articles found that adolescents who went through puberty earlier than their peers scored higher on measures of internalizing and externalizing problems and their subdomains (distress, fear, antisocial behavior, substance use, eating problems), in both boys and girls. The associations were small, about Cohen's d 0.20, and sex did not moderate them. How pubertal timing was measured explained part of the spread between studies; sample type and mean age did not.

2734.content: In three laboratory experiments with University of Southampton undergraduates playing a step-level public-goods game (Experiment 1: 120 students, 40 men; Experiment 2: 93, 43 men; Experiment 3: 90, 48 men), men gave more to their group when told their university was being compared with other universities than when told individuals were being compared: 92 against 57 percent of men contributed in Experiment 1, and men gave about 213 against 155 pence (of 300) in Experiment 2 and 235 against 159 in Experiment 3. Women's contributions did not differ between conditions in Experiments 2 and 3, and in Experiment 1 fewer women contributed under group competition (53 against 78 percent). In Experiment 3 men also identified more strongly with their group under group competition; women did not.

2735.content: Abstract only. Eight women whose menstrual cycles had stopped after strenuous exercise or low weight (hypothalamic amenorrhea, with low leptin) were observed for one month and then given recombinant human leptin for up to three months; six similar women received no treatment. Nothing changed in the controls or in the month before treatment. On leptin, luteinizing hormone levels and pulse frequency rose within two weeks, follicles, ovarian volume and estradiol rose over three months, three of the eight women had an ovulatory cycle and two more had follicle development and withdrawal bleeding. Thyroid hormones, IGF-1 and markers of bone formation also rose; cortisol did not.

2736.content: Abstract only. Ten healthy adults in an fMRI scanner saw fearful or happy faces for 33 ms, each followed at once by a neutral face for 167 ms (backward masking); 8 of the 10 reported not having seen the emotional faces. Although subjects reported seeing only neutral faces, the BOLD signal in the amygdala was higher for masked fearful faces than for masked happy faces, with signal rises to fearful faces and falls to happy faces.

2737.content: Abstract only. In five experiments, each on one trait (attractiveness, likeability, trustworthiness, competence, aggressiveness), people judged unfamiliar faces shown for different lengths of time. Judgments made after 100 ms correlated highly with judgments made with no time limit, and longer exposure did not significantly raise these correlations. From 100 to 500 ms judgments became more negative and confidence rose; from 500 to 1,000 ms judgments did not change significantly, with one exception, while confidence rose for some traits.

2738.content: Animal evidence, abstract only. Rats (Rattus norvegicus) trained to press a lever for sucrose pellets, and separately taught that a 30-second light came with free sucrose, were given amphetamine (0, 2, 10 or 20 micrograms) microinjected into the nucleus accumbens shell and tested with no reward available. Amphetamine selectively magnified the burst of lever pressing that the light cue triggered, even though neither sucrose nor the cue followed the presses. In taste-reactivity tests, the same injections did not raise the positive facial reactions to sucrose taste (liking) at doses that raised cue-triggered wanting.

2739.content: A meta-analysis of 30 reports (77 effect sizes, 9,361 children and adolescents under 18) on the serotonin transporter variant 5HTTLPR. Adverse environments went with worse outcomes (behavioural, psychiatric or developmental, as each study measured them) in carriers of a short allele (ss or sl: r 0.22) and hardly at all in ll carriers (r 0.06), a significant difference. Supportive environments went with better outcomes in short-allele carriers (r 0.21) and ll carriers (r 0.11), a difference that was not significant across all samples. In samples more than 80 percent white the difference held both ways: adverse r 0.18 against 0.04, supportive r 0.17 against 0.05 (Q contrast 3.92, p 0.048).

2740.content: In a random-digit-dial telephone survey of 6,654 Ontario adults in 2003, 4.8 percent scored as moderate or severe problem gamblers on the Canadian Problem Gambling Index (3.8 and 1.0 percent). Prospective gambling-expenditure diaries kept by 364 of them, checked against actual provincial revenue, indicated that this 4.8 percent supplied about 36 percent of Ontario gambling revenue (20.1 to 49.2 percent across the confidence interval of the prevalence the authors report), more than seven times their share of the population. The share was about 61 percent for gambling machines, 45 percent for horse racing, 32 percent for casino table games, 22 percent for bingo and raffles and 18 percent for lotteries and instant tickets.

2741.content: Fitting a multilevel overdispersed Poisson model to 'How many X do you know?' answers about 32 groups from 1,370 US adults (the McCarty and colleagues survey), the authors estimate that the median American knows about 610 people (650 for men, 590 for women), with a mean of about 750 and 90 percent of people between about 250 and 1,710. Age, sex, education, work and income together explained only 10 percent of the variation in network size.

2742.content: In a year (2007) of call records from one European mobile operator, covering 3.2 million subscribers with known age and sex, the number of people a person called in a month was highest at about age 25, fell until about 45, held level from 45 to 55 and fell again after 55. Men had more monthly contacts than women before about age 39 and women more than men after. Most people kept monthly phone contact with about 15 people; the mean fell from 15 to 20 contacts in the early phase to 8 to 15 after age 40.

2743.content: In a laboratory market at Penn State (144 students, 48 per market, 30 rounds of a buyer-seller trust game), trading among strangers re-matched every round with no information was the least efficient, trusting and trustworthy; a market showing each seller's shipping history (online-style feedback) did better; and a market where the same pairs traded every round did best. Averaged over all rounds, the feedback market reached 2.8 times the efficiency of the strangers market, and the partners market 1.8 times that of the feedback market. Trust and trustworthiness fell over the rounds among strangers and stayed stable in the other two markets.

2744.content: Across five studies, people who had just talked with someone underestimated how much the other person liked them. In Study 1a, 36 strangers recruited near Yale rated their liking for a five-minute conversation partner at 5.82 on a 7-point scale and guessed the partner's liking for them at 5.17. The gap appeared among 118 members of the public meeting strangers at UK workshops (Study 4), and among 102 Yale first-year students rating their assigned suitemates five times over a year (Study 5), where it held in September, October, December and February and was gone by May.

In Study 1a (36 participants recruited near Yale), shyness moderated the liking gap. The shyest third liked their partner at 6.16 and guessed the partner liked them at 5.02, a gap of 1.14 points on a 7-point scale; the middle third showed a gap of 0.55; the least shy third showed no significant gap (0.25). Scores on scales for rejection sensitivity, self-esteem and narcissism did not moderate the gap.

2745.content: Across eight studies in the United States and Denmark (surveys and behavioural experiments, total N 8,434), people reported the same level of hostility in political discussions online and offline (Study 4, US: 0.17 on both scales), and a person's offline political hostility was strongly correlated with their online political hostility (r 0.84). Status-driven risk taking predicted hostility equally in both settings (beta 0.52 offline, 0.51 online). Hostile people did not select into online over offline discussion, and readers did not over-perceive hostility in online messages.

Bor and Petersen report that online political discussions are perceived as more hostile than offline ones, and offer initial evidence that this is because hostile, status-driven people take part intensively in political debate both online and offline, while online their behaviour is far more visible and reaches more targets.

2746.content: Matching three monthly surveys of 3,649 Facebook users (reporting on 26,134 friends) with the site's server logs, the authors found that composed one-to-one messages received from a friend (comments, messages, wall posts) and reading the friend's posts went with a rise in reported closeness the next month, over and above in-person, phone and other online contact. One-click actions (likes, pokes) did not. The changes were small (about 0.01 to 0.02 points on a 7-point closeness scale per step of activity), and neither directed messages nor reading changed closeness with family members.
