In the same panel, the more a person posted updates to their whole network, the less close they reported feeling to any given friend the next month (about 0.02 points lower per extra status update a month), and the more a friend broadcast, the less close the person felt to that friend (beta -0.03), once one-to-one contact and reading were held equal.

2747.content: Abstract only. After being angered, participants hit a punching bag while thinking about the person who had angered them (rumination), hit it while thinking about becoming physically fit (distraction), or did not hit a bag (control). The rumination group then reported more anger than the distraction and control groups, and gave the loudest noise blasts to the person who had angered them, followed by the distraction group and then the control group. Doing nothing at all lowered anger and aggression more than venting.

2748.content: In an online experiment with 667 US Mechanical Turk workers, a quiz rigged to go badly (negative mood) and a discussion seeded with troll-like comments (negative context) each raised the share of troll-like posts, and together doubled it: 35 percent of posts were troll-like with positive mood and benign context, 47 and 49 percent with one negative condition, and 68 percent with both.

In over 16 million comments on CNN.com, one in four posts flagged for abuse came from users with no earlier flagged post. In sub-discussions, the chance that the fifth post was flagged was 2 percent when none of the first four were flagged, 7 percent with one flagged, and 49 percent with four. Flagging also peaked late at night and early in the work week.

2749.content: In six experiments by one Oxford-led group (five with videos watched in the laboratory, one at live comedy and drama shows at the Edinburgh Fringe), adults' pain thresholds (a frozen wine-cooler sleeve, an inflated blood-pressure cuff, or a wall-sit) were measured before and after the session. Thresholds rose after sessions in which people laughed and did not rise after neutral videos or drama. In experiment 5, an unfunny video chosen to raise positive mood did not raise pain thresholds, and positive mood scores after it did not differ from those after the neutral videos. The authors read the rise as endorphin release triggered by laughter itself.

In experiment 4, 62 adults (21 men, 41 women) were randomly assigned to watch a 15-minute neutral video alone, a comedy video alone, or the comedy video in a group of four. People laughed most in the group comedy condition, less with comedy alone and least with the neutral video. Pain threshold rose more after group comedy than after the neutral video alone (p = 0.043). Comedy watched alone fell in between and did not differ significantly from either the neutral video alone (p = 0.861) or group comedy (p = 0.110). The authors read this as a dose effect: a group raises the amount of laughter, and the pain threshold follows the laughter.

2750.content: Using reciprocated posts to define ties, the authors built ego networks from two Facebook datasets (130,338 and 5,761 active egos, data from 2009) and one Twitter dataset (60,790 egos). Clustering contacts by how often they were contacted gave layers that scale by about three, as offline: in Facebook dataset 1 the cumulative layer sizes averaged 1.68, 5.28, 14.92 and 40.93 people, and in Twitter (five layers) 1.55, 4.52, 11.17, 28.28 and 88.31. Contact rates per layer were close to face-to-face values; in Facebook an alter in the inner layers was contacted at least about every five to twelve days, and at least every six months in the outer one.

All three online datasets showed an innermost layer of about 1.5 people, inside the classic layer of about 5, contacted at very high rates (on average at least once every five days in Facebook and every other day in Twitter). The authors note that this layer had only been hypothesised from offline data.

2751.content: Abstract only. In six experiments, having an activity measured (for example counting steps while walking or pages while reading) made people do more of it and at the same time enjoy it less. The author attributes this to measurement undermining intrinsic motivation: by drawing attention to output, it makes an enjoyable activity feel more like work. Measurement also lowered continued engagement in the activity and subjective well-being.

2752.content: Abstract only. In two studies, people's affection for a television character went with seeing the character as real. In Study 2, participants were passively shown a picture of either their favourite television character or a familiar character they did not favour while doing a well-learned and a new motor task. With the favourite character's picture present they did better on the well-learned task and worse on the new task, the classic pattern people show when another person is in the room (social facilitation); the non-favourite character's picture did not produce this.

2753.content: The authors morphed photographs of 17 infants to make high, unchanged and low baby schema versions (rounder face, higher forehead, bigger eyes, smaller nose and mouth, or the reverse, within 2 standard deviations of real infants). 122 Drexel University undergraduates took part; after exclusions 62 rated cuteness and 44 rated how much they would like to take care of each infant. High baby schema faces were rated cuter (F = 137.3, p < 0.001) and drew more wish to take care than unchanged and low baby schema faces. Women, and not men, also gave higher care ratings to high than to unchanged faces.

2754.content: Abstract only. Saliva testosterone was measured in 20 young healthy men before, during and after five films chosen to be erotic, sexual, aggressive, stressful (dental surgery) or neutral. Testosterone rose 15 minutes after the start of the erotic and the sexual films and fell during the dental surgery film; the neutral and aggressive films changed nothing. No film left testosterone different after the showing from before it.

2755.content: Abstract only. In a field experiment participants reconnected with an old friend by phone or by e-mail, and in laboratory experiments strangers chatted by video, voice or text. Contact that included voice (phone, video chat, voice chat) produced stronger feelings of connection than text (e-mail, text chat) and was no more awkward. People's expectations about awkwardness and connection were miscalibrated, and this could lead them to prefer text.

2756.content: In Study 1, 613 US ninth graders (mean age 14.3) took part in a three-minute simulated social media session with eleven seemingly same-age peers, who were in fact computer scripts, and were randomly assigned to receive few or many likes on their profile. Those given few likes felt more strongly rejected and reported more negative affect and more negative thoughts about themselves.

Study 3 (579 US high school students) repeated the effect of few likes from strangers and tested prior face-to-face peer victimization at school (being hit, threatened or excluded in the past two weeks) as a moderator. Teenagers who had been victimized more reported stronger rejection, more negative affect and more self-blaming thoughts after few likes; their expectation of getting likes did not explain this.

In Study 2, a subset of 145 Study 1 students from two schools kept a 10-day stress diary and filled in the Children's Depression Inventory, a self-report symptom scale, at the start and end of ninth grade. Those who felt more rejected after few likes in the task reacted to day-to-day social stressors with more negative affect and negative thoughts, and scored higher on depressive symptoms at the end of the school year, 8 months later.

2757.content: Abstract only. In experiments using online messaging and modified speed dating, the authors put people at the low end of social status and physical attractiveness into the pool of possible partners. Then choices differed by sex as stated preferences do: men more than women chose on physical attractiveness, women more than men on social status, and people who valued a trait more on paper weighted it more in their choices. The sex difference held for long-term partners; for short-term partners both sexes avoided people low in physical attractiveness.

2758.content: Abstract only. A meta-analysis of 173 published studies tested the actor-observer hypothesis, that people explain their own behaviour by the situation and other people's by their person. Average effect sizes ranged from d = -0.016 to d = 0.095, close to zero. The asymmetry held only in some conditions (a highly idiosyncratic actor, hypothetical events, actor and observer who were intimates, coded free-response explanations), and it held for negative events and reversed for positive events, which the author reads as a self-serving pattern.

2759.content: Abstract only. College students ranked 12 gossip scenarios about professors, relatives, friends, acquaintances, strangers, a same-sex rival or a romantic partner for interest, for how likely they were to pass them on, and for whom they would tell. Damaging news about rivals and good news about friends and lovers were the most prized and most likely to be passed on. Apart from romantic partners, both sexes were more interested in same-sex others. Men most often confided gossip in their romantic partner; women were as likely to tell same-sex friends as partners.

2760.content: In call records from a single European operator (9 billion calls among 20 million users over 11 months), people with more contacts spent more total time on the phone, but for very large networks (around 300 contacts) the total did not rise in proportion, so people with large networks did not give proportionally more time and had weaker ties on average, measured as time spent calling. Time per contact grew with network size up to a maximum at about 20 contacts and fell for people with more than about 40. Everyone spread time very unevenly, with most calls going to a few people.

Average call time per contact rose with the number of contacts up to a maximum at about 20 contacts, and people with more than about 40 contacts had weaker ties on average. This 10 to 40 limit was the same over 3, 7 and 11 months of data. The authors link it to the layer of about 30 closer relationships in offline networks.

2761.content: Abstract only. In Study 1 (52 people), a person's expressed liking for a target signalled good intentions toward the target, and those implied good intentions carried the target's liking back, in feeling and in behaviour. In Study 2 (173 people), liking in feeling was returned in every condition, while liking in behaviour was not returned when the admirer's stated intentions did not match the intentions the liking implied.

2762.content: Male house mice (Mus musculus) with a dopamine transporter knockdown that keeps 10% of normal transporter and raises synaptic dopamine by about 70% (12 mutants, 12 wild-type controls) ate 21% more chow and drank about 15% more water. In a runway task for a sweet cereal reward they learned faster, left the start box sooner, paused and turned back far less, and ran straight to the goal, at the same running speed. In a taste reactivity test their positive facial reactions to sucrose were no higher than those of controls, and at the strongest sucrose solution they were lower.

2763.content: Abstract only. In longitudinal data from over 2,500 consumers across 6 years, analysed with a latent growth model, materialism and loneliness each raised the other over time, and loneliness contributed more to materialism than materialism to loneliness. Valuing possessions as a happiness medicine or a measure of success increased loneliness and grew most with loneliness; seeking possessions for fun (material mirth) decreased loneliness and was unaffected by it.

2764.content: In a census of all 532,197 comments on 1,612 online petitions on the German platform openpetition.de (May 2010 to July 2013), 20.62% of comments held at least one swearword or insult from the authors' list. Commenters could choose to show their real name or stay anonymous; only 29.2% chose anonymity. Aggression was higher where a petition carried a heated debate or a scandal in the news, and higher among commenters living in small villages and cities. The authors read online firestorms as low-cost enforcement of social norms against public actors.

In the same openpetition.de census, comments by commenters who showed their real names held more aggressive expressions than comments by anonymous ones, in the random-effects and in the fixed-effects model (which compares commenters within the same petition). The authors call the average effect small and note that many of the very aggressive commenters appeared under their real names.

2765.content: Among 84 male coronary bypass patients (authors at the University of California, San Diego), assigned before surgery to a room alone or to a two-bed room with a roommate who was a cardiac or non-cardiac patient and was either awaiting or recovering from surgery, those whose roommate had already had surgery were less anxious before their own operation, walked about more after it and went home sooner than those whose roommate was still waiting for surgery. Patients with a cardiac roommate also walked about more and left sooner than those with a non-cardiac roommate. Patients with no roommate generally recovered slowest.

2766.content: A meta-analysis of 63 conditions from 50 published and unpublished choice overload experiments (5,036 participants) found a mean effect of choice overload of virtually zero (D = 0.02, 95% CI -0.09 to 0.12), with considerable variation between studies that came mostly from a few studies with large positive or negative effects. No sufficient condition for choice overload could be identified; effects did not depend on the number of options, on whether the choice was real or hypothetical, or on country.

In the same meta-analysis, a meta-regression showed that when consumption was the outcome, or when choosers had well-defined preferences or expertise beforehand, larger assortments did better (more choice was better). Unpublished and more recent experiments were somewhat less likely to find choice overload.

2767.content: A meta-analysis of 99 observations (7,202 participants) from earlier choice overload studies found four factors that make large assortments harder to choose from: a more complex choice set, a harder decision task, more uncertainty about one's preferences, and a goal of spending little effort. Once these moderators were taken into account, the overall effect of assortment size on choice overload was significant, which the authors note runs counter to the earlier meta-analysis (Scheibehenne and colleagues 2010).

2768.content: In an experiment by a Florida State University group, phone notifications alone (call and message alerts, sound or vibration, that participants did not interact with) significantly disrupted performance on an attention-demanding task. The disruption was comparable in size to the distraction seen when people actively use a phone for calls or texting. The authors propose that the alerts prompt task-irrelevant thoughts (mind wandering).

2769.content: In an experiment with 130 female undergraduates (authors at Flinders University, Adelaide, Australia), those randomly assigned to view a set of Instagram fitspiration images (an online trend meant to inspire exercise and healthy eating) reported more negative mood, more body dissatisfaction and lower state appearance self-esteem afterwards than those who viewed travel images. The difference was carried by how much they compared their own appearance with the images (state appearance comparison).

2770.content: Thirty-one adults in Gothenburg, Sweden (16 men, 15 women, mean age 24.5) were stroked on the forearm with a soft goat-hair brush at 0.3, 3 and 30 cm per second, the brush either held by an experimenter or moved by a robot, once without and once with knowing the source. Pleasantness ratings were very similar for hand-held and robot strokes at every speed, whether or not people knew the source. Strokes at 3 cm per second, the speed that best drives C-tactile afferents, were rated most pleasant. Hand-held strokes were rated more intense at the two slower speeds.

2771.content: In a survey of 794 preadolescents and adolescents (authors at the University of Amsterdam), more online communication went with closer friendships, but only among those who mainly talked online with friends they already had; among those who mainly talked with strangers there was no such link. Socially anxious young people communicated online less often, but valued the internet more for intimate self-disclosure, which went with more online talk.

2772.content: Ninety-four college students kept a record of every social comparison they noticed making over 2 weeks (the Rochester Social Comparison Record). The direction of comparison, upward or downward, varied with the relationship to the person compared with, and a negative mood before a comparison went more often with comparing upward than downward.

In the same two-week diary study of 94 college students, comparing oneself with someone better off (upward) went with lower subjective well-being afterwards, and comparing with someone worse off (downward) with higher well-being. Students with high self-esteem made more self-enhancing comparisons.

2773.content: In visual search experiments (authors at the Karolinska Institute, Stockholm), participants found a snake or spider picture among flowers or mushrooms faster than a flower or mushroom among snakes or spiders. Search for the snake or spider was unaffected by where the target sat in the grid and by how many distractors there were, which the authors read as parallel search for threat pictures and serial search for the others. People afraid of snakes (but not spiders), or of spiders (but not snakes), were faster still at finding the animal they feared, and no different from controls for the other pictures.

2774.content: A systematic review found 17 studies of a warm shower or bath before bed, 13 of which gave data for meta-analysis. Water at 40 to 42.5 degrees C was associated with better self-rated sleep quality and sleep efficiency, and when taken 1 to 2 hours before bedtime, for as little as 10 minutes, with a significantly shorter time to fall asleep. The authors link the effect to the fall in core body temperature that follows, as blood flow to the palms and soles carries heat out of the body.

2775.content: In laboratory rats (Rattus norvegicus), the photopigment melanopsin was found in the cell bodies, dendrites and first stretch of the axons of a small subset of retinal ganglion cells, about 2.5% of them (about 1% in the house mouse, Mus musculus). Every rat ganglion cell that projected to the suprachiasmatic nucleus and responded to light on its own (intrinsically photosensitive, 18 cells) contained melanopsin, and the 4 ganglion cells without such responses did not.

In house mice (Mus musculus) with a tracer gene (tau-lacZ) placed in the melanopsin gene, the axons of the melanopsin-containing retinal ganglion cells ran through the optic nerves to both suprachiasmatic nuclei, the circadian clock, where they ended densely, and also to the intergeniculate leaflet and the olivary pretectal nucleus, which serve clock resetting and the pupil reflex. They did not reach the dorsal lateral geniculate, the main relay for image-forming vision.

2776.content: In a laboratory study (authors at the Psychiatric University Clinic, Basel), how much the blood vessels in the skin of the hands and feet widened, which raises heat loss from them, was the best physiological predictor of falling asleep quickly.

2777.content: Nine healthy men took 200 mg of caffeine at 07:10 or placebo. Caffeine in saliva fell from its peak an hour after intake to a low level just before sleep at 23:00, yet against placebo, sleep efficiency and total sleep time that night were significantly lower. In non-REM sleep, EEG power was lower in the slowest band (0.25 to 0.5 Hz) and higher in the sleep spindle range; in REM sleep, power was lower from 0.75 to 4.5 Hz and from 5.25 to 6.0 Hz.

2778.content: Forty-four people aged 19 to 82 spent a baseline night and then 72 hours in temporal and social isolation in a laboratory with continuous EEG and body temperature recording. The fastest drop in body temperature came on average 60 minutes before sleep onset on the baseline night and 44 minutes before sleep onset during the isolation period. During isolation, the interval from that drop to sleep onset correlated with how much slow-wave sleep followed.

2779.content: In freely moving domestic cats (Felis catus), extracellular adenosine measured by microdialysis in the cholinergic basal forebrain was higher in waking than in slow-wave sleep, rose steadily during 6 hours of enforced wakefulness (kept awake by play and handling) from 30.0 to 58.9 nM, about twice the starting level, and fell only slowly over 3 hours of recovery sleep, still above the starting level at the end (six cats).

When adenosine was raised to about twice its usual level by local perfusion of an adenosine transport blocker (NBTI), the cats slept as they do after long waking (less wakefulness, more slow-wave sleep, more delta EEG power) only when the perfusion was in the cholinergic basal forebrain; the same rise of adenosine in a control part of the thalamus did not change sleep.

2780.content: In hamsters, including a mutant strain with a short circadian period, small grafts of tissue from the suprachiasmatic region restored daily rhythms to animals made arrhythmic by destroying their own suprachiasmatic nucleus. The restored rhythms always ran at the period of the donor's genotype, whichever way the transplant went and whatever the host's genotype.

2781.content: Using a thermosuit to control skin temperature through the night, the authors found that raising skin temperature by only 0.4 degrees C, without changing core temperature, reduced night-time wakefulness and shifted sleep to deeper stages (both P<0.001) in young and older healthy people and in people with insomnia, most of all in the elderly. In elderly participants it almost doubled the share of slow-wave sleep and cut the probability of early morning awakening from 0.58 to 0.04.

2782.content: Among 21,600 German residents who filled in the Munich ChronoType Questionnaire, mid-sleep on free days (corrected for sleep debt, age and sex) shifted with longitude within the single German time zone. In places of up to 300,000 inhabitants, 82 percent of the German population, mid-sleep moved about 34 minutes later from east to west across 9 degrees of longitude (r = 0.962 across longitude bins), close to the 36 minute difference in dawn time between 6 and 15 degrees east on 21 June. The authors read this as the clock being set predominantly by sun time rather than by social clock time.

In the same sample, the coupling to sun time weakened with city size: r = 0.934 across 9 towns of 300,001 to 500,000 people and r = 0.703 across 11 cities of more than 500,000, with flatter east to west slopes, and average chronotype grew later as population size rose. The authors suggest that people in large cities get less outdoor light, so the natural light and dark cycle is a weaker signal for their clocks.

2783.content: In albino laboratory rats (Rattus norvegicus), bilateral electrolytic lesions of the suprachiasmatic nuclei permanently eliminated the nocturnal and circadian rhythms in drinking and in locomotor activity, while destroying the medial preoptic area had no effect on 24-hour drinking rhythms. The authors propose that neurons in the suprachiasmatic region generate the 24-hour behavioural rhythms and their entrainment to the light and dark cycle.

2784.content: In a double-blind crossover study of 20 healthy young men who habitually took about 478 mg of caffeine a day, each spent 10 days on caffeine (150 mg three times a day, morning and afternoon), on placebo, and on caffeine followed by two days of placebo (withdrawal). In an 8-hour sleep window starting about 5 hours after habitual bedtime, near the circadian peak of REM sleep, total sleep and sleep stages did not differ between conditions. REM sleep began later and built up more slowly after daily caffeine than after placebo, and the men reported more difficulty waking and more tiredness on waking.

2785.content: In a randomised, double-blind, within-subject study of 20 young men who habitually drank caffeine, 10 days of 150 mg caffeine three times a day, in the morning and afternoon, did not significantly change the onset, amplitude or area of the salivary melatonin rhythm or the cortisol rhythm compared with 10 days of placebo or with withdrawal, measured in a 43-hour laboratory protocol with controlled light and posture. During withdrawal the men reported more sleepiness, had more attentional lapses and showed signs of higher sleep pressure in an evening nap.

2786.content: In a preregistered study of 30 already-established community groups in Cornwall, UK (150 adults from sports clubs, volunteer groups, businesses, bands and chess clubs), members did a general knowledge quiz alone and then as a team and rated each team-mate anonymously. Members rated as more influential in the team discussion were rated higher on prestige (coefficient 0.46) and on dominance (0.55), and prestige and dominance ratings were statistically independent of each other. Prestige ratings went with being liked (0.67) and dominance ratings with being disliked (minus 0.48); people named as someone others would like to learn from had high prestige and no higher dominance.

In the same study, neither prestige nor dominance ratings predicted whom the group chose to answer a bonus round for prize money. Members chose the team-mate with the highest individual quiz score (coefficient 0.78), although they had not been told the scores, and quiz score did not predict prestige ratings. Prestige and dominance ratings instead went with roles held before the task, such as team captain or group administrator.

2787.content: In a 2006 partial replication of Milgram's Experiment 5, 70 adults took part up to the point where the learner first protested aloud (150 volts); since 79 percent of Milgram's participants who went past that point continued to the end, the author estimated what participants would have done. Obedience rates were only slightly lower than those Milgram found 45 years earlier, participants who saw a confederate refuse obeyed as often as those who saw no refusal, and men and women did not differ.

2788.content: In 193 healthy adults aged 21 to 55 who rated their own standing on a 9-rung ladder of social standing and were then given a rhinovirus or influenza virus by nasal drops and kept in quarantine, those lower on the ladder more often developed an objectively verified cold. Among infected people the odds of a clinical cold were 3.84 times higher for the lowest third of ladder scores and 2.38 times higher for the middle third than for the highest third. The association held with income and education controlled (3.65 and 2.44), neither of which predicted colds, and held with mastery, optimism, self-esteem, purpose, extraversion and emotional style controlled. Ladder position was not related to becoming infected; it was related to how ill infected people became.

In the same study, adding sleep efficiency to the model reduced the association between ladder position and colds by 20 percent and adding sleep duration reduced it by 16 percent; with both added the association fell by 28 percent and was no longer significant. Smoking, alcohol and exercise did not change it. The authors read this as poorer sleep among people of lower subjective standing partly carrying the link.

2789.content: Among 595 adults aged 18 to 35 from the US and Canada, recruited on MTurk, who had gone through a non-mutual break-up in the past six months, split at random into an exploratory half and a preregistered confirmatory half, those who had been broken up with reported much more breakup distress (16-item Breakup Distress Scale) and negative feeling than those who ended the relationship, in both halves (exploratory half: omega squared 0.217 for distress and 0.371 for negative feeling). People who had been ghosted reported about the same distress as people who had been told directly. The authors conclude that being the rejected partner with no control over the ending mattered more than how the break-up was done.

In the same study, relationships that ended by ghosting were shorter (mean 25 weeks against 37 in the exploratory half) and had lower reported commitment (4.57 against 5.58) than relationships ended by a direct conversation. In both halves direct break-ups were reported as more distressing than ghosting break-ups, and this difference became non-significant once prior commitment was controlled. Ghosting break-ups used more avoidance and more distant, mediated communication.

2790.content: Each week the Dutch Postcode Lottery draws one postal code at random and gives cash and a new BMW to the lottery players living in it. Players who won spent the extra money mostly on cars and other durables, and most BMW winners sold their BMW. Neighbours living next door to winners who had not played the lottery had significantly higher car consumption than other non-players, which the authors read as a social effect of the winnings.

2791.content: Reviewing lesion, immediate early gene, neuroanatomical and hormone studies, Newman reports that in the male Syrian hamster (Mesocricetus auratus) hormonal and smell signals are integrated in nuclei of the medial extended amygdala, where androgen- and estrogen-sensitive neurons modulate olfactory and vomeronasal input, and that this region and the medial preoptic area form a circuit for male sexual behaviour. Data from hamsters, other rodents and other mammals place this circuit inside a larger network that also controls female sexual behaviour, parental behaviour and several forms of aggression. Newman proposes that an animal's social responses are best seen as one repertoire of closely linked, hormone-regulated behaviours shaped by development and experience.

2792.content: In a web-based study of 2,670 people, self-esteem was more strongly tied to how people rated their own mate value among those who reported less short-term mating success in the past, and less strongly tied among those in a committed relationship or with children. As the authors predicted, these patterns were found in men only. The authors propose a sociometer that tunes itself to the attributes that matter for acceptance in the person's current mating situation.

2793.content: In three experiments, putting people into a state of low power raised their willingness to pay for auction items and their reservation prices in negotiations, only when the products were associated with status. The authors argue that powerlessness is aversive, that status is one basis of power and that products can signal status, so low power fosters a wish to acquire status products to make up for the missing power.

2794.content: Judgements of competence made by other people from the faces of US congressional candidates alone predicted the election outcomes better than chance, for example the winner in 68.8 percent of the 2004 Senate races, and were linearly related to the margin of victory. The judgements were specific to competence and were formed within a one-second exposure to the faces. The authors conclude that rapid, unreflective trait inferences can contribute to voting choices.

2795.content: In 32 adults who first waited passively in an fMRI scanner for brief foot shocks whose voltage (10 to 90 percent of their own maximum) and delay (1, 3, 9 or 27 seconds) were shown in advance, and then made real choices between voltage and delay pairs, participants chose the shorter delay in 78.9 percent of choices where the voltage was equal, and 27 of 32 did so more than half the time. Nine participants, classed as extreme dreaders, preferred more voltage sooner to less voltage later, although choosing sooner did not end the session any earlier.

During the waiting period, the extreme dreaders showed earlier and more sustained rises in activity in the posterior parts of the cortical pain matrix (primary and secondary somatosensory cortex, caudal anterior cingulate and posterior insula) than mild dreaders, and this rate of rise matched their later choices. The right amygdala showed a dread response in both groups that did not differ between them. The authors read dread as rooted partly in attention to the expected bodily response.

2796.content: One hundred and sixty male and female undergraduates read 12 scenarios with a present or potential threatening person, built to vary the features that shape defence in rats and mice (size of the threat, whether escape was possible, how ambiguous the threat was, its distance, and whether there was a place to hide), and chose their main response to each. The links between these features and the chosen response (flight, freezing, hiding, defensive threat or attack, or checking the threat) matched eight hypotheses taken from the rodent literature, gave some support to two more, failed for three, and produced only one significant link the animal work had not predicted. Men and women chose alike, except that women far more often chose to yell, scream or call for help.

2797.content: In a questionnaire study of 381 Israeli adults, viewers asked how they would react if their favourite television character were taken off the air reported expected negative reactions similar to those that follow the end of social relationships. The expected reactions were stronger the more intense the viewer's one-way (parasocial) relationship with the character, and were related to attachment style as scored on the questionnaire: anxious-ambivalently attached respondents expected the most negative responses.

2798.content: In four studies of University of British Columbia undergraduates (52, 82, 86 and 47 students), those who scored higher on a questionnaire of chronic perceived vulnerability to disease more strongly associated foreign outgroups with danger on an implicit association test and held less positive attitudes toward subjectively foreign (not familiar) immigrant groups. In the 213 students of the four studies combined, perceived vulnerability to disease went with more negative attitudes (beta 0.23) with belief in a dangerous world held constant.

In two experiments, students shown a slide show about how easily germs spread, compared with a slide show about accidents, favoured familiar over foreign immigrants on some measures. In Study 5 (57 students) the control group endorsed Scottish and Nigerian immigration about equally (5.85 and 6.07), while the disease group endorsed Scottish immigrants more (6.36) and Nigerian immigrants less (5.53); effects on other items were weaker and inconsistent. In Study 6 (45 students) the slide show did not change attitude items. When splitting an immigration advertising budget, the control group gave 47.48 percent to foreign countries and the disease group 37.57 percent.

2799.content: Abstract only. In an fMRI study, adults who identified themselves as White or Black viewed photographs of White and Black faces. Across all participants the amygdala responded more to faces of the other racial group than to faces of their own group, but only during later presentations: the amygdala response habituated over repeated own-group faces and stayed up to other-group faces.

2800.content: Abstract only. A meta-analysis of family and twin studies of people diagnosed with panic disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, phobias and obsessive-compulsive disorder found that first-degree relatives of a person with the label were 4 to 6 times as likely (summary odds ratios) to carry the same label. Only for the labels panic disorder and generalized anxiety disorder were there enough large twin studies to pool; these gave heritabilities of 0.43 for panic disorder and 0.32 for generalized anxiety disorder as diagnosed, with most of the remaining variance in liability assigned to experiences not shared within the family (for the generalized anxiety label in women, shared family environment may also have a part, the authors report).

2801.content: Reviewing their own startle studies with a danger and safety cue design (one shape pair came with an airblast to the throat, another never did), the authors report that Vietnam veterans, whatever their diagnosed PTSD status, all learned in their button-press expectations which cues meant an airblast and which meant safety. In the startle reflex, veterans with high current PTSD symptoms (13) showed strong fear to the danger cue, no difference between danger and safety cues and no drop when the safety cue was added, while veterans with a history of PTSD and low current symptoms (14) responded like healthy controls (28). The authors report the same pattern in younger Croatian combat veterans diagnosed with PTSD, from unpublished data.

2802.content: In an fMRI study of 21 adults diagnosed with specific phobia of snakes (Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV, no other diagnoses, never medicated), people waited for a possible snake video on trials where a fast button press could prevent it and on trials where it could not. Waiting with control gave more activity in the ventromedial prefrontal cortex than waiting without control, and no other region differed. In the 12 people with full signal coverage, the ventromedial prefrontal cortex was more coupled with both amygdalae while waiting for controllable snake videos than for controllable fish videos; against uncontrollable snake videos, the extra coupling was found only with the posterior midcingulate cortex.

2803.content: In male house mice (Mus musculus, laboratory strain C57BL/6), switching on neurons of the ventrolateral part of the ventromedial hypothalamus with light made 11 of 16 males attack intruders that males rarely attack (females and castrated males) within 4 to 5 seconds; 6 of 10 attacked anaesthetized mice and 6 of 8 attacked an inflated glove when it was moved. Electrical stimulation of the same area did not produce attack. Silencing these neurons with a drug-gated channel (33 mice) shortened attack on male intruders and delayed the first attack, 25 percent did not attack at all, and aggression returned eight days later.

In the same male house mice (Mus musculus), most cells in this area that fired during encounters with males were pushed below their baseline during encounters with females (14 of 18 male-excited cells). Light stimulation of the area made males attack a female in over 80 percent of trials before mounting, but the same light was often ineffective during intromission, worked in 30 percent of cases between intromissions, and worked again at the pre-mounting rate after ejaculation.

2804.content: Abstract only. In laboratory studies, prompting thoughts about finances lowered cognitive test performance among poor participants and not among well-off ones. In a field study, the same farmers scored lower on cognitive tests before harvest, when poor, than after harvest, when better off; the authors report that this was not accounted for by time available, nutrition, work effort or measured stress, and propose that money concerns take up mental resources.

2805.content: In preregistered online replications of 20 studies drawn at random from papers citing the founding scarcity paper (each replication with 2.5 times the original sample), effect sizes were smaller than the originals in 80 percent of studies and in the opposite direction in 30 percent; 4 of the 20 replications were significant. The scarcity manipulations asked people to recall lacking resources, limited resources within a task, or showed images of lack. The authors conclude that within this set scarcity primes had minimal influence on cognitive ability, product attitudes or well-being, while feeling poor may influence financial and consumer decisions.

2806.content: Abstract only. From items answered by 249 respondents, the authors built a 17-item Celebrity Worship Scale that fit one dimension, with no bias by age, gender or kind of celebrity (acting, music, sports, other). The scale orders three stages: low levels are individual behaviour such as watching and reading about a celebrity, slightly higher levels take on a social character, and the highest levels combine empathy with the celebrity's successes and failures, over-identification, compulsive behaviour and obsession with details of the celebrity's life. The authors propose absorption and addiction as what carries a person up the scale.

2807.content: In house mice (Mus musculus) trained that one tone came with a mild footshock and another tone never did, freezing at test was highest to the threat tone, lower when the safety tone sounded together with the threat tone, and lowest to the safety tone alone (13, 12 and 13 mice per condition), a pattern repeated in three further surgical groups. Ventral hippocampal neurons that project to the prelimbic cortex, and not those projecting to the infralimbic cortex or basolateral amygdala, were more active to the safety and combined cues than to the threat cue, and their activity went with freezing.

In healthy adults aged 18 to 30 given a conditioning task with coloured shapes as cues and an aversive sound, skin conductance was highest to the threat cue, lower when a safety cue was paired with the threat cue, and lowest to the safety cue (22 people with skin conductance data). In fMRI (50 people), functional connectivity between the ventral (anterior) hippocampus and the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex differed between threat, safety and combined conditions, while its connectivity with the anterior ventromedial prefrontal cortex and basolateral amygdala did not.

2808.content: In field experiments in Zurich and Bern, run both in the original way with shirts and in a double-blind way with caps (the confederate did not know which cap label she or he wore), a confederate wearing a shirt or cap with a luxury brand label (Lacoste) got no more passers-by to answer a short survey and collected no more money for a children's cancer charity than with no label (720 passers-by in each compliance experiment, 360 in the low-income donation experiment). A green (organic) label brought no benefit either. In neighbourhoods with low socioeconomic status the luxury label tended to bring less compliance and less money (significant only at the 10 percent level).

2809.content: Abstract only. In fear-conditioning experiments with white and black Americans, people from a racial group other than the participant's own were more readily associated with an aversive stimulus than people from the participant's own group, in both groups. The authors compare this to the readier learning of fear to snakes than to birds, and suggest that close, positive contact across groups might reduce it.

2810.content: In an online survey experiment with 1,015 Americans recruited on Amazon Mechanical Turk and shown 36 real headlines (half false, half true; half favouring each party), people asked to judge accuracy rated true headlines accurate 55.9 percentage points more often than false ones, while people asked whether they would share them were moved more by whether the headline suited their own party (19.3 points) than by whether it was true (5.9 points). One false headline was rated accurate by 15.7 percent of Republicans, while 51.1 percent of Republicans said they would consider sharing it.

In a field experiment, 5,379 Twitter users who had shared links to Breitbart or Infowars were sent one private message asking them to rate the accuracy of a single non-political headline, with the message rolled out on randomly assigned days. Afterwards the average quality of the news sources they shared (fact-checker ratings) rose by 4.8 percent and the summed quality by 9.0 percent on days they would tweet (2.1 and 4.0 percent counting days without tweets), and the gap between mainstream and fake or hyperpartisan links shared was 2.8 times larger.

2811.content: Abstract only. In a double-blind crossover study, 20 healthy men received a low dose of Salmonella abortus equi endotoxin (0.8 ng/kg) or saline. Endotoxin produced no physical sickness symptoms and no change in blood pressure or heart rate, a mild rise in temperature (0.5 degrees C), and higher TNF-alpha, soluble TNF receptors, IL-6, IL-1 receptor antagonist and cortisol; after it the men reported a passing rise in anxiety (effect size 0.55) and depressed mood (effect size 0.66), and verbal and nonverbal memory scores fell (effect sizes 0.55 to 0.64). The rises in anxiety and depressed mood scores correlated with cytokine secretion (r = 0.49 to 0.60 and r = 0.40 to 0.75).

2812.content: Abstract only. In questionnaires from 329 people about their local television news, parasocial interaction with a favourite local news personality went most strongly with liking for the news, seeing the news as realistic, and watching for information. Loneliness went with less talking with other people and more reliance on television, and loneliness and parasocial interaction were not correlated.

2813.content: In 16 healthy adults aged 19 to 35 scanned with fMRI, identical painful heat was given on trials where they were told a fast, correct joystick response could shorten it (the schedule was in fact preset) and on trials where they were told it could not. Heat believed controllable gave less activation in the anterior cingulate, insular and secondary somatosensory cortices, and also in regions including the amygdala, hippocampus and thalamus, than heat believed uncontrollable. Pain ratings did not differ (7.20 and 7.19 out of 10).

2814.content: Among 216 adults with cortisol data, recruited from the Boston area and a Harvard executive education programme for US government and military officials, the 148 who managed others had lower salivary cortisol (0.54 standard deviations lower on average) and lower trait anxiety scores than the 65 who did not, also after sex, age, education, income and mood were held equal. Among 75 leaders with cortisol data, more total subordinates and more authority went with lower cortisol and lower anxiety scores, and sense of control (Personal Sense of Power scale) statistically mediated both links, fully for anxiety scores. Merely having many direct reports did not go with more sense of control.

2815.content: Abstract only. Reviewing brain-stimulation studies in cats (Felis catus) and rats (Rattus norvegicus), the authors report that in the cat two distinct circuits involving the hypothalamus and the periaqueductal gray carry two kinds of aggression, defensive rage and predatory (quiet-biting) attack, modulated by serotonin, GABA, glutamate, opioids, cholecystokinin, substance P, noradrenaline, dopamine and acetylcholine. In the rat a single area, largely the intermediate hypothalamic area, is crucial for attack, and the authors attribute variation in rat attack in natural settings largely to environmental variables.

2816.content: Abstract only. A meta-analysis of 120 studies over four decades on one-way bonds with media figures (parasocial relationships) found no significant relationship between social deficiencies and these bonds. The bonds were strongly correlated with things that also build face-to-face bonds (for example felt similarity), with other forms of media involvement (identification, transportation) and with being persuaded, and only moderately correlated with parasocial interaction during viewing.

2817.content: In 12 healthy women given trains of painful electric shocks in an fMRI scanner, trains they could stop themselves were rated less intense (63.7 against 68.9 on a 0 to 100 scale) and less frightening (anxiety rating 2.3 against 4.7 on a 0 to 10 scale) than physically identical trains they believed were stopped by another person or by a computer. Self-stopped pain went with more activity in the dorsal anterior cingulate, right dorsolateral and both anterolateral prefrontal cortices, and activity in the dorsal anterior cingulate and right anterolateral prefrontal cortex was higher on trials rated less painful.

2818.content: In a set of experiments with 1,476 participants in total, people who ate from a shared plate (a Chinese-style meal) cooperated more in social dilemmas and negotiations than people who ate the same food from separate plates. The authors report that sharing one plate raised the diners' sense of coordination, which went with more cooperative and less competitive behaviour, and that the effect held among strangers.

2819.content: In 45 healthy adults in London who learned over 320 trials which of two cues signalled a painful electric shock, while the odds changed every 26 to 38 trials, subjective stress ratings, pupil diameter and skin conductance all rose and fell with the participant's own estimate of irreducible uncertainty, highest when a shock seemed as likely as not. Stress ratings also rose with the number of shocks received since the last rating. Saliva cortisol rose above baseline 20 minutes after the first shocks.

In the same 45 adults, people whose stress ratings followed uncertainty more closely learned the shock task better (r = 0.37), and so did people whose pupil size followed it more closely (r = 0.62). People with higher scores on a questionnaire of life stress over the past month (the Perceived Stress Scale) behaved in the task as if they believed the world was less stable (Spearman rho 0.39).

2820.content: Barber and Santuzzi built a scale for workplace telepressure, the preoccupation with and urge to answer work messages quickly. In their second survey study, telepressure was distinct from job involvement, commitment and general and ICT work demands, and telepressure went with physical and cognitive burnout, absenteeism, sleep quality and e-mail responding, beyond those factors.

2821.content: In a natural field experiment, 2,471 workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk (1,318 from the US and 1,153 from India) were paid the same falling piece rate to mark cells in medical images. Those told they were labelling tumour cells to help medical researchers began the task more often than those given no purpose (80.6% against 76.2%, a rise of about 4.6 points) and were about 23% more likely to label five or more images; those told their work would be discarded marked cells 7.2% less accurately, with no change in how much they did. Workers in the two countries responded alike.

2822.content: In a prospective study in Spain with brain scans before and after a first pregnancy, 25 first-time mothers lost grey-matter volume across pregnancy, symmetrically, in the front and back of the cortical midline and parts of the lateral prefrontal and temporal cortex, regions that overlap the network used to think about others' minds; 20 women who did not become pregnant showed no such change. The change was consistent enough that a classifier sorted every woman correctly as having been pregnant or not between scans. 19 first-time fathers showed no such change, which the authors read as tying it to pregnancy itself.

In the same study the grey-matter change across pregnancy went with the mothers' scores on the Maternal Postnatal Attachment Scale for quality of attachment and absence of hostility toward the newborn, and nearly 30% of the voxels that responded more to pictures of the mother's own baby than to other babies lay in tissue that had lost volume. Eleven mothers scanned again about 2.3 years after birth, before any second pregnancy, still showed the reductions in all regions except the left hippocampus, which had partly recovered.

2823.content: Jasienska and Ellison report lowered salivary progesterone, a sign of suppressed ovarian function, in women from an agricultural community who did hard physical work while staying in neutral energy balance. They present it as the first evidence that energy spent on work, without a negative energy balance, goes with suppression of reproductive function in women, and offer two evolutionary readings, 'pre-emptive ovarian suppression' and 'constrained down-regulation'.

2824.content: In laboratory house mice (Mus musculus), galanin-expressing neurons of the medial preoptic area receive inputs from more than 20 brain areas and send separate pools of projections to different targets. Switching these pathways on with light showed a division of labour: the projection to the periaqueductal grey increased pup grooming and stopped pup attacks in virgin males, the projection to the ventral tegmental area raised the number of times an animal climbed a barrier to reach pups without changing how it treated them, and the projection to the medial amygdala reduced interactions with adult intruders. Silencing the first two pathways in virgin females reduced pup grooming and barrier crossing respectively.

In the same mice, the brain areas feeding the parenting neurons that were active during parenting differed by sex and reproductive state: inputs from pheromone-processing areas (medial amygdala and bed nucleus of the stria terminalis) were active in fathers and virgin females but not in mothers, and the largest number of active inputs was found in fathers. In laboratory mice virgin males typically attack and kill pups, while virgin females and sexually experienced males and females care for them.

2825.content: In male Sprague Dawley rats (Rattus norvegicus), a 5 s chamber blackout given right after each of a series of inescapable tail shocks removed the drop in time spent exploring a juvenile rat 24 h later, the same protection that being able to end the shocks gives. Unlike control, the safety signal did not reduce serotonin activation in the dorsal raphe nucleus, and silencing the ventromedial prefrontal cortex with muscimol, which abolishes the effect of control, left the effect of the safety signal in place.

In the same rats, lesions on both sides of the posterior 'sensory' insular cortex completely blocked the protective effect of the safety signal, while rats with the same lesions were still protected by being able to end the shocks with a wheel turn: a double dissociation between the safety route and the control route.

2826.content: 78 adult workers reported their experience at random moments over one week (experience sampling). The quality of experience depended more on being in flow (high challenge met by high skill) than on being at work or at leisure, for every measure except relaxation and motivation, and the great majority of flow moments were reported at work. People were nonetheless more motivated in leisure than at work, whatever the quality of the experience.

2827.content: 132 employees from 13 organizations gave daily survey reports over 4 days on which they had to remain available for work outside working hours and 4 days on which they did not; 51 of them also gave morning saliva cortisol. Comparing each person with themselves, being on call outside working hours went with differences in start-of-day mood and in the cortisol awakening response the next morning. The person's sense of control over their own off-job activities carried the link with mood, and did not carry the link with cortisol. The authors conclude that hours in which employees must stay available cannot be counted as leisure.

2828.content: 18 heterosexual men in an fMRI scanner at Caltech watched video they believed was live of either an attractive woman or an unattractive man reaching to caress their legs; every caress was in fact given by the same woman, who did not know the condition. On a scale from -5 to +5 they rated the caress they believed came from the man as unpleasant (mean -2.53) and the one they believed came from the woman as pleasant (mean 3.05), and their skin conductance showed more arousal to the 'male' caress.

In the same men, the primary somatosensory cortex, until then thought to code mainly the physical features of touch, responded more when they believed the woman was caressing them than the man, although the touch on the skin was the same; its trial-by-trial activity rose with how pleasant they rated each caress. Of the areas classically linked to the feeling of touch, the orbitofrontal cortex also told the two apart, while the insula and anterior cingulate did not.

2829.content: In a survey of 1,551 parents, the authors compared how scores of parental burnout (exhaustion in the parental role, emotional distance from one's children and a sense of ineffectiveness as a parent) and scores of job burnout related to seven outcomes the parents reported. Parental burnout went with addictions and sleep problems about as strongly as job burnout did, more strongly with couple conflict and a mindset of estrangement from the partner, and specifically with neglect of and violence toward one's children and with thoughts of escape and suicide.

2830.content: A meta-analysis of studies relating employees' perceived control (autonomy in job design and participation in decisions) to 19 outcomes found that, across all studies combined, higher perceived control was associated with higher job satisfaction, commitment, involvement, performance and motivation, and with fewer physical symptoms, less emotional distress, less role stress, less absenteeism, less intent to leave and less turnover. Autonomy and participation studies showed the same pattern separately, except that participation was not associated with absenteeism in the single study available.

2831.content: Couples gave two blood samples at one of four times before or after the birth of their baby, with exposure to sounds, sights and smells of newborns between the samples. Men and women showed similar differences in hormone levels by stage: higher prolactin and cortisol just before the birth and lower sex steroids (testosterone in men, estradiol in women) after it. Men with more pregnancy-like (couvade) symptoms and men most affected by the infant cues had higher prolactin and a larger drop in testosterone after the test, and hormone levels were correlated between partners.

2832.content: 25 healthy adults aged 19 to 29 had two PET scans with the tracer fallypride labelled with fluorine-18, one after placebo and one after d-amphetamine, to measure how much dopamine their brain released, and on another day did the effort expenditure for rewards task, choosing between an easy task for a small reward and a hard task for a larger one at reward probabilities of 12%, 50% and 88%. People with more dopamine release in the left striatum (caudate) and ventromedial prefrontal cortex chose the hard option more often, most clearly when the reward was unlikely; people with more dopamine release in the insula on both sides chose it less often.

2833.content: In an online survey of 2,247 mostly well-educated American mothers (84% with at least a college degree), recruited 2005 to 2010, how supported the mothers felt explained as much or more of their personal well-being as how they felt in the parenting role. In hierarchical regressions the support variables explained a unique R squared of .13 against .06 for the parenting variables on depression scores (Zung Self-Rating Depression Scale), .17 against .05 for emptiness, .44 against .00 for loneliness and .21 against .03 for life satisfaction; for anxiety and stress scores and fulfillment the two sets explained about the same.

Of the support measures, four had unique associations with all seven outcomes (depression, anxiety and stress scores, emptiness, loneliness, life satisfaction, fulfillment): feeling unconditionally loved, feeling comforted when in distress, authenticity in relationships, and satisfaction with friendships. Being married was uniquely associated only with higher life satisfaction, and satisfaction with the partner was not associated with depression, anxiety, loneliness or fulfillment scores once the four were counted.

2834.content: In the NICHD Study of Early Child Care and Youth Development, 1,261 children recruited at birth were assessed at 15, 24, 36 and 54 months. Care by the mother alone did not predict child outcomes, while several features of child care predicted outcomes modestly to moderately: higher-quality care went with better cognitive, language and pre-academic scores at every age and with better socioemotional and peer outcomes at some ages.

In the same cohort, more hours in child care predicted more behaviour problems and conflict as rated by the care providers, and more time in centre care went with higher cognitive and language scores together with more problem behaviour and less prosocial behaviour, again as rated by the care providers.

2835.content: In a single-blind within-subject trial, 17 children aged 7 to 12 professionally diagnosed with ADHD each took three individually guided 20-minute walks one week apart, in random order: in a city park, downtown, and in a well-kept residential neighbourhood. Concentration on Digit Span Backwards was better after the park walk than after the downtown walk (p = .0229, Cohen's d = .52) or the neighbourhood walk (p = .0072, d = .77), effect sizes the authors call comparable to those reported for recent formulations of methylphenidate.

2836.content: In a review of children's physiological responses to out-of-home childcare, Vermeer and Groeneveld state that children's cortisol levels being higher at childcare than at home is a well-replicated finding. The studies they review suggest that childcare quality matters while group size and type of care do not, and that the elevation is more pronounced in toddlers than in infants and in inhibited and aggressive children.

2837.content: A meta-analysis of 33 randomised trials (2,256 adults diagnosed with borderline personality disorder) found psychotherapies moderately more effective than control interventions on borderline-relevant outcomes combined (symptoms, self-harm, suicide) at the end of treatment: Hedges g = 0.32 in stand-alone designs and 0.40 in add-on designs. Dialectical behaviour therapy (g = 0.34) and psychodynamic approaches (g = 0.41) were the only types that beat control interventions.

Risk of bias moderated the effects (meta-regression slope beta = -0.16), publication bias was persistent, particularly at follow-up, and only 13 trials reported borderline-relevant outcomes at follow-up (g = 0.45). The authors conclude that the effects of psychotherapies for this diagnosis are small, inflated by risk of bias and publication bias, and particularly unstable at follow-up.

2838.content: A Cochrane review of 28 randomised trials (almost 17,000 women) found that women given a psychosocial or psychological intervention in pregnancy or after birth were less likely to score above the cut-off for postpartum depression than women given standard care (average RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.66 to 0.93; 20 trials, 14,727 women). Most trials defined the outcome as an Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale score above 12.

Two kinds of support that brought a person to the mother after birth stood out: intensive, individualised home visits by public health nurses or midwives (RR 0.56, 95% CI 0.43 to 0.73; two trials, 1,262 women) and telephone support from a peer, a mother who had herself had and recovered from what the trial labels postpartum depression, who made on average 8.8 contacts (RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.38 to 0.77; one trial, 612 women in Ontario, Canada). Interpersonal psychotherapy also lowered depressive symptom scores (SMD -0.27; five trials, 366 women).

In one trial in the review (Morrell 2000), home visits by a community support worker gave no protection against postpartum depression scores (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.62 to 1.25); the review notes that these lay workers spent much of their time on housework and infant care and little on emotional support. Antenatal classes about postpartum depression showed no preventive effect on scored symptoms across four trials (average RR 1.01, 95% CI 0.77 to 1.32).

2839.content: A meta-analysis of 16 randomised trials (45,826 participants; 15 of the 16 in samples without a diagnosis of depression) found, in the figures as corrected by two errata, that dietary interventions reduced depressive symptom scores compared with control conditions (Hedges g = 0.162, 95% CI 0.055 to 0.269), with similar effects in high-quality trials and against both inactive and active controls. There was no effect on anxiety symptom scores (11 trials, g = 0.085, not significant).

Trials that named a nutrition professional (dietitian or nutritionist) delivering the intervention showed an effect on depressive symptom scores (12 trials, g = 0.329), while the four delivered without one did not differ from control (g = 0.124, p = .328). Trials in mostly female samples showed benefits, and the four in mostly male samples showed a slight worsening that fell short of significance (g = -0.208).

2840.content: In a UK non-inferiority trial, 440 adults who met DSM-IV criteria for major depressive disorder were randomised to behavioural activation, delivered by junior mental health workers with no professional therapy training, or to cognitive behavioural therapy, delivered by accredited therapists. At 12 months PHQ-9 depression scores were the same in both arms (8.4 against 8.4 points; mean difference 0.1, 95% CI -1.3 to 1.5), and behavioural activation cost less to deliver (mean intervention cost about 975 against 1,235 pounds per participant).

2841.content: In the Ohsaki Study, a prospective cohort of 43,391 Japanese adults asked 'Do you have ikigai in your life?', 3,048 died over 7 years. Those who did not find a sense of ikigai (a life worth living) had a higher risk of death from any cause than those who did (multivariate adjusted hazard ratio 1.5, 95% CI 1.3 to 1.7); the excess was in cardiovascular deaths (1.6; 1.3 to 2.0) and deaths from external causes (1.9; 1.1 to 3.3), with no significant excess for cancer (1.3; 1.0 to 1.6).

2842.content: A Cochrane review of 75 randomised trials (4,507 participants, mostly women) diagnosed with borderline personality disorder found that therapies tailored to the diagnosis reduced BPD symptom severity compared with treatment as usual (SMD -0.52, 95% CI -0.70 to -0.33; 22 trials, 1,244 participants; moderate-quality evidence), about 3.6 points on the 0 to 36 Zanarini scale, above the 3.0-point threshold the authors set for a clinically relevant change. Self-harm, suicide-related outcomes, psychosocial functioning and depressive symptoms also improved, but none of these reached the authors' threshold for a clinically relevant difference, and the evidence for them was of low or very low quality.

Compared with treatment as usual, the different types of therapy (most trials tested dialectical behaviour therapy or mentalisation-based treatment, among more than 16 kinds) showed no clear evidence of differing from one another in their effect on BPD severity and psychosocial functioning.

2843.content: In UK primary care records (IQVIA Medical Research Data, 7,655,931 people aged 3 to 99, 2000 to 2018), 35,877 people (0.5%) had been diagnosed with ADHD and 18,518 (0.2%) had an ADHD drug prescribed. The rates of diagnoses of ADHD and of prescriptions rose from 2000 to 2018 in every age group except 3 to 5 year olds; the relative rise was largest among adults, about 20-fold for diagnoses and nearly 50-fold for prescriptions among men aged 18 to 29.

Diagnoses of ADHD and prescriptions were more common in boys and men than in girls and women, in children than in adults, and nearly twice as common in the most deprived fifth of areas as in the least deprived. By 2018, 255 per 10,000 boys and 67.7 per 10,000 girls had been diagnosed with ADHD, against 74.3 per 10,000 men and 20 per 10,000 women.

2844.content: Among 5,639 US adults with clinician-identified depression in the past 12 months, drawn from the 2009 to 2010 National Survey on Drug Use and Health, only 38.4% met the 12-month criteria for a DSM-IV major depressive episode on the survey's structured interview; among those aged 65 or older, 14.3% did. Those who did not meet the criteria reported less distress and impairment and used fewer services, yet a majority of both groups were prescribed and used psychiatric medications.

2845.content: In the authors' analysis of US medical visits, the share of visits at which an antidepressant was prescribed but no psychiatric diagnosis was noted rose from 59.5% in 1996 to 72.7% in 2007. The authors report that much of the growth in antidepressant use came from prescriptions by non-psychiatrist providers without an accompanying psychiatric diagnosis, and say the results do not clearly indicate a rise in inappropriate use.

2846.content: Fifteen patients who reported sexual side-effects from an SSRI completed the Laukes Emotional Intensity Scale. Compared with controls they reported less ability to cry, less irritation, less caring about others' feelings, less sadness, erotic dreaming, creativity, surprise, anger, expression of feelings, worry, sexual pleasure and interest in sex (p < 0.05). 80% described clinically significant blunting of several emotions, and their total blunting score did not correlate with their score on the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale.

2847.content: In a May 2012 cross-sectional audit of self-selected UK mental health services, 2,600 patients had a recorded ICD-10 diagnosis of personality disorder and 68 percent of them carried the label emotionally unstable personality disorder (EUPD). Of those diagnosed with EUPD, 92 percent were prescribed psychotropic medication, most often an antidepressant or an antipsychotic, mainly for the swings of emotion the label describes. The authors conclude that this prescribing is largely outside the licensed indications, and that for patients with the EUPD label alone the drugs were reviewed less often over the previous year.

2848.content: Reanalysing the patient-level data of STAR*D (4,041 adults seeking care at 41 North American clinics who screened positive for major depressive disorder, up to four open-label antidepressant steps) by the trial's own protocol, the authors found a cumulative remission rate of 35.0 percent on the blinded Hamilton scale (HRSD score under 8) after up to four treatment steps, against the 67 percent the STAR*D investigators reported. The reported figure used a clinic-administered self-report scale the protocol excluded as an outcome, counted 99 patients who already scored as remitted at entry and 125 who scored as remitted when entering their next step, and left out 370 early dropouts the protocol classed as non-remitters. Adding the self-report remissions for patients missing an exit HRSD raised the rate to 41.3 percent.

2849.content: Reviewing four meta-analyses of antidepressant trials submitted to the US FDA and analysing the published STAR*D effectiveness trial, the authors report that the FDA trial data suggest antidepressants are only marginally better than placebo, with publication bias and the reporting of secondary outcomes as if primary inflating their apparent efficacy. They report that in STAR*D the effectiveness of antidepressant treatment was probably lower still than the modest figure its authors reported, with the dropout rate apparently rising at each step of the trial.

2850.content: Pooling 102 surveys of 171,756 children and adolescents from every world region (general population or school samples, DSM or ICD criteria, 1978 to 2005), the authors estimated that 5.29 percent met the criteria for ADHD or hyperkinetic disorder, with large variability between studies. In a metaregression, the diagnostic criteria used, the source of information, whether impairment was required for the diagnosis, and the region of the study were each significantly associated with the rate. The authors conclude that the variability is explained mainly by the methods of the studies, and that location plays a limited role: North America differed only from Africa and the Middle East.

2851.content: Updating two systematic reviews (154 original surveys, 135 in the multivariate model), the authors found that the methods of a survey were significantly associated with how many children met the criteria for ADHD, while the region and the year of the study were not. They conclude that across three decades there is no evidence of an increase in the number of children in the community who meet the criteria when standardised diagnostic procedures are followed.

In the same meta-regression, rates of children meeting ADHD criteria were an estimated 5.47 percentage points higher when based on teacher reports than on a best-estimate procedure, 2.32 points higher when no impairment was required, and 2.42 and 4.09 points lower under DSM-III-R and ICD-10 than under DSM-IV. The final model accounted for 44.1 percent of the variance between surveys.

2852.content: Using population databases covering 154.5 million people in 13 countries and one Special Administrative Region between 2001 and 2015, the authors found that in 2010 the share of children aged 3 to 18 using ADHD medication ranged from 0.27 to 6.69 percent (0.95 percent in Asia and Australia, 4.48 in North America, 1.95 in northern Europe, 0.70 in western Europe). The authors report that the share of children using ADHD medication rose over time in every country and region, by 0.02 to 0.26 percentage points a year. Among adults the 2010 share ranged from 0.003 to 1.48 percent, and it also rose. The authors report that methylphenidate was the most used ADHD drug in most countries.

2853.content: A random-effects meta-analysis of 57 studies (1995 to 2012) found that people with a prior traumatic brain injury, mild injuries included, were more often diagnosed with a neurological or psychiatric illness at least a year later: pooled odds ratio 1.67 for any of the illnesses studied, 1.55 for neurological and 2.00 for psychiatric diagnoses. Diagnosed depression (odds ratio 2.14), bipolar disorder (1.85), mixed affective disorder, mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease were each more common after injury; the association with psychotic disorders did not reach significance. Several injuries carried no higher odds than one.

2854.content: In a double-blind study, 14 boys the authors describe as normal (prepubertal, mean age 10 years 11 months) received a single dose of dextroamphetamine (0.5 mg per kg) or placebo. On the drug the group moved less, reacted faster and did better on cognitive tests. The authors write that this response resembles the one reported in children labelled hyperactive or with minimal brain dysfunction, which casts doubt on models assuming such children have a specific or paradoxical response to stimulants.

2855.content: In an online survey of 1,431 adult antidepressant users from 38 countries, 61 percent reported at least ten of 20 listed adverse effects as a result of the drug. The most common were feeling emotionally numb (71 percent), feeling foggy or detached (70), feeling not like myself (66), sexual difficulties (66), drowsiness (63) and a reduction in positive feelings (60). Half reported suicidality as a result of the drugs, 59 percent reported withdrawal effects and 40 percent 'addiction'.

In the same survey, one third of the 1,431 antidepressant users reported that they did not recall being told about any side effects by the prescriber, and fewer than 5 percent recalled being told about suicidality, emotional numbing, withdrawal effects or addiction.

2856.content: A systematic search for empirical studies on the neurobiology of people diagnosed with borderline personality disorder (BPD) found 146 articles in three areas: hormones and biological samples, structural brain imaging, and functional brain imaging. The authors describe the findings as heterogeneous and fit them into an integrative model of stress hormones, brain metabolism and emotion and cognition circuits centred on the amygdala. The abstract names no test in clinical use.

2857.content: In the UK Clinical Practice Research Datalink (GP records of 6.8 million patients in 1998 to 9.6 million in 2018; 65,665 with a recorded autism diagnosis by 2018), the authors report that the yearly number of new autism diagnoses recorded rose 787 percent between 1998 and 2018, an exponential trend (model R squared 0.98). The mean age at which people were diagnosed rose from 9.6 to 14.5 years. The authors write that the rise could reflect more autism but more likely reflects increased reporting and application of the diagnosis.

In the same records, the authors report that the rise in new autism diagnoses was steeper for females than males and was greatest among adults. The authors read the faster rise among adults, females and people without severe autism as a sign that greater recognition underlies the change, noting campaigns to raise awareness in these groups and no clear account of why more adults and females would be developing autism.

2858.content: A systematic review of 74 studies of older adults in long-term care homes (mostly few facilities, in developed countries) found a median of 58 percent diagnosed with dementia, and 78 percent of those with dementia showed behavioural and psychological symptoms. A median 10 percent met the criteria for major depressive disorder and 29 percent had depressive symptoms. The authors report that many psychiatric diagnoses appear more common in care homes than among older people living in the community; the 2004 US National Nursing Home Survey gave similar figures.

2859.content: In a four-site double-blind trial, 395 bereaved US adults who met the authors' criteria for complicated grief (median 2.3 years since the death; 78 percent women) were randomised to citalopram, placebo, complicated grief psychotherapy with citalopram, or the psychotherapy with placebo, all with supportive medication visits. Citalopram alone did no better than placebo on the grief response rate at week 12 (45.9 versus 37.9 percent much or very much improved) or week 20 (69.3 versus 54.8 percent), nor at any other assessment, and showed no difference on grief symptom, impairment or avoidance scales.

In the same trial, the 16-session complicated grief psychotherapy with placebo produced more responders than placebo alone (82.5 versus 54.8 percent), and adding citalopram to the psychotherapy did not raise the grief response rate (83.7 versus 82.5 percent), though it lowered depressive symptom scores on the QIDS somewhat more. Suicidal thoughts fell further among those who had the psychotherapy.

2860.content: Radiologists' reports on MRI brain scans of 656 patients who presented with a psychotic episode (most diagnosed with schizophrenia) and 722 matched controls in Utrecht (1995 to 2010) were classified blind to diagnosis. A normal brain was reported in 74.4 percent of patients and 73.4 percent of controls; clinically relevant abnormalities in 11.1 and 11.8 percent; abnormalities of no clinical relevance in 14.5 and 14.8 percent. None of the findings in the patients was judged a possible cause of the psychotic symptoms. The authors conclude that MRI need not be part of routine screening for psychotic patients.
