2861.content: In a placebo-controlled multicentre trial, 437 adults diagnosed with social anxiety disorder (DSM-IV) took paroxetine for 12 weeks; the 323 who responded were randomised to stay on paroxetine (162) or be switched to placebo (161) for 24 weeks. Over those 24 weeks, 14 percent on paroxetine and 39 percent on placebo met the trial's relapse criterion, and at the end 78 against 51 percent were rated improved.

2862.content: A review of brain-imaging classification studies of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and ADHD reports that both labels are given on the basis of parent interview and clinical observation, that for ASD significant site differences have been reported in best-estimate clinical diagnoses even across sites using standardised instruments, and that no objective biological marker exists for diagnosing ASD. The authors conclude that the field cannot yet use brain-based markers to diagnose an individual with a specific label, and add that a marker must be present before symptoms, defined independently of the diagnostic symptoms and specific to one label, criteria that very few of the reviewed studies meet.

In the large shared data sets the review covers, brain scans told labelled people from controls only modestly. In 590 people aged 6 to 35 from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange, anatomical measures classified ASD against controls with 56 and 60 percent accuracy; pairwise connectivity data from 964 people at 16 sites gave 60 percent. In the ADHD-200 competition (973 people, 21 teams), the classifier best at specificity in sorting people into controls and two ADHD subtypes reached 61 percent accuracy with 21 percent sensitivity, and another study using only site, sex, age, handedness and IQ, with no scan, reached 62.52 percent, higher than any imaging classifier. The review notes that almost all studies reporting high accuracies had fewer than 100 participants.

2863.content: Abstract only. Pooling published and new data on the timing of relapse in 1,210 patients diagnosed with schizophrenia after their maintenance antipsychotic was stopped, the authors found that in studies where the drug was withdrawn abruptly (49 patients) or gradually over 3 weeks or more (58 patients), relapse came earlier after abrupt withdrawal: a 25 percent relapse risk was reached in 6 weeks against 10 weeks, and the difference lasted at least 6 months. The authors read this as drug-withdrawal stressors from long-term adaptation to the drug, and conclude that early relapse may be spared by slow removal.

Abstract only. In the same pooled data on 1,210 patients diagnosed with schizophrenia (1,006 taken off oral antipsychotics abruptly), relapse risk after abrupt stopping reached 50 percent within 30 weeks, with remarkably little additional risk after that up to 3.7 years; inpatients relapsed faster than outpatients (10 against 18 weeks to a 25 percent risk). The authors report that most patients who stayed stable for 6 months stayed stable for long periods without medication.

2864.content: Abstract only. Of the 170 panel members who wrote the diagnostic criteria for the DSM-IV and DSM-IV-TR, 95 (56 percent) had one or more financial associations with pharmaceutical companies, and every member of the panels on mood disorders and on schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders had such ties. The commonest kinds were research funding (42 percent), consultancies (22 percent) and speakers bureaus (16 percent). The authors report that the ties were strongest in the diagnostic areas where drugs are the first-line treatment.

2865.content: From the disclosures of DSM-5 task force and work group members, Cosgrove and Krimsky report that 69 percent of the DSM-5 task force had ties to the pharmaceutical industry, against 57 percent of the DSM-IV task force, a relative increase of 21 percent despite the new disclosure rule. The authors report that three quarters of the work groups had a majority of members with such ties, and the most tied panels were those where drugs are the first-line treatment: 67 percent of the mood disorders panel (12 members), 83 percent of the psychotic disorders panel (12) and all 7 members of the sleep-wake disorders panel.

2866.content: The authors report that in the MOXXI electronic prescribing records of community primary care in two urban regions of Quebec, 2006 to 2015, 158 physicians wrote 101,759 antidepressant prescriptions for 19,734 adult patients, each with the treatment indication recorded at the point of prescribing. Depression was the label recorded for 55.2 percent of them; the others were for anxiety disorders (18.5 percent), insomnia (10.2 percent), pain (6.1 percent), panic disorders (4.1 percent) and smaller groups including fibromyalgia, migraine, menopausal hot flushes and ADHD. The authors report that over the 10 years the share prescribed for depression fell for SNRIs, SSRIs and tricyclics and rose for the other antidepressants, mainly mirtazapine.

In the same Quebec records, 29.4 percent of all antidepressant prescriptions, and 65.6 percent of those not written for depression, were for an indication the drug was not approved for by Health Canada or the US Food and Drug Administration, most often for insomnia and pain (82.9 percent of the prescriptions for pain were off-label). Some indications were off-label for every antidepressant, among them migraine, menopausal hot flushes, ADHD and digestive disorders.

2867.content: In a randomised experiment, 38 healthy urban residents of the San Francisco Bay Area (mean age 26.6) walked alone for 90 minutes, 5.3 km, either through grassland with scattered oaks near Stanford or along a busy multi-lane road in Palo Alto. On the 12-item rumination scale of the Reflection Rumination Questionnaire, self-reported rumination fell after the nature walk (from 35.4 to 33.1, d 0.34) and did not change after the urban walk; the group by time interaction fell short of significance (P = 0.07). Blood flow in the subgenual prefrontal cortex, measured by arterial spin labelling, fell after the nature walk and not after the urban walk, a significant interaction. Heart rate and breathing rate did not change differently between the walks.

2868.content: Abstract only. In a randomised single-blind trial at a university hospital in Italy, 180 patients with the metabolic syndrome were assigned to a Mediterranean-style diet with detailed advice to eat more whole grains, fruit, vegetables, nuts and olive oil, or to a prudent low-fat control diet. After 2 years the intervention group ate more fibre and more mono- and polyunsaturated fat, and had lower serum hs-CRP (P = .01) and interleukin 6 (P = .04) than the control group, less insulin resistance and better endothelial function; 40 of 90 still had features of the metabolic syndrome against 78 of 90 controls. Physical activity rose by about 60 percent in both groups with no difference between them. The intervention group lost more weight (4.0 against 1.2 kg).

2869.content: In a preregistered single-blind randomised trial at Macquarie University, Australia, 101 university students aged 17 to 35 who scored 7 or more on the DASS-21 depression subscale and ate a diet high in processed food and sugar were assigned to 3 weeks of diet change (more vegetables, fruit, whole grains, fish, nuts, olive oil; less refined carbohydrate, sugar, processed meat and soft drink) or to their habitual diet; 38 per group completed. After 3 weeks the diet group scored lower than controls on the CESD-R (P = .007, d 0.65) and the DASS-21 depression subscale (P = .002), controlling for baseline, and also lower on the anxiety and stress subscales. At a 3-month phone follow-up of 33 diet-group members, DASS-21 depression scores stayed below baseline.

In the same trial, the diet group cut its intake of foods high in saturated fat and refined sugar and raised its intake of the recommended foods, with fruit and vegetable intake also checked by spectrophotometry. In a regression on the CESD-R change, the change in processed food intake was the only diet variable with a unique contribution, explaining 15.8 percent of the variance; the change in recommended foods did not contribute on its own.

2870.content: In the IDEA randomised trial in Pittsburgh, 470 adults aged 18 to 35 with a BMI of 25 to under 40 all received 6 months of a low-calorie diet, more prescribed exercise and group sessions; then one arm self-monitored diet and activity on a website and the other wore an upper-arm activity monitor with a web interface, both with phone calls and text prompts, to 24 months. 74.5 percent completed. Weight loss at 24 months was 3.5 kg with the wearable and 5.9 kg without it, a difference of 2.4 kg (P = .002). Body composition, fitness, physical activity and diet improved in both arms with no difference between them.

2871.content: In the Moving to Opportunity experiment, 4,498 women with children in public housing in US urban tracts where 40 percent or more were poor were assigned at random, 1994 to 1998, to a voucher usable only in a low-poverty tract plus moving counselling (1,788), an unrestricted voucher (1,312) or no offer (1,398); 48 percent used the low-poverty voucher. Measured 10 to 15 years later, fewer women in the low-poverty voucher group than in the control group had a BMI of 35 or more (4.61 percentage points fewer, against 35.5 percent of controls), a BMI of 40 or more (3.38 points fewer, against 17.7 percent) and glycated haemoglobin of 6.5 percent or more (4.31 points fewer, against 20.0 percent). The unrestricted voucher group did not differ significantly from controls. The authors call the reductions modest but potentially important and the mechanisms unclear.

In the same experiment, the paper reports what the move changed. At 4 to 7 years, the share of women who felt safe or very safe on the streets near home by day was 74.9 percent in the control group and 9.1 points higher in the low-poverty voucher group, and the share reporting collective efficacy, the social cohesion of the neighbourhood, was 54.0 percent in controls and 10.6 points higher; at 10 to 15 years the gaps were 3.7 and 8.2 points. Access to routine health care did not differ. The unrestricted voucher group also felt safer (9.0 points at 4 to 7 years) and reported more collective efficacy at 4 to 7 years (5.3 points) and none at 10 to 15 years, and showed no significant health difference.

2872.content: Abstract only. A meta-analysis of 37 randomised studies of massage therapy, across 9 outcomes, found that a course of massage gave its largest effects on trait anxiety and depression scores, of a size similar to psychotherapy, and that multiple sessions reduced pain assessed later.

Abstract only. In the same meta-analysis, a single massage session reduced state anxiety scores, blood pressure and heart rate, and did not reduce negative mood scores, immediately assessed pain or cortisol.

2873.content: Abstract only. In the FINGER trial in Finland, 1,260 people aged 60 to 77 with a raised dementia risk score and average or slightly low cognition were randomised to 2 years of combined diet, exercise, cognitive training and vascular risk monitoring, or to general health advice; outcome assessors were masked. On a comprehensive neuropsychological test battery, the total Z score rose by 0.20 in the intervention group and 0.16 in the control group, a between-group difference of 0.022 per year (95 percent CI 0.002 to 0.042, P = 0.030). Adverse events, mostly musculoskeletal pain, occurred in 7 percent of the intervention group and 1 percent of controls.

2874.content: Abstract only. In a double-blind controlled trial, 25 preschool children aged 3 to 5 and 23 school-age children aged 6 to 10 whose parents described them as sensitive to sugar each followed three diets for 3 weeks apiece, with the family: high in sucrose, low in sucrose with aspartame, or low in sucrose with saccharin as placebo, all nearly free of additives. Intake on the sucrose diet averaged 5,600 and 4,500 mg per kg of body weight per day. Among the sugar-sensitive children, none of 39 behaviour and cognition measures differed among the diets; among the preschoolers 4 of 31 measures differed, with no consistent pattern.

2875.content: Abstract only. Comparing USDA nutrient tables of 1950 and 1999 for 43 garden crops, mostly vegetables, after adjusting for water content, the authors found apparent, statistically reliable declines as a group for 6 of 13 nutrients (protein, calcium, phosphorus, iron, riboflavin and vitamin C) and no reliable change for the other 7. Median declines ranged from 6 percent for protein to 38 percent for riboflavin. For single foods and nutrients the ratios were usually not distinguishable from no change, and about 28 percent of the ratios that did differ reliably showed an increase.

Abstract only. The authors suggest that any real declines in the nutrient content of these crops between 1950 and 1999 are most easily explained by changes in the cultivated varieties, in which there may be trade-offs between yield and nutrient content.

2876.content: In a narrative review, Drewnowski and Darmon report that refined grains, added sugars and added fats are among the cheapest sources of dietary energy, while lean meats, fish, fresh vegetables and fruit cost more, and that the energy density of foods runs inversely to their energy cost, so that more energy-dense diets cost less per day.

2877.content: In a systematic review of 151 studies on diet cost and nutrition economics, the authors found that in every country studied, energy-dense foods made of refined grains, added sugars or fats were cheaper per calorie than the nutrient-dense foods that dietary guidelines recommend.

In French national food data (1,117 foods, 2007 prices), the median cost of a calorie was highest for fruits and vegetables (0.82 euro per 100 kcal) and for meat, eggs and fish (0.64), intermediate for dairy (0.32) and lowest for fats and sweets (0.22), refined starches (0.14) and added fats (0.06).

2878.content: Inserting the rise in US food energy supply from the 1970s to the 2000s (adjusted for waste) into equations from doubly labelled water studies, the model gave a weight gain of 4.0 kg in children, the same as the 4.0 kg measured in national surveys, and 10.8 kg in adults against 8.6 kg measured. They conclude that the rise in energy intake is more than enough to account for the weight gain, and that reversing it would take about 2,000 kJ (500 kcal) less a day for adults and 1,500 kJ (350 kcal) for children, or about 110 to 150 minutes more walking a day.

2879.content: Across 69 countries (24 high-, 27 middle- and 18 low-income) with measured body weight surveys at least four years apart (1971 to 2010), food energy supply from FAO food balance sheets and average body weight both rose in 56 countries, and in 45 of these the rise in food energy supply was larger than the rise in intake a validated model needed to produce the weight gain. The association between change in supply and change in weight was significant overall and in high-income countries (P < 0.001).

2880.content: Among 686 children aged 10 to 12 in Belgium, Greece, Hungary, the Netherlands and Switzerland who wore an accelerometer for about six days, girls spent 500 minutes a day and boys 474 minutes a day sedentary (under 100 counts per minute), about eight hours of their waking day. Moderate-to-vigorous activity averaged 32 minutes a day for girls and 43 for boys, and 4.6 percent of girls and 16.8 percent of boys reached 60 minutes a day.

2881.content: Forty adults who met the authors' criteria for cocaine dependence were randomised to Community Reinforcement Approach treatment with or without vouchers, exchangeable for retail items, earned for cocaine-free urine samples in weeks 1 to 12. With vouchers, 75 percent completed 24 weeks of treatment against 40 percent without (P = .03), and documented continuous abstinence averaged 11.7 weeks against 6.0 weeks (P = .03). At 24 weeks the voucher group had improved more on the Addiction Severity Index drug scale.

2882.content: A Cochrane meta-analysis of 86 comparisons from 58 randomised trials (6,603 participants, all in high-income countries, 81 percent of trials in the USA) found that people ate more when given larger portions, packages or tableware (SMD 0.38, 95% CI 0.29 to 0.46), children (SMD 0.21) and adults (SMD 0.46) alike, rated moderate-quality evidence. The authors estimate that removing larger sizes across the whole diet could cut daily energy intake from food by 144 to 228 kcal (8.5 to 13.5 percent) among UK adults and children.

2883.content: In a cluster randomised trial at a US warehouse retailer, 25 worksites got a wellness programme from 2015 to 2017 (twelve modules on nutrition, physical activity and stress reduction, run by registered dietitians, with gift-card incentives averaging about 300 dollars) and 135 did not. After three years, workers at programme sites more often reported regular exercise (5.9 points) and actively managing their weight (6.9 points), but there were no significant differences in self-reported health, clinical markers, health care spending or use, absenteeism, tenure or job performance. On the survey, stress at work (38.5 percent against 39.7), unmanaged stress (29.8 against 30.7), reported unmanaged depression and the SF-8 mental summary score did not differ.

2884.content: The authors introduce the Day Reconstruction Method, in which people reconstruct the previous day episode by episode and rate how they felt in each, and report that the method's reports from 909 employed women in the USA corresponded closely to established results from experience sampling.

2885.content: In a review by about 40 researchers proposing a dimensional classification, the authors state that the evidence to date shows the problems the DSM and ICD label as disorders lie on a continuum with normal-range functioning, and that not one mental disorder in those manuals has been established as a discrete category.

The same review reports that in the DSM-5 field trials 40 percent of the diagnoses tested did not reach even a relaxed cutoff for acceptable agreement between two clinicians, while the same problems often showed excellent reliability when scored as dimensions.

2886.content: In 45 healthy volunteers randomised double-blind to citalopram 20 mg, reboxetine or placebo for 7 days (15 per group), functional MRI on the last day showed that citalopram lowered the brain response to chocolate (sight and taste) in the ventral striatum and ventromedial and orbitofrontal cortex, and lowered the response to an unpleasant taste and the sight of mouldy strawberries in the lateral orbitofrontal cortex. Reboxetine did not lower the ventral striatal response to reward.

In the same trial the volunteers' own ratings of how pleasant, how intense and how much wanted the chocolate and the unpleasant stimuli were did not differ between the citalopram, reboxetine and placebo groups, and visual analogue mood ratings did not differ between the groups over the week; the authors note that the brain response fell without any felt loss of reward.

2887.content: In a secondary analysis of the 2010 British Gambling Prevalence Survey (a representative household sample of 7,756 people aged 16 and over), using reported days of play and monthly spend on 15 forms of gambling and the DSM-IV and PGSI problem gambling screens, the authors estimate that problem gamblers account for a far larger share of days played and money lost than their share of the population: for some forms as much as 20 to 30 percent of all days play and spend, with moderate-risk gamblers a possible further 10 to 20 percent.

2888.content: In 2,367 school students aged 13 to 18 from India, Indonesia, Nigeria, Serbia, Turkey, Bulgaria and Croatia, the authors tested whether the self-report Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) measures the same thing in each country, using confirmatory factor analysis of its 25 items. The original five-scale model (emotional symptoms, conduct problems, hyperactivity-inattention, peer problems, prosocial behaviour) fitted poorly in all seven countries, and no single model fitted all of them, so tests of equal loadings and thresholds could not even be run. The authors conclude that the SDQ self-report lacks measurement invariance across these nations and needs revision before scores are compared between countries.

2889.content: 131 German teachers (69 percent women, mean age 46.6) rated emotional exhaustion and work engagement on the last working day before a two-week Easter or Whitsun vacation, on the first working day after it, and two and four weeks after. Exhaustion fell and engagement rose right after the vacation; exhaustion rose again by two weeks and further by four weeks, and engagement fell back by two weeks. The authors report that the gains faded within one month, faster for teachers who met more time pressure and pupil misconduct after return, and more slowly for those with relaxing leisure time in the first two weeks.

2890.content: In the National Comorbidity Survey Replication, a nationally representative face-to-face household survey of 9,282 English-speaking US adults (2001 to 2003) using the fully structured WHO Composite International Diagnostic Interview, the estimated lifetime share who met DSM-IV criteria was 28.8 percent for anxiety disorders, 20.8 percent for mood disorders, 24.8 percent for impulse-control disorders, 14.6 percent for substance use disorders and 46.4 percent for any of them. Half of all lifetime cases had started by age 14 and three fourths by age 24. The authors conclude that about half of Americans will meet the criteria for a DSM-IV disorder sometime in their life.

2891.content: In the National Comorbidity Survey Replication (9,282 US adults interviewed with the fully structured CIDI), the authors estimate that 12.1 percent met DSM-IV criteria for social phobia at some time in life and 7.1 percent in the past year. Nearly one in four respondents (24.1 percent) reported at least one lifetime social fear, most often public speaking (21.2 percent) and speaking up in a meeting or class (19.5 percent). The chance of meeting the criteria rose steadily with the number of fears reported, from 12 percent among people with one fear to nearly 80 percent among people with all 14.

2892.content: A meta-analysis that updates Salas and colleagues (1999) on a larger database, based on 60 correlations, found that team building had a positive moderate effect across all the team outcomes it examined (cognitive, affective, process and performance), and was most strongly related to affective and process outcomes. It examined four components: goal setting, interpersonal relations, problem solving and role clarification, and reports effects by team size.

2893.content: A systematic review found 24 randomised trials of befriending, defined as an agency-arranged relationship whose main aim is emotional support (median one hour a week for about 3 months, most often by lay volunteers), given to family carers, pregnant and postnatal women, older people with low support, recently bereaved people, and people diagnosed with depression, schizophrenia or physical illness. Against usual care or no treatment, befriending lowered scores on depression scales modestly: standardised mean difference -0.27 in the short term (median 12 weeks, 9 trials) and -0.18 in the long term (median 13 months, 5 high-quality trials). The authors found signs of publication bias in the short-term results, and befriending did less well than CBT in the few head-to-head comparisons.

In the four trials that measured, as a short-term outcome (median 27 weeks), the support people rated from those around them, the befriender left it unchanged: standardised mean difference 0.004 (95% CI -0.14 to 0.15). The befriender was one arranged helper, not people who knew and needed the person.

2894.content: In a non-randomised controlled study in Sydney, Australia, 17 adults who acquired a dog within a month of baseline were compared with 29 who put off getting one until the study ended and 25 with no plan to get one (71 in all; no men in the dog group). UCLA Loneliness Scale scores (0 to 60) fell by an estimated 8.41 points from baseline to three months and 7.12 points to eight months in the dog group, with a significant group by time interaction (p = 0.03). Positive and negative affect and psychological distress showed no clear change in the dog group. In the authors' supplementary analysis adjusting for education, the loneliness result was nullified.

At the end of the study, 82.4 percent of the 17 new dog owners said they had got to know people in their neighbourhood because of their dog, 76.5 percent said they could ask such people for information or advice, and 35.3 percent counted one of them as a friend.

2895.content: In a randomised trial in a residential care facility in Auckland, New Zealand, 40 residents in hospital and rest home care were assigned to group sessions with the robot seal Paro (twice a week for an hour over 12 weeks) or to normal activities. Residents who interacted with the robot had significant decreases in loneliness compared with the control group. In observations, residents talked to and touched the robot more than the resident dog, and more residents took part in conversation about the robot than about the dog.

2896.content: A meta-analysis of studies of team building found no significant overall effect on team performance. On objective performance measures there was a nonsignificant tendency for performance to fall, and on subjective measures a small significant tendency for it to rise. Interventions that emphasised role clarification were more likely to raise performance, while those that emphasised goal setting, problem solving or interpersonal relations were not, and effects grew smaller as teams got larger.

2897.content: The National Congregations Study surveyed nationally representative samples of US congregations in 1998, 2006 to 2007, 2012 and 2018 to 2019 (5,333 congregations in all, named by General Social Survey respondents and described by a key informant, usually a clergy member; 73 to 86 percent cooperated). In 2018 to 2019 the median congregation had 70 regular participants, adults and children counted, while the average attendee worshipped in a congregation of 360 regular participants. The largest 9 percent of congregations held about half of all churchgoers.

2898.content: A systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of 13 studies (5,115 residents aged 55 to 102, mean 83.5, 68 percent women; studies from Finland, Malaysia, Norway, Cyprus, Malta, Australia, Egypt, Spain, the Netherlands, China and Sweden) estimated that 61 percent of older people in residential and nursing care homes were moderately lonely or worse and 35 percent severely lonely. Estimates varied widely between studies: 31 to 100 percent for moderate and 9 to 81 percent for severe loneliness. Most studies used a single self-rated question, and most excluded residents with dementia or severe cognitive impairment.

2899.content: Lane and colleagues report all eight intranasal oxytocin studies their Louvain laboratory ran from 2009 to 2014 (453 participants, 13 outcome measures, 25 tasks, placebo-controlled designs, between-subject in all but the sleep study, built on the affiliation, social salience and social approach accounts of oxytocin). Oxytocin had a statistically significant main effect in only one of 25 tasks and a significant interaction in five. Pooled over the cognitive, emotional and behavioural measures, the effect was d = 0.003 (95% CI -0.10 to 0.10). Only five publications came out of the eight studies, and only one of them reported a null result; the lab had also failed to replicate its own earlier finding that oxytocin raised trust.

2900.content: In a review of intranasal oxytocin research, Leng and Ludwig state that very little of the large doses given in the nose appears to reach the cerebrospinal fluid, while blood levels rise to supraphysiologic levels with likely effects on the gut, heart and reproductive tract. They add that many reported oxytocin measurements were made with discredited methods, and that claims that blood measurements reflect release in the brain are questionable at best.

2901.content: In a critical review of research on oxytocin and trust in humans, Nave, Camerer and McCullough report that the simplest promising finding, that intranasal oxytocin raises trust, has not replicated well; that plasma oxytocin evidence is flawed by how oxytocin is measured in peripheral body fluids; and that recent large-sample studies failed to find consistent links between oxytocin receptor gene variants and trust. They conclude that the cumulative evidence does not reliably tie human trust to oxytocin.

2902.content: Pooling the healthy-subject studies in three published meta-analyses of intranasal oxytocin and human social behaviour, Walum, Waldman and Young found a weighted mean effect size of d = 0.28 and a median sample of 49, which gives the average study a statistical power of 16 percent; for clinical trials (median sample 26, d = 0.32) power was 12 percent. Reaching 80 percent power at d = 0.28 would need about 352 people. Combining this power with plausible prior odds, they estimate that no more than about 24 percent of reported positive findings are likely to be true, and conclude that most published positive findings in the field are likely false positives.

In 33 papers on intranasal oxytocin and human behaviour published in 2014, 29 (88 percent) reported at least one positive finding, while only 62 of 357 tests (17 percent) were significant; only 3 papers mentioned any correction for multiple comparisons. By contrast, 30 vole experiments (668 animals) that changed the oxytocin and vasopressin systems in the brain and scored partner preference gave a pooled effect size, d = 0.76, which the authors read as a sign that the nasal route delivers small effects.

2903.content: In a randomised trial at a university in Malaysia, 176 psychology undergraduates (64.2 percent women) who had used pornography at least three times a week for the past four weeks were assigned to try to abstain for 7 days (86) or to use it as usual (90), and reported craving, positive and negative affect and withdrawal symptoms each night. There were no significant effects of abstaining on craving, negative affect, positive affect or withdrawal symptoms, and this did not depend on how problematic their use scored. In exploratory analyses, abstaining raised craving only among those who both scored high on problematic use and had used daily.

In the same trial, 47 of the 86 people asked to abstain from pornography for 7 days (54.65 percent) reported no use at all during the week, and 39 (45.35 percent) used it at least once: 7 once, 11 twice, 9 three times and 12 four or more times.

2904.content: Comparing young women's access to the birth control pill and to abortion in the 1960s and 1970s, Myers reports that trends in sexual behaviour suggest the pill fuelled the sexual revolution, but neither those trends nor difference-in-difference estimates show that pill access substantially changed family formation; the estimates instead point to liberalised abortion access as what allowed large numbers of women to delay marriage and motherhood.

2905.content: A systematic review of 47 prospective studies of short-term abstinence across six behaviours (exercise, gambling, gaming, mobile phone use, pornography use, social media use) found few prospective studies except for exercise. Exercise showed the clearest pattern of withdrawal-related symptoms, mainly mood disturbance. Short-term abstinence showed promise as an intervention for gaming, pornography, mobile phone and social media use, but the studies did not adequately assess counterproductive effects such as rebound or compensatory behaviour.

2906.content: A content analysis of 304 scenes from best-selling pornographic videos found physical aggression, mainly spanking, gagging and slapping, in 88.2 percent of scenes and verbal aggression, mainly name-calling, in 48.7 percent. Those who did the aggression were usually men and the targets overwhelmingly women, and targets most often showed pleasure or responded neutrally.

2907.content: Using new American Community Survey marital-history data (about 1.3 million women a year) and controlling for the ageing of the married population, Kennedy and Ruggles find that the age-standardised US divorce rate rose by 40 percent between 1980 and 2008 (25 percent with 1980 as the standard population) and that 2011 had the highest rate of any year to date. Divorce rates doubled over two decades among people over 35, while among the youngest couples they were stable or falling. They show that vital statistics and retrospective surveys after 1990 undercount divorce, which made the rate look stable or falling.

Kennedy and Ruggles report that divorce rates among people over age 35 doubled over the two decades to about 2010, while divorce among people in their teens and early twenties dropped; they read the pattern as a baby-boom cohort pattern: that generation divorced at unprecedented rates when young and continues to as it ages.

2908.content: In a letter describing the proposed ICD-11 diagnostic guidelines, its authors, one of them from the WHO, state that compulsive sexual behaviour disorder was classified under impulse control disorders and kept out of the ICD-11 grouping for substance use and addictive behaviours, on the grounds that it is not yet known whether the processes behind it are the same as in substance use, gambling and gaming. They describe the label as a persistent failure to control intense sexual urges over an extended period, such as six months or more, with marked distress or impairment.

The same letter states that under the ICD-11 guidelines the label should not be given for distress that comes from moral judgments or disapproval of one's own sexual urges or behaviour, nor for high sexual interest without impaired control, nor for the high sexual interest and masturbation common in adolescents; and that people who call themselves "sex addicts" or "porn addicts" may not show the features of the label on examination.

2909.content: Using the Transition to Adulthood Supplement of the US Panel Study of Income Dynamics (3,213 respondents aged 18 to 23, 2007 to 2017), Lei and South found that fewer romantic relationships being formed and falling alcohol use were the most important measured explanations of the decline in young adults' recent sexual activity, with falling earnings and more computer gaming also playing important roles; together the measured factors accounted for three-quarters of the decline. Within-person (fixed-effect) models in 655 respondents suggested that forming a romantic relationship, going to college and drinking alcohol likely have causal effects on the probability of having sex.

2910.content: In Part II of the US National Comorbidity Survey Replication (5,692 adults), screening questions from the International Personality Disorder Examination were linked to clinician interviews in a probability subsample of 214, and multiple imputation estimated that 9.1 percent met criteria for any DSM-IV personality disorder and 1.4 percent for borderline personality disorder. Sex, race-ethnicity, family income and marital status were not significantly related to any of the personality disorder labels as estimated; unemployment went with the borderline label.

The authors report that they found no sex difference in the rate of borderline personality disorder, whereas many clinical samples report the label more often in women, and suggest that the clinical sex gap may reflect who ends up in clinical samples (help-seeking and base rates) rather than a difference in the population.

2911.content: In 269 popular videos uploaded to PornHub over a decade, Shor and Seida found no consistent rise in aggressive content; the average recent video contained shorter segments showing aggression. Videos containing aggressive acts were less likely to be viewed and less likely to be ranked favourably by viewers, who preferred videos in which women clearly perform pleasure.

2912.content: In the McLean Study of Adult Development, 290 inpatients who met DIB-R and DSM-III-R criteria for borderline personality disorder and 72 inpatients with other personality disorder labels (77 percent of all subjects women, average age 27) were interviewed every two years for ten years. At baseline 90 percent of the borderline group reported a history of self-mutilation and 79 percent of suicide attempts. In the ninth and tenth years fewer than 18 percent reported self-mutilation and fewer than 13 percent a suicide attempt, and about three-quarters reported neither.

The authors report that fewer than 5 percent of the borderline patients were ever in a psychotherapy with proven efficacy for self-destructive acts and that no medication has been shown to reduce them, although about 70 percent were in therapy and on standing medication at eight and ten years; they suggest the decline may be due partly to treatment and partly to maturation. The suicide rate, 12 of 290 (4.1 percent), was below the 9 to 10 percent of earlier follow-back studies.

2913.content: In three experiments, participants who were asked to reflect on rituals they had performed after a loss, or who were assigned to perform a new ritual after a loss (of a loved one, of a partner, or in a lottery), reported lower grief. Greater feelings of control after the ritual mediated the link, and the benefit held also for people who did not believe rituals work.

2914.content: In a randomised trial in a trauma intensive care unit (82 patients without brain injury, 2002 to 2003), 44 were assigned to aggressive fever treatment (acetaminophen 650 mg every 6 hours above 38.5 degrees C, plus a cooling blanket above 39.5) and 38 to permissive treatment (none until 40 degrees C). There were 7 deaths in the aggressive group and 1 in the permissive group (p = 0.06, Fisher exact test), and 131 against 85 infections; the trial was stopped at the first interim analysis because of the mortality difference.

2915.content: Using demographic microsimulation of US kinship networks and the age pattern of COVID-19 deaths, Verdery and colleagues estimate that each COVID-19 death leaves about 8.91 surviving Americans (95 percent of simulations between 7.89 and 9.87) who have lost a grandparent, parent, sibling, spouse or child; by kin type, about 4.01 lose a grandparent, 2.15 a parent, 2.04 a sibling, 0.46 a spouse and 0.20 a child. The multiplier was stable across infection scenarios and was 8.86 for White and 9.18 for Black Americans.

2916.content: In a trial, 150 outpatients diagnosed with major depression were randomly assigned to behavioural activation alone, to behavioural activation plus training to change automatic thoughts, or to full cognitive therapy, all given by four experienced cognitive therapists. Despite good adherence and an allegiance favouring cognitive therapy, the full treatment did no better than either component at the end of treatment or at 6-month follow-up, and both components changed negative thinking and attributional style as much as full cognitive therapy did.

2917.content: A Cochrane review of 27 studies (10,565 adults with alcohol problems; 21 randomised or quasi-randomised) compared Alcoholics Anonymous and clinician-delivered Twelve-Step Facilitation (AA/TSF), which links people to AA, with other treatments such as cognitive behavioural therapy and motivational enhancement therapy. In the randomised trials where all treatments were manualised, AA/TSF raised the rate of continuous abstinence at 12 months (risk ratio 1.21, 95% CI 1.03 to 1.42; 2 studies, 1,936 participants; rated high-certainty evidence), and the advantage held at 24 and 36 months. On drinking intensity and alcohol-related consequences AA/TSF did about as well as the other treatments. In Project MATCH, 24% of outpatients in AA/TSF were completely abstinent through the first year, against 15% with CBT and 14% with motivational enhancement therapy.

Within the review, the Twelve-Step Facilitation variants that linked patients directly to existing AA members, prescribed and monitored attendance and discussed sponsorship did better on drinking outcomes than usual-care referral that only recommended AA (Timko 2006, Kaskutas 2009). The authors conclude that handing out AA literature or mentioning AA is not enough, and that being strategic in connecting the patient to AA matters.

2918.content: A meta-analysis of 34 trials offering adults personal financial incentives (mostly cash or vouchers, usually on top of counselling or other support given to both arms) to stop smoking, lose weight or be more active found that incentives increased behaviour change up to 18 months from the start (odds ratio 1.53) and up to three months after the incentives stopped (odds ratio 2.11), with no effect beyond that. The effect after removal rested on smoking cessation, most of it in pregnant smokers; weight-loss changes were not kept after the payments ended, and three studies of physical activity found no effect. Incentives worked more among people with high deprivation at 6 to 12 months (odds ratio 2.17).

2919.content: In a field experiment in post-ISIS Iraq, Christians displaced by ISIS were assigned at random to an all-Christian soccer team or to a team mixed with Muslims. Christians with Muslim teammates were more likely to vote for a Muslim player from another team for a sportsmanship award, to register for a mixed team the next season, and to train with Muslims 6 months after the league.

In the same experiment, playing on a mixed team did not substantially change the Christians' behaviour in other settings, such as eating at a restaurant in Muslim-dominated Mosul or attending a mixed social event, and did not consistently change their attitudes toward Muslims.

2920.content: Among 44 adults seeking outpatient treatment in Rhode Island who met DSM-IV criteria for pathological gambling, the 25 who gambled mainly on machines met the criteria on average 1.08 years after they began gambling regularly, against 3.58 years for those who gambled mainly on traditional forms. Gender and lifetime diagnoses of substance use or depressive disorders were not associated with how fast the criteria were met.

2921.content: Using the US National Survey of Families and Households and the US Census, Compton and Pollak found that education and age were the most robust predictors of how close adult children live to their mothers: college graduates were less likely to live near their mothers, and older children lived further away. Characteristics showing the adult child's own need for help, such as having grandchildren, were not correlated with living close or living together, while the mother's needs, such as disability, were correlated with living together but not with living close.

2922.content: Using survey data on gamblers in France, Quebec and Germany, the authors measured how concentrated gambling spending was with Gini coefficients. Most gamblers spent moderate amounts and a few spent much more; across the datasets the Gini coefficient rose with the share of revenue that came from people scored as problem gamblers and with how much more those people spent than other gamblers.

2923.content: A three-level meta-analysis of 295 independent studies (more than 30,000 patients, published 1978 to 2017) found that the alliance between patient and therapist was associated with treatment outcome in face-to-face psychotherapy at r = .278 (95% CI .256 to .299; equivalent to d = .579), and at r = .275 in 23 studies of Internet-based therapy. 2% of the effect sizes were negative. The association held across who rated the alliance, the measures, the treatment approach, patient characteristics and countries.

2924.content: A systematic review of 138 qualitative studies (published 1976 to 2015) covering 170 study populations from 77 nationalities or ethnic groups coded how people describe what the studies labelled depression. Depressed mood or sadness was reported in 68.8% of populations, fatigue in 58.8% and sleep problems in 58.2%. Features reported often that are not DSM-5 diagnostic criteria included social isolation or loneliness (54.1%), crying (43.5%), anger (37.6%), headaches (35.3%) and general pain (34.1%), while concentration problems and psychomotor change, both DSM-5 criteria, were rarely mentioned. The authors conclude that the DSM model and standard instruments may not reflect how the experience is described worldwide.

2925.content: A systematic review of 111 publications (about 28.6 million consultations, 67 countries, literature from 1946 to 2016) found that average primary care consultation length ranged from 48 seconds in Bangladesh to 22.5 minutes in Sweden, and that 18 countries holding about half the world's population had 5 minutes or less. The most recent UK figure, from 13.4 million consultations in 2014 records, was 9.22 minutes, and UK consultation length had been rising by about 4.2 seconds a year.

2926.content: In anonymised records from 142 English general practices (CPRD), 2003 to 2013, the share of first-ever episodes labelled depression that were given an antidepressant within 12 months fell from 72.5% to 61.0%, while for recurrent episodes it rose from 74.3% to 77.8%, so overall about 70% were treated with a drug throughout. Mean antidepressant prescriptions per patient per year doubled, from 2.06 to 3.98, which the authors attribute to longer treatment courses.

2927.content: A meta-analysis of 40 studies (49 estimates, 16 countries, about 32,000 people) found that compulsive buying behaviour, as measured by screening instruments, had a pooled prevalence of 4.9% in adult representative samples (8 estimates, 10,102 participants), 8.3% among university students, 12.3% in non-representative adult samples and 16.2% in shopping-specific samples. Younger age and being female were associated with higher rates; location (United States or not) was not. Heterogeneity was large, mainly from the different measures and time frames used.

2928.content: Reviewing puberty data worldwide, Parent and colleagues report that between the mid-19th and the mid-20th century the average age at first menstruation fell from 17 to under 14 years in the United States and some Western European countries, about 0.3 years per decade in Norwegian, Finnish and US data. After 1960 the fall slowed or stopped in rich countries (small rises in the UK, Sweden and Belgium; in Denmark 13.3 years in 1964 and 13.4 in 1990 to 1991), while it continued in India, China and parts of Eastern Europe. In girls living in underprivileged conditions in China and Senegal the mean age was as late as 16.1 years, and the authors read these data as showing the crucial role of socioeconomic and nutritional conditions.

2929.content: In one cohort, 64 patients diagnosed with borderline personality disorder were followed up for a mean of 27 years and reassessed with the Revised Diagnostic Interview for Borderlines, the SCID for DSM-III-R and symptom and functioning scales. Most had improved compared with a 15-year follow-up, and only five still met the criteria for the diagnosis. Mean Global Assessment of Functioning score was 63.3. Fourteen met SCID criteria for dysthymia and this subgroup scored worse on all measures.

In the same 27-year follow-up of 64 patients diagnosed with borderline personality disorder, the total share of the original cohort who had died by suicide reached 10.3 percent, and 18.2 percent of all patients had died.

2930.content: In the US General Social Survey of 1996 and 2006 (face-to-face national samples, vignettes written to meet DSM-IV criteria), the share of the public who attributed a vignette of major depression to neurobiological causes (labelled it a mental illness and named a chemical imbalance or a genetic problem) rose from 54 to 67 percent. Naming a chemical imbalance as the cause of the vignette written to the major depression criteria rose from 67 to 80 percent (Table 1), and labelling it as the normal ups and downs of life fell from 78 to 67 percent.

In the same 1996 and 2006 US surveys, holding a neurobiological view of a vignette raised the odds of endorsing treatment but was either unrelated to rejection of the person or raised it, and no measure of social distance or perceived danger fell over the decade. For the vignette written to the major depression criteria, in 2006 a neurobiological view raised the odds of judging the person dangerous to others by a factor of 2.70.

2931.content: The Australian Productivity Commission's 1999 inquiry, drawing on its own National Gambling Survey, estimated that problem gamblers made up 15 percent of regular (non-lottery) gamblers, about 2.1 percent of adults, and accounted for around one third of all gambling spending in Australia, about 3.6 billion dollars a year. Their losses averaged 12,200 dollars a year against just under 650 dollars for other gamblers. Ten percent of gamblers accounted for around 70 percent of total gambling spending in 1997-98.

2932.content: In a randomised trial across seven health regions of Ontario, 701 new mothers who scored above 9 on the Edinburgh postnatal depression scale in the first two weeks were assigned to usual care or usual care plus telephone support from a volunteer mother from their community who had recovered from postnatal depression herself (four hours of training; a mean of 8.8 contacts). At 12 weeks, 14 percent (40/297) of the supported mothers and 25 percent (78/315) of the controls scored above 12 on the scale, about half the risk; at 24 weeks the difference (11 versus 14 percent) was no longer significant, after controls who scored high had been referred for treatment. Loneliness scores did not differ.

2933.content: In a trial, 80 outpatients diagnosed with nonseasonal depression and already on antidepressants were randomised to four recommendations prescribed together (diet, exercise, sunlight exposure and sleep patterns) or to a control group for six months, with blinded assessment. The authors report a better course of depressive symptoms, a higher rate of responders and remitters and less psychiatric drug prescription in the active group.

2934.content: In a double-blind multicentre randomised trial in primary care, 273 patients were given four combined written recommendations on diet, exercise, light exposure and sleep hygiene or a control intervention and followed for 12 months. Both groups improved in their scores on the Beck Depression Inventory, with no significant difference between them (7.0 versus 7.6, p=0.594). The authors could not monitor whether patients carried out the recommendations and conclude that written advice alone is not enough.

2935.content: In a multi-institutional cohort of 577 patients with antibodies against the GluN1 subunit of the NMDA receptor (anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis; ages 1 to 85, median 21, 81 percent female, 38 percent with a tumour, mostly ovarian teratoma), 501 were followed at least 4 months (median 24 months). With first-line immunotherapy (steroids, intravenous immunoglobulin, plasmapheresis), tumour removal and, in those who did not respond, second-line immunotherapy (rituximab, cyclophosphamide), 394 of 501 reached a good outcome (modified Rankin Scale 0 to 2) within 24 months, and at 24 months 81 percent (203 of 252) had a good outcome; 9.5 percent had died. Early treatment and no need for intensive care went with a good outcome, and second-line immunotherapy improved outcome in those who failed first-line treatment (odds ratio 2.69).

2936.content: In the Apple Women's Health Study, 71,341 US participants born between 1950 and 2005 recalled their age at first menstruation. Mean age at menarche fell from 12.5 years among those born 1950 to 1969 to 11.9 years among those born 2000 to 2005; early menarche (before age 11) rose from 8.6 to 15.5 percent, very early menarche from 0.6 to 1.4 percent, and late menarche fell from 5.5 to 1.7 percent. The share reaching regular cycles within 2 years of menarche fell from 76.3 to 56.0 percent. The trend was stronger among Asian, non-Hispanic Black and other or multiple race groups and among people who rated their socioeconomic status low.

In a subset of 9,865 participants of the same US cohort who recalled their weight and height at menarche, body mass index at menarche rose across birth years, and an exploratory mediation analysis estimated that 46 percent (95% CI 35 to 61 percent) of the trend toward earlier menarche ran through body mass index at menarche. Girls in the healthy weight and underweight range still showed a trend toward earlier menarche.

2937.content: In a review in the American Journal of Psychiatry, two Johns Hopkins researchers report that recent technical work shows structural MRI, resting-state functional MRI and diffusion tensor imaging to be highly sensitive to common artifacts such as head motion and breathing, which may dominate the results. These and other confounders (smoking, body weight, metabolic variation, medical illness, psychoactive drugs, alcohol use, mental state) tend to differ systematically between patient and control groups, and on that ground they write that the evidence that MRI findings in patients with psychiatric diagnoses are neurobiologically meaningful is inconclusive.

2938.content: In a large field experiment, Facebook users were randomly offered subscriptions to conservative or liberal news outlets on Facebook, and the author tracked subscriptions, the posts users saw in their feed, visits to news sites, sharing, and political opinions and attitudes. Conditional on subscribing, Facebook's algorithm was less likely to show users posts from outlets of the opposing side.

In the same randomised field experiment, being offered subscriptions to news outlets of the opposing political side lowered negative attitudes toward the opposing party, while the political leaning of the outlets had no detectable effect on political opinions. Random variation in news exposure on Facebook also shifted the slant of news sites people visited.

2939.content: In a 2017 field experiment with over 1,765 people, participants first stated how much one week of Facebook was worth to them (67 dollars) and were then randomly assigned to a verified one-week Facebook restriction or normal use. Those kept off Facebook read less news, were less likely to recognise politically skewed news stories, reported being less depressed and reported healthier activities; the effects were strongest for men. After the restriction the value they put on Facebook rose.

2940.content: Using Facebook's internal classifiers on all active adult US users in 2020, the median user received 50.4 percent of the content in their Feed from politically like-minded friends, Pages and groups and 14.7 percent from cross-cutting sources. Just 20.6 percent got more than three quarters of their exposures from like-minded sources, and only 32.2 percent had a quarter or more from cross-cutting sources.

In a preregistered field experiment with 23,377 consenting US adult Facebook users from 24 September to 23 December 2020, the Feed of the treatment group was changed to show less content from like-minded sources (falling to 36.2 percent against 53.7 percent in controls). Exposure to cross-cutting sources rose only from 20.7 to 27.9 percent; most of the freed space went to neutral sources. There was no measurable change on 8 preregistered attitude measures, including affective polarization and ideological extremity; the authors rule out effects of 0.12 standard deviations or more either way.

2941.content: In a one-week experiment in late 2015 with 1,095 participants in Denmark, those who took a break from Facebook reported higher life satisfaction and more positive emotions than those who kept using it. The gains were larger for heavy users, passive users and users who tended to envy others on Facebook.

2942.content: In a field experiment, 51 preteens spent five days at an overnight outdoor education camp where television, computers and mobile phones were not allowed, and were compared with 54 matched school-based controls who kept their usual media use. On tests of inferring emotions from photographs of faces and from videotaped scenes with the words removed, the camp group's recognition of nonverbal emotion cues improved significantly more than the controls', controlling for gender, ethnicity, media use and age.

2943.content: Using de-identified data on 10.1 million US Facebook users, Facebook researchers measured ideological homophily in friend networks, how much the algorithmically ranked News Feed changed the diversity of the shared news users encountered, and which ideologically discordant stories users clicked. Compared with the algorithmic ranking, users' own choices played a stronger role in limiting exposure to cross-cutting content.

2944.content: Combining two INED surveys of how French couples met (Alain Girard's 1959 survey, 1,650 people for couples formed 1914 to 1959, and the 1984 'Formation des couples' survey, 2,950 people after 1959), the authors report that a little under 10 percent of unions formed between the two World Wars followed a meeting arranged by third parties, a share already falling fast after 1945 and insignificant by the 1960s.

In the same French surveys, four settings (the neighbourhood, work, the dance and visits to private homes) accounted for three quarters of marriages among couples who met between 1914 and 1929; fifty years later the same settings accounted for one third. Meeting in the neighbourhood, more than one marriage in five in the 1920s, had almost disappeared by the 1980s.

2945.content: In a survey of 1,060 US teens aged 13 to 17 run by NORC at the University of Chicago for Common Sense Media from 30 April to 14 May 2025 (719 from a probability panel, 341 from a non-probability panel, weighted), 72 percent said they had used AI companions at least once and 52 percent used them at least a few times a month; 13 percent used them daily. Thirty-three percent used them for social interaction and relationships, such as conversation practice, emotional support, role-play, friendship or romance.

In the same survey, 31 percent of US teens found conversations with AI companions as satisfying as or more satisfying than those with real-life friends (21 percent about the same, 10 percent more satisfying) and 67 percent found them less satisfying. Among teens who had used AI companions, 33 percent had chosen to discuss important or serious matters with an AI companion instead of a real person.

2946.content: A cross-temporal meta-analysis of 164 samples (41,641 American, Canadian and British college students, 71% female, mean age 20.7) who completed the Hewitt and Flett Multidimensional Perfectionism Scale between 1989 and 2016 found that all three kinds of perfectionism rose linearly with year, after controlling for gender and country. The largest rise was in socially prescribed perfectionism (the sense that others demand perfection of you): about 0.40 standard deviations over the period, so that the average student of 2017 scored at the 66th percentile of the 1989 distribution. Self-oriented perfectionism rose 0.12 SD and other-oriented perfectionism 0.19 SD.

2947.content: In an online survey of 7,422 adult gamers (self-selected, recruited through gaming forums), the amount spent on loot boxes, paid-for randomised rewards in games, rose step by step with problem-gambling severity as scored on the Problem Gambling Severity Index: the authors report a link of eta squared 0.054 between severity category and loot-box spending, against 0.004 for spending on other in-game purchases. Those classified as problem gamblers spent the most on loot boxes and those classified as non-problem gamblers the least.

2948.content: A Harris poll of a randomly selected national sample of 1,178 US youth aged 8 to 18 found that about 8% of the video-game players met the author's clinical-style criteria for pathological gaming. The players who met the criteria spent about twice as much time playing as the others and reported poorer school grades; meeting the criteria went with poorer school performance even after controlling for sex, age and weekly hours of play, and also went with reported attention problems.

2949.content: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 145 studies covering 2.1 million participants estimated that 1,406 million people (22.9% of the world population) were myopic (-0.50 dioptres or worse) in 2000 and 163 million (2.7%) highly myopic (-5.00 D or worse). Combining these figures with urbanisation and population data and with regression estimates of change over time, the authors project 4,758 million myopic people (49.8% of the world population, 95% CI 43.4% to 55.7%) and 938 million highly myopic people (9.8%) by 2050.

2950.content: Using FAO national per capita food supply data for 152 countries (98% of the world's population) from 1961 to 2009, the authors found that national food supplies became more alike in which crops they rest on: similarity of each country to the global standard composition rose by 16.7% on average (up to 59.7% for a single country), and mean similarity between countries rose by 35.7%. The convergence went with a growing supply of a few globally important cereal and oil crops (wheat, rice, maize, soybean, palm oil, sunflower) and a decline of other cereals, oil crops and starchy roots such as millets, sorghum, rye, yams and cassava. Over the same period food supplies grew in calories, protein, fat and weight, with a larger share from energy-dense foods.

In the same FAO data, each country's food supply came to include more of the 52 measured crop commodities between 1961 and 2009, the contribution of these commodities became more even, and the share of the single most important commodity fell. The authors therefore describe the emerging global standard food supply as relatively species-rich at the national level but species-poor globally. Fifty crop commodities, which they estimate come from 94 species, now supply the top 90% of the world's calories, protein, fat and food weight.

2951.content: In a Pew Research Center survey of 4,860 US adults (American Trends Panel, address-based random sampling, 16 to 28 October 2019), 30% said they had ever used an online dating site or app and 12% said they had married or been in a committed relationship with someone they first met through one. In Pew's 2013 survey the figures were 11% and 3%. Among 18 to 29 year olds 48% had ever used a dating site or app. Pew notes that the 2013 survey was by telephone and the wording changed, so the two years are not strictly comparable.

2952.content: A conceptual review proposes a taxonomy of the structural features of video games, the features built into the game that may help start, develop and keep up play over time: social features, manipulation and control features, narrative and identity features, reward and punishment features, and presentation features. The authors write that researchers have compared the rewarding elements of video games with those of slot machines, and that features shaping gambling frequency and spending had been classified in the gambling literature, while games had seen few such attempts.

2953.content: In a random-sample national household telephone survey of 2,513 US adults in spring and summer 2004 (response rate 56.3%), the authors classified respondents with the Compulsive Buying Scale screen. The authors report an estimated point prevalence of compulsive buying by that screen of 5.8% (6.0% of women, 5.5% of men). Those classified as compulsive buyers were younger, more often reported incomes under 50,000 US dollars, gave more maladaptive answers on most consumer-behaviour measures, and were more than four times less likely to pay off credit card balances in full.

2954.content: Using Twitter's complete follow graph from the second half of 2012 (175 million active users, about 20 billion follow edges), researchers at Twitter found that 42% of follow edges were returned, leaving 58% one-way. More than 30% of active users had not a single mutual tie, which the authors read as using Twitter only to broadcast or to consume information. The largest strongly connected component held 68.7% of active users, against more than 99% in the Facebook and MSN Messenger graphs, which they put down to the abundance of unreturned edges.

2955.content: In two large online experiments with representative samples of American consumers, people shown mild dark patterns (interfaces built to confuse or steer) were more than twice as likely to sign up for a dubious paid service as the control group, and those shown aggressive dark patterns almost four times as likely. Aggressive patterns produced a backlash among consumers and mild ones did not; less educated participants were more susceptible to mild patterns. In the second study hidden information, trick questions and obstruction worked best, and where dark patterns were used the price of the service made no difference to whether people signed up.

2956.content: An automated crawl of about 53,000 product pages on the roughly 11,000 most popular shopping websites (Alexa list, 2019) found 1,818 instances of dark patterns, of 15 types in 7 categories, on 1,254 websites (about 11.1%). The more popular a site, the more likely it carried dark patterns. 183 websites used plainly deceptive ones (234 instances), and 22 third-party companies sold dark patterns as a ready-made service. The authors call the counts a lower bound, since the crawler read only text on product, cart and checkout pages.

2957.content: In four surveys, three of them with registered analysis plans (18,932 adults: young adults in the US, the UK, Canada and Germany, and all-age samples in the UK and the US), between 0.3 and 1.0 percent met the DSM-5 criteria proposed for Internet Gaming Disorder, scored as reporting five or more of nine indicators plus significant distress from gaming. Among players, 58.5 to 69.8 percent reported no indicator. The authors report the label as less common than the rate for Gambling Disorder in the British Gambling Prevalence Survey.

In the fourth of these surveys (5,777 US adults), the people who met the proposed Internet Gaming Disorder criteria reported more regular gaming than other players (Bayes factor 11.29), while their reported physical activity, social activity, mental health, physical health and social health did not differ from other players by the preregistered Bayesian tests.

2958.content: In a randomised trial in Stockholm, 120 outpatients diagnosed with recurrent depression, bipolar disorder, generalized anxiety disorder or ADHD, each with insomnia scored above 14 on the Insomnia Severity Index, slept for four weeks under a 6 or 8 kg metal chain blanket or a 1.5 kg plastic chain blanket. With a blind rater, 59.4 percent under the weighted blanket against 5.4 percent under the light one halved their Insomnia Severity Index score (Cohen's d 1.90), and 42.2 against 3.6 percent fell to 7 or below. In a 12-month open phase in which all could use a weighted blanket, 92 percent of the 119 who finished the controlled phase met the response mark.

In the same trial, wrist actigraphy in 77 participants recorded before and after showed no significant change in total sleep time or in time awake after sleep onset across the weighted blanket group, while participants under it reported better sleep maintenance on visual scales. Time awake after sleep onset fell only among those whose Insomnia Severity Index score halved.

2959.content: Among 324,242 US adults in the National Health Interview Survey (1985, 1990 and 2004 to 2012), asked how many hours of sleep they usually get in 24 hours, the age-adjusted mean fell from 7.40 hours in 1985 to 7.18 hours in 2012, and the share reporting 6 hours or less rose from 22.3 to 29.2 percent, about 70.1 million adults in 2012. From 2004 to 2012 both the mean and the short-sleep share changed little.

2960.content: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 24 controlled crossover studies in healthy adults aged 18 to 65 found that caffeine taken before a night's sleep reduced total sleep time by about 45 minutes (20 studies, n 340) and sleep efficiency by 7 percent, lengthened the time to fall asleep by 9 minutes and time awake after sleep onset by 12 minutes, and shifted sleep from deep (N3 and N4) toward light (N1) stages. The loss of sleep time shrank by 2.8 minutes for each hour earlier the caffeine was taken and grew with dose; the authors' model puts a 107 mg coffee at least 8.8 hours and a 217.5 mg pre-workout serve at least 13.2 hours before bedtime to avoid a loss of total sleep time.

2961.content: Combining the most recent provincial prevalence surveys (CPGI or SOGS, 1996 onward) with the gambling spending respondents reported in eight Canadian provinces, Williams and Wood estimate that problem gamblers, on average 4.2 percent of adults (3.1 percent in Prince Edward Island to 5.9 percent in Saskatchewan), accounted for 23.1 percent of reported gambling spending, more than five times their share of the population. The provincial shares ranged from 6.3 percent in Prince Edward Island to 37.5 percent in Ontario. The authors call the figure tentative: reported spending averaged 2.1 times actual provincial gaming revenue.

2962.content: Analysing the complete graph of the 721 million people who were active Facebook users in May 2011 (logged in within 28 days and with at least one friend), Facebook researchers counted 68.7 billion reciprocal friendships, a mean of about 190 friends per user; the median was 99. Most users had fewer than 200 friends, while a small minority had many hundreds or thousands, up to the site's cap of 5,000. Among the 149 million US users, the mean number of US friends was about 214.

The friend-count distribution on Facebook in May 2011 showed a kink near 20 friends, which the authors attribute to features of the product that encourage users with few friends to add more until they reach 20, and a hard cutoff at 5,000 friends, a limit set by Facebook.

2963.content: In a counterbalanced crossover trial, 16 students (12 women, mean age 25) slept at home with ambulatory polysomnography after reading a story for 30 minutes in bed, from an iPad (58.3 lux at the eye) or from a printed book (26.7 lux). Against the book, the iPad night lowered rated sleepiness before lights out, delayed the build-up of slow wave activity by about 30 minutes and reduced slow wave activity after sleep onset. Sleep onset latency and the timing of sleep states did not differ between the two nights.

2964.content: A systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of 53 prevalence studies from 2009 to 2019 (226,247 participants, 17 countries) put the worldwide share meeting the studies' criteria for gaming disorder at 3.05 percent (confidence interval 2.38 to 3.91), and at 1.96 percent when only studies with stricter sampling such as stratified random samples were kept. The choice of screening tool accounted for 77 percent of the variance between studies; adolescent samples, lower cut-off scores and smaller samples gave higher rates, and the rate among males was about 2.5 times that among females.

2965.content: From fieldwork with US teenagers in eighteen states between 2005 and 2012, including 166 semi-structured interviews in 2007 to 2010, boyd reports that teens repeatedly said they would rather meet friends in person, and that parental fear, lack of transport, curfew and loitering rules, venues that bar teens, and heavily scheduled lives kept them from meeting face to face. She reads social media as, for many, the only public space where they could gather with many peers while physically stuck at home.

2966.content: In a nationally representative online survey of 10,093 US adults (Pew Research Center American Trends Panel, 8 to 13 September 2020), 41 percent reported having personally experienced at least one of six kinds of online harassment (offensive name-calling, purposeful embarrassment, physical threats, stalking, sustained harassment, sexual harassment). The share reporting the more severe kinds rose from 15 percent in 2014 and 18 percent in 2017 to 25 percent; 48 percent of 18 to 29 year olds reported the more severe kinds. Among those harassed, 75 percent said their most recent experience was on social media, and half said they were targeted for their political views.

2967.content: In a nationally representative online survey of 6,034 US adults (Pew Research Center American Trends Panel with an LGB oversample from Ipsos KnowledgePanel, 5 to 17 July 2022), three in ten said they had ever used a dating site or app. One in ten partnered adults (married, cohabiting or in a committed relationship) said they met their partner on a dating site or app, rising to 20 percent of partnered adults under 30 and about a quarter of LGB partnered adults.

2968.content: A meta-analysis of 19 studies (20 randomized controlled trials, 5,612 participants; 10 studies in Africa, 9 in Asia, published 2000 to 2019) of mental health interventions given by lay counsellors: members of the local community with no mental health training before the study, trained for it, and not working as health workers, teachers or NGO staff. Compared mostly with no intervention or usual care, the interventions lowered symptom scores on the trials' scales for post-traumatic stress (13 studies), depression, anxiety and alcohol use, with Hedges' g = -0.616 (95% CI -0.866 to -0.366), a medium effect; the authors found no evidence of publication bias.

2969.content: In a randomized field experiment, 86 students who had scored C, D or F on the first exam of a large introductory psychology course received an email each week for six weeks: a review question only, the review question plus messages urging them to keep their self-esteem high, or the review question plus messages urging them to take personal control of their grades. D and F students in the self-esteem condition fell from 57% correct on the first exam to 38% on the final, while D and F students in the other two conditions did not change (time by condition by grade interaction, F(2, 74) = 3.10, p = .05). The control messages did not raise grades either.

2970.content: A systematic review of 40 papers (5 randomized trials, 4 non-randomized trials, 17 cohort studies) on formal, regular volunteering found that in cohort studies volunteers reported fewer depressive symptoms (favourable in four of six cohorts that measured them) and more life satisfaction and wellbeing, with no consistent difference in physical health. A meta-analysis of five cohort studies, adjusted for baseline differences, found volunteers at lower risk of death (risk ratio 0.78, 95% CI 0.66 to 0.90).

In the five small randomized trials of volunteering (308 participants, nearly all older US adults, most volunteering with children in schools, such as the Experience Corps trial), no significant effects were found on depressive symptom scores, self-rated health or self-esteem; some trials reported gains in physical activity and cognitive function. The authors judge the trials likely underpowered, with high attrition.

2971.content: Using state-by-state forecasts based on the polls a week before the 2008 US presidential election, the authors computed the probability that a single vote would decide the national outcome: about 1 in 10 million in the states where it was highest (New Mexico, Virginia, New Hampshire, Colorado) and 1 in 60 million for the average US voter.

2972.content: Abstract only. Using a data set with measures of the preferences of average citizens, economic elites and organized interest groups on 1,779 US policy issues, a multivariate analysis found that economic elites and business-oriented interest groups have substantial independent effects on US government policy, while average citizens and mass-based interest groups have little or no independent influence.

2973.content: In two field studies at the global headquarters of two Fortune 500 multinationals that removed walls and cubicles, employees wore sociometric badges (infrared, microphone, location) before and after the move. At the first company, 52 participants spent 72% less time in face-to-face interaction (about 5.8 hours per person per day before, 1.7 after), while emails sent to other participants rose 56% and instant messages 67%. At the second company, 100 employees spent 67% to 71% less time face to face and emailed each other 22% to 50% more. The authors read the drop as employees preserving privacy when everyone could see them.

2974.content: In field experiments in 24 forests across Japan (2005 to 2006), 280 male university students (mean age 21.7) each spent one day at a forest site and one day at a city site in a crossover design (12 per experiment, order assigned at random), sitting and viewing the scene for about 14 minutes and walking for about 16 minutes. Compared with the city, in the forest salivary cortisol was 13.4% lower after viewing and 15.8% lower after walking, pulse rate 6.0% and 3.9% lower, systolic blood pressure 1.7% and 1.9% lower, and heart rate variability showed more parasympathetic and less sympathetic activity; walking load did not differ between sites.

2975.content: A meta-analysis of electronic performance monitoring at work (94 independent samples, 23,461 workers) found no significant relation between the presence of monitoring and performance, or any kind of performance behaviour. The presence of monitoring went with more worker stress and strain (ρ = .16, 95% CI .13 to .20), and this held at every level of purpose, invasiveness and timing of the monitoring.

2976.content: A meta-analysis of 22 studies published after 2001 (76 comparisons, samples of 14 to 514 people; 9 from the USA, 7 Europe, 5 Asia, 1 Middle East) compared health outcomes before and after gardening, or between gardeners and non-gardeners. Gardening, including horticultural therapy, went with better outcomes overall (Hedges' d = 0.42, 95% CI 0.36 to 0.48), including fewer reported depression and anxiety symptoms, less stress and more life satisfaction, quality of life and sense of community. Egger's test showed publication bias; after trim and fill the effect stayed positive (0.35, 95% CI 0.27 to 0.43). Effects were larger in before-after comparisons, in horticultural therapy and in patients.

2977.content: Abstract only. Records of patients recovering from gallbladder removal (cholecystectomy) at a suburban Pennsylvania hospital between 1972 and 1981 were examined: 23 patients assigned to rooms with windows looking out on a natural scene had shorter postoperative stays, fewer negative comments in nurses' notes and took fewer potent painkillers than 23 matched patients in similar rooms whose windows faced a brick wall.

2978.content: Abstract only. In a study combining quantitative and qualitative data on people's work, the more time people spent handling email, the greater their sense of being overloaded, and the more email they processed, the greater their perceived ability to cope. Contrary to earlier studies, time spent working did not mediate the link between email and overload.

Abstract only.
