After controlling for established developmental risk factors, children in the most isolated quarter had a higher risk at 32 of being diagnosed with past-year major depression (relative risk 1.76, 95% CI 1.12 to 2.77), of C-reactive protein above 3 mg/L (1.60, 1.04 to 2.47) and of metabolic risk clustering (1.96, 1.21 to 3.17). Most of the isolated children (86.0 percent) were not maltreated and 70.1 percent were not in low socioeconomic status.

3084.content: Abstract only. In a 2-year longitudinal follow-up of young women in the transition to adulthood, the authors report that women with one or more childhood adversities (such as family violence or a parent with psychopathology or alcoholism) were more likely to become depressed after less total stress than women without such adversity, and that this was not accounted for by chronic stress or prior depression. The abstract gives no sample size and no effect sizes.

3085.content: Abstract only. In postmortem hippocampus, suicide victims with a history of childhood abuse had lower glucocorticoid receptor mRNA, fewer transcripts carrying the receptor's 1F splice variant and more cytosine methylation of the neuron-specific NR3C1 promoter than suicide victims without childhood abuse or controls. Promoter constructs methylated to mimic the abused group's pattern bound less of the NGFI-A transcription factor and showed less NGFI-A-inducible transcription. The authors read this as the human counterpart of the rat finding that maternal care programs hippocampal glucocorticoid receptor expression. The abstract gives no group sizes.

3086.content: In the second wave of a US national survey (NESARC, 34,653 adults interviewed 2004 to 2005), past-year stressful life events went with higher 12-month rates of a major depressive episode, PTSD and other anxiety diagnoses, and the added risk was larger in people who reported more childhood adversities before age 17. For women with three or more major past-year events against none, the difference in risk of being diagnosed with a major depressive episode was 27.3 percentage points among those reporting three or more childhood adversities and 14.8 among those reporting none; for men it was 22.7 against 9.7. The effect appeared mainly in people with three or more childhood adversities; the number of major events needed to show it differed between the sexes (for depression, three or more in women, one or two already in men).

In the same NESARC sample, people who reported more childhood adversities rated their perceived stress higher at the same number of past-year stressful events, and the rise in perceived stress with more events was steeper among those reporting three or more adversities than among those reporting none. Among women, perceived stress was higher with more childhood adversity in 17 of 18 comparisons within a given level of past-year events; among men in 11 of 18.

3087.content: Abstract only. Using PET with the mu-opioid receptor tracer [11C]carfentanil before and immediately after drinking alcohol, in heavy drinkers and control subjects, the authors found that drinking released the body's own opioids in the nucleus accumbens and the orbitofrontal cortex, and release in the two regions was positively correlated. In heavy drinkers, the change in orbitofrontal binding correlated with problem alcohol use and with the reported high. The abstract gives no sample sizes.

3088.content: Abstract only. Comparing 58 children with high and 100 with low lead levels in shed teeth (dentine), the children with high levels scored significantly lower on the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children (Revised), on verbal subtests, on three other measures of auditory or speech processing and on a measure of attention, and none of 39 other variables studied explained the differences. Teachers' ratings of all 2,146 children whose teeth were analysed showed non-adaptive classroom behaviour becoming more frequent in step with dentine lead level. The exposure was below doses that produce symptoms of lead poisoning severe enough to be recognised clinically.

3089.content: Following 2,891 adolescents in the Helsinki metropolitan area, Finland, over five waves from age 13 to 19 with a random-intercept cross-lagged model, the authors found that when a teenager's depressive symptoms (scored on the 10-item Finnish Depression Scale) were higher than that teenager's own average, active social media use (chatting, sharing, following friends) was slightly higher a year later (B = 0.13, p = 0.039). Higher than usual social media use was not followed by more depressive symptoms (B = 0.01, p = 0.802). The authors call the links very small, statistically weak and somewhat inconsistent over time.

3090.content: In an experiment, 36 toddlers aged 24 to 30 months were randomly assigned to learn new verbs through live interaction with an adult, through a video chat in which the adult responded to the child, or through a yoked video of those same chats that did not respond to the child (12 per group). Children trained live or by video chat looked significantly longer at the matching action at test; children trained by the non-responsive video performed at chance. The video chat and live groups did not differ.

3091.content: Abstract only. Bianchi reports that despite the rapid rise in mothers' paid work, mothers' time with children has stayed quite stable over time: in the past, mothers not in paid work lost time with children to unpaid family work and housework and to substitute carers, especially in large families, while employed mothers today protect time with children by working part-time, leaving paid work for some years, and cutting housework, volunteer work and leisure. Fathers in marriages were spending more time with their children than in the past. The abstract gives no figures and does not name the country.

3092.content: Reviewing historical and empirical evidence on industry conduct, Brownell and Warner describe the tobacco industry's playbook: stressing personal responsibility, paying scientists whose research raised doubt, attacking the science that found harm as 'junk', making self-regulatory pledges, lobbying with large resources against government action, bringing in 'safer' products, and at the same time manipulating and denying both the addictiveness of cigarettes and their marketing to children. In 1994 the heads of every major US tobacco company denied under oath before Congress that they believed smoking gave rise to lung cancer or that nicotine was addictive.

The same review compares the food industry with tobacco and finds both similarities and differences: food companies have issued their own pledges of concern for public health, pursue self-regulation (for example a pledge to cut traditional soft drinks in schools that left sports drinks untouched, and a pledge on marketing to children), fund research and professional organisations, and market 'healthier' products, as tobacco did. The authors say food differs from tobacco and the food industry differs from tobacco companies in important ways.

3093.content: Extending their 2015 analysis to 2015 data, Case and Deaton report that total mortality among US white non-Hispanic adults in midlife kept rising, with most of the rise from drug overdoses, suicides and alcohol-related liver deaths (deaths of despair) together with a stalled decline in heart disease deaths, mostly among those with a high school degree or less. From 1998 to 2015 mortality rose for white non-Hispanic men and women without a college degree and fell for those with one, in every five-year age group from 35 to 39 through 55 to 59, while mortality of black and Hispanic Americans and of midlife adults in other rich countries kept falling.

Testing whether current income explains the mortality turn, Case and Deaton find that it cannot give a comprehensive account: the income profiles of black and Hispanic Americans, whose mortality fell, were no better than those of whites, and in European data mortality trends did not follow income trends despite very different paths of median income after the Great Recession.

Case and Deaton propose a preliminary account of cumulative disadvantage across birth cohorts: for whites without a college degree, each cohort entering the labour market since the 1970s met worse job prospects, and with them came falling marriage, unstable partnerships, social isolation and withdrawal from work. In their birth-cohort analysis, deaths of despair, pain, poor health as people rated it themselves, never marrying and, for men, being out of the labour force rose together from one cohort to the next, while those with a college degree saw much smaller changes. They note that black Americans may have more extensive kin networks and churches to support them.

3094.content: A review of 76 neuroimaging studies with an activation likelihood meta-analysis of 36 functional MRI studies (51 experiments, 1,993 patients and healthy controls, plus the earlier Etkin and Wager meta-analysis) found that, as groups, people diagnosed with social anxiety disorder showed more activity than controls in the bilateral amygdala and adjacent regions (bed nucleus of the stria terminalis, parahippocampal gyrus), right insula, anterior cingulate, left dorsolateral and medial prefrontal cortex and occipitotemporal regions, and in medial parietal and occipital regions. No region was consistently more active in controls.

The authors state that they cannot draw inferences about whether their model is specific to social anxiety disorder, since other anxiety disorders, except PTSD, lack comparable meta-analyses; that the specificity of the findings has not yet been investigated; and that the shortage and small size of structural studies and the heterogeneity of methods preclude strong conclusions. They write that it is open whether the changes reflect a general disturbance of emotion processing shared with OCD and depressive diagnoses.

3095.content: Abstract only. Using social network analysis, the authors mapped the social networks of 22 clinical patients, 11 diagnosed with borderline personality disorder and 11 with no personality disorder. The networks of the patients with the borderline label held more former romantic partners and more relationships that had ended. Patients without a personality disorder reported more positive relations (trust, social support) with the more central members of their networks, while the borderline group did not discriminate among network members. The authors read this as a deficit in social cognition for positive relations.

3096.content: Abstract only. In 5,083 twins and 1,285 of their non-twin siblings who completed the borderline features scale of the Personality Assessment Inventory (PAI-BOR), the authors found both gene-environment interaction and gene-environment correlation. After a divorce or break-up, violent assault, sexual assault or job loss, the environmental variance in borderline features was higher, so heritability was lower in exposed people; after sexual assault, genetic variance was also lower. For some life events, the genes that influence borderline features also raised the likelihood of being exposed to the event.

3097.content: Abstract only. In an fMRI study, 20 unmedicated patients diagnosed with borderline personality disorder and 20 healthy participants matched for age and education played Cyberball, a virtual ball-tossing game, in blocks of exclusion, inclusion and a control condition with predefined game rules, and rated how excluded they felt after each block. Both groups reported feeling similarly excluded when they were excluded, but the diagnosed patients also reported feeling more excluded than the controls during inclusion and the control condition. In all three conditions the diagnosed patients showed stronger activation of the dorsal anterior cingulate and medial prefrontal cortex, and activity in regions such as the insula and precuneus did not vary with the condition in the diagnosed group as it did in the controls.

3098.content: Abstract only. In a PET study of seven healthy adults, [11C]raclopride binding to dopamine D2/D3 receptors was measured before and after an intravenous dose of dextroamphetamine (0.3 mg per kg). The change in binding, the authors' measure of dopamine release, was greater in the anteroventral striatum (accumbens area, ventromedial caudate and anteroventral putamen) than in the dorsal caudate. The rise in euphoria ratings correlated with the change in binding in the anteroventral striatum (r = -0.95) and not in the dorsal caudate (r = 0.30, not significant), and in a post hoc analysis tension-anxiety scale scores also correlated with it (r = 0.80, uncorrected). The authors conclude that the size of ventral striatal dopamine release goes with the size of the hedonic response to the drug.

3099.content: In a PET study with the mu-opioid receptor tracer [11C]carfentanil in Michigan, 17 medication-free adults diagnosed with current major depressive disorder by SCID interview (mean 17-item Hamilton score 18.5) and 18 matched healthy controls received rejection and acceptance feedback in a social feedback task. Both groups reported feeling equally more sad and rejected during rejection. In the controls, rejection released the body's own opioids at mu receptors in the right nucleus accumbens, both amygdalae, the midline thalamus and the periaqueductal gray; in the diagnosed group no region showed release and both amygdalae showed the opposite change. Five minutes after the last rejection the controls' sad and rejected ratings had returned toward baseline while the diagnosed group's ratings stayed raised.

In the same study, acceptance feedback raised happy and accepted ratings in both groups, more in the diagnosed group, but these ratings returned quickly toward baseline after the acceptance trials ended. After acceptance the controls reported higher self-esteem and more desire for social interaction, and the diagnosed group did not. In the controls, the rise in desire for social interaction correlated with opioid release at mu receptors in the left nucleus accumbens (r = 0.60); no such link was found in the diagnosed group, whose left nucleus accumbens showed the opposite change during acceptance.

3100.content: Abstract only. In an fMRI study of 20 romantic couples, the female partner was scanned while her partner stood just outside the scanner and received unpleasant electric shocks. Holding the partner's arm while he or she was in pain, compared with control conditions, went with more activity in the ventral striatum and the septal area, regions involved in maternal behaviour in animals. Greater activity in these regions went with higher self-rated support-giving effectiveness and social connection (r = 0.55 to 0.64), and more septal activity during support giving went with less activity in the left (r = -0.44) and right (r = -0.42) amygdala.

3101.content: Abstract only. In the Cardiovascular Health Study in four US counties, 824 older adults completed the Neuropsychiatric Inventory; 362 were classified as having dementia and 320 as having mild cognitive impairment by clinical criteria and expert committee review. In the previous month 75 percent of those with dementia (62 percent clinically significant) and 43 percent of those with mild cognitive impairment showed at least one neuropsychiatric symptom on the inventory; among those with dementia the most frequent symptoms were apathy (36 percent), depression (32 percent) and agitation or aggression (30 percent). The authors report no difference in the rate of symptoms between Alzheimer-type and other dementias except for aberrant motor behaviour (5.4 against 1 percent).

3102.content: In a PET study with the mu-opioid receptor tracer [11C]carfentanil, 18 unmedicated women diagnosed with borderline personality disorder and 14 healthy women were scanned in a neutral state and while recalling a rehearsed sad personal memory. At baseline the diagnosed women had higher mu-opioid receptor availability than the controls in the orbitofrontal cortex, caudate, nucleus accumbens and left amygdala (average group differences of 25 to 47 percent) and lower availability in the posterior thalamus. During sadness the diagnosed women showed more release of the body's own opioids than the controls in the pregenual anterior cingulate, left orbitofrontal cortex, left ventral pallidum, left amygdala and left inferior temporal cortex, and less in the left nucleus accumbens, hypothalamus and right hippocampus. Correlations with impulsiveness and dissociation scores did not survive correction for multiple comparisons.

3103.content: Abstract only. A meta-analysis of 19 functional imaging studies of negative against neutral stimuli (281 patients diagnosed with borderline personality disorder, 293 healthy controls) and 10 studies of grey matter (263 diagnosed patients, 278 controls) found that, on average, the diagnosed patients showed relatively more activation of the left amygdala and posterior cingulate cortex and blunted responses of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex to negative stimuli. The left amygdala showed both more activity and smaller grey matter volume. The higher amygdala activity was found in medication-free samples and not in samples of diagnosed patients taking psychotropic medication.

3104.content: In Part II of the US National Comorbidity Survey Replication (5,692 adults), people who met the survey's criteria for borderline personality disorder (5 or more symptoms endorsed) more often reported each of three chronic sleep problems on most days for at least two weeks in the past year: delayed sleep onset (adjusted odds ratio 1.8), waking after sleep onset (1.9) and waking earlier than desired (2.3), after accounting for chronic health problems, other diagnoses, suicidal ideation in the past year and sociodemographic factors. 63 percent of those meeting the criteria reported at least one of these sleep problems. The author reports that these odds ratios were similar in size to those of labels traditionally linked with poor sleep, such as major depression and generalized anxiety.

In the same survey, the number of borderline symptoms interacted with chronic sleep problems: people with more symptoms and more sleep problems reported more social and emotional impairment (beta = .19), cognitive impairment (beta = .17) and self-care problems (beta = .08), after accounting for covariates. No interaction was found for days out of role, role impairment or physical mobility.

3105.content: In a PET study with [11C]raclopride, 20 healthy men who usually drank no more than two caffeinated drinks a day were scanned once after placebo and once after 300 mg of caffeine by mouth, about the caffeine in 2 to 3 cups of coffee. Compared with placebo, caffeine raised the availability of dopamine D2/D3 receptors in the putamen and ventral striatum and not in the caudate. Because dopamine release would have lowered that availability, the authors conclude that caffeine at usual doses does not raise striatal dopamine, and read the result as more D2/D3 receptors or a change in their affinity. In the ventral striatum the rise in receptor availability went with the rise in self-rated alertness.

3106.content: A systematic review found 32 studies published from 1980 to December 2015, 20 of them pooled in a meta-analysis, comparing the sleep of people diagnosed with borderline personality disorder with that of healthy or clinical controls. Against healthy controls the diagnosed groups differed on objective sleep continuity (time to fall asleep, total sleep time, sleep efficiency) and sleep architecture (REM latency and density, slow wave sleep), mostly measured by laboratory polysomnography, and on self-reported nightmares and sleep quality. The authors report that these differences were independent of depression and of psychotropic medication, and that there were few significant differences between the diagnosed groups and clinical control groups, most of them depressed. Two of the 32 studies were prospective and the rest cross-sectional.

3107.content: Abstract only. In a Scotland-wide record-linkage cohort of 766,244 children who attended school between 2009 and 2013, 7,413 (1.0 percent, 84.8 percent boys) were dispensed medication approved solely for treating ADHD, the authors' marker of the label. The authors report that after adjustment for sociodemographic, maternity and comorbidity factors these medicated children had more unauthorised absence (incidence rate ratio 1.16) and exclusion from school (5.79), more often a record of special educational need (odds ratio 8.62), lower attainment (odds ratio 3.35), more often left school before age 16 (64.3 against 28.4 percent), were more often unemployed after leaving (odds ratio 1.39), and were more often admitted to hospital overall (hazard ratio 1.25) and for injury (1.52).

3108.content: In a historical review, Gunderson reports that the label 'borderline' arose under psychoanalysis for patients thought to sit at the border of schizophrenia, and stayed a rarely and inconsistently used term until the 1970s. He reports that Kernberg defined borderline personality organisation in 1967, that criteria in the 1970s made the syndrome reliably assessable, and that the label entered DSM-III in 1980 as borderline personality disorder. He writes that at that point the validity of the label rested mainly, and precariously, on its clinical usefulness in predicting a set of problems clinicians met with these patients.

Gunderson writes that patients given the borderline label attracted pejorative descriptions in the 1970s literature, quoting them as 'fickle, egocentric, irresponsible, love-intoxicated' and 'intractable, unruly', and that in retrospect the failures of psychoanalytic therapies were explained solely by the labelled patients' own motivations. He describes the label, from the review's start, as a suspect category largely neglected by psychiatric institutions and given to patients few clinicians want to treat.

3109.content: In a Dutch multicentre randomised non-inferiority trial, 249 adults with three or more past episodes classified as major depression by DSM-IV criteria, in full or partial remission and on maintenance antidepressants for 6 months or more, all took an 8-week group course of mindfulness-based cognitive therapy; 128 were then asked to taper off the antidepressant over 5 weeks under a psychiatrist and 121 stayed on it. Over 15 months, 54 percent of the taper group (69 of 128) and 39 percent of the stay group (47 of 121) met SCID interview criteria for relapse or recurrence, which failed the trial's non-inferiority margin, and time to relapse was shorter after tapering (hazard ratio 1.59). Depression severity scores over the 15 months differed little between the groups, with a small difference at 3 months around the time of stopping, and quality of life did not differ.

In the same trial the authors report that only 53 percent of the taper group followed the discontinuation protocol, against 75 and 71 percent in two earlier trials by Kuyken and colleagues, that many participants and their psychiatrists were reluctant to stop, and that the class was given in mixed groups with patients who were not stopping, so participants may have lacked support or been discouraged from stopping. They also report that withdrawal effects of antidepressants may be misread as signs of relapse.

3110.content: Abstract only. In a historical essay, one of whose authors was a member of the group, Kendler, Munoz and Murphy report that a discussion group at Washington University, begun in 1967 at the urging of the resident John Feighner and led by Eli Robins, set out to review past contributions to psychiatric diagnosis and within a year turned to writing new diagnostic criteria, published in 1972. They report that the Feighner criteria were soon widely cited and used in research and formed the basis of the Research Diagnostic Criteria, which were central to DSM-III. The authors name three contributions: operationalized criteria, a renewed emphasis on illness course and outcome, and basing criteria on empirical evidence whenever possible.

3111.content: Abstract only. A meta-analysis of eight follow-up studies found by searches from 1980 to 2005, together comprising 1,179 patients diagnosed with borderline personality disorder, counted 94 deaths by suicide. Set against national suicide rates for the same age groups, years and countries, every study found suicide more frequent among the diagnosed patients than in the general population, and the authors report that suicide appeared more frequent in the first phases of follow-up than in later, chronic phases.

3112.content: Abstract only. In a literature review of studies on how mental health clinicians perceive and react to patients diagnosed with borderline personality disorder, the authors found psychiatric nurses were the group studied most, then mixed samples of clinicians, then psychologists, and no study of psychiatrists alone. Sample sizes were generally small and methods varied, and the overwhelming majority of the studies reported negative perceptions of and emotional responses toward patients with this diagnosis. The authors read this as a human reaction to the patients' behaviour, and they note that other researchers read it as prejudice.

3113.content: The authors re-scored the personality disorder interview of the US National Epidemiologic Survey on Alcohol and Related Conditions (wave 1 2001-2002, 43,093 adults; wave 2 2004-2005, 87% retained), counting a DSM-IV criterion toward a diagnosis only when the respondent said that item had brought trouble or problems. Under this rule the share of US adults meeting the criteria for any personality disorder diagnosis fell from 21.5% to 9.1%, and for borderline personality disorder from 5.9% to 2.7% (Table 1). The original survey rule had required only one of the endorsed items to bring problems.

In the same re-scored US survey, the borderline personality disorder label was met significantly more often by women than by men under both scoring rules: 6.16% of women and 5.59% of men under the original rule (odds ratio for men 0.90, 95% CI 0.86 to 0.94), and 3.02% of women and 2.44% of men under the revised rule (odds ratio 0.80, 95% CI 0.75 to 0.86) (Table 2). The difference is small in size and reaches significance in a very large sample.

3114.content: Among 34,481 US adults in wave 2 of the National Epidemiologic Survey on Alcohol and Related Conditions, scored with the stricter rule that every counted criterion must bring problems, an estimated 2.7% met the criteria for borderline personality disorder (95% CI 2.5 to 3.0): 3.0% of women and 2.4% of men. Rates were higher among adults with family income under $20,000 a year (4.8%), adults under 30 (4.3%) and adults who were separated, divorced or widowed (4.5%).

In the same US survey, 74.9% of the adults who met borderline personality disorder criteria reported having gone to a physician, therapist, counselor or other professional for mental health concerns, and 63.1% reported having been prescribed medication for mental health concerns. Women reported slightly more treatment use, a difference that was not significant.

3115.content: Abstract only. Four authors describe the change in the WHO's ICD-11 classification of the personality disorder labels: the separate personality disorder categories were replaced by one dimensional diagnosis, given in two steps, one of five levels of severity and then up to five prominent trait domains. The working group argued that only a dimensional system fitted the evidence. Those who wanted the borderline category kept resisted, and after long discussion a 'borderline pattern' descriptor was added as an option chosen after severity is set.

3116.content: Abstract only. In public goods experiments (members choose how much to contribute to a good shared by the group), the authors varied two things separately: the number of people in the group and the return each member gets from each token put in. Contributions to the shared good fell when a larger group came with a lower return per token; a larger group with the same return per token did not lower giving.

3117.content: Abstract only. Recording with tungsten microelectrodes from the supraorbital nerve of the forehead in humans, Nordin identified eleven nerve units with unmyelinated (C) fibres (conduction 0.6 to 1.4 m/s). Eight had low touch thresholds (0.23 g or less) and fired at up to about 100 impulses per second to weak touch; slow stroking, even with cotton wool, was a particularly effective stimulus and rapid stroking reduced the response. Three had high thresholds and answered only to painful stimuli. The author states these low-threshold C units had all the main features of the C mechanoreceptors known from the cat and other primates but not previously proven to exist in man.

3118.content: Abstract only. In two studies the authors tested whether obesity sets off the mind's pathogen-avoidance responses. In study 1, people who were chronically more concerned about catching diseases from others held more negative attitudes toward obese people, most of all after they had seen pictures of obese individuals. In study 2, obesity was implicitly associated with disease-related concepts, most of all when the threat of pathogen transmission had been made salient. The authors conclude that pathogen detection is hypersensitive and appears to play a part in the stigma against obese people.

3119.content: University students in Ghana (103, 57 women), a country with a long history of high infectious disease, scored higher than students in Philadelphia, USA (96, 58 women) on disgust and contamination scales: Disgust Scale Revised d = 0.49, pathogen disgust d = 0.72, moral disgust d = 0.59, the contamination items of the Padua Inventory d = 0.92 and germ aversion d = 0.97. Of the three standard disgust subscales, only contamination disgust differed between the countries (d = 1.29); core disgust (d = 0.22) and animal-reminder disgust (d = 0.22) did not differ significantly. Perceived infectability did not differ.

In the same study, contamination sensitivity (Padua Inventory contamination items) accounted statistically for the country difference in overall disgust: the country effect on the Disgust Scale Revised fell from beta = 0.312 to 0.003 once contamination scores were added (Sobel z = 5.16, p < 0.001), and the country effect on pathogen disgust roughly halved (0.760 to 0.357).

3120.content: Abstract only. People shown disgusting material, compared with neutral and negative-emotion control groups, showed an oral inflammatory response: salivary tumour necrosis factor alpha and albumin rose and secretion of salivary immunoglobulin A fell; the control groups showed no such change. The authors read the inflammatory response as a response to disease threat selectively set off by disgust.

3121.content: Abstract only. Healthy men were randomly assigned to view food-disgust, non-food-disgust, food-control or negative-emotion images. Disgust raised core body temperature relative to the negative-emotion control, as did food images, and disgust also raised salivary tumour necrosis factor alpha and albumin relative to the control conditions. The type of disgust made little difference.

3122.content: Abstract only. In the Flemish Gut Flora Project, a population sample of 1,054 people in Flanders, Belgium, with checks in independent data sets of 1,070 people in total, butyrate-producing Faecalibacterium and Coprococcus bacteria were consistently associated with higher scores on quality-of-life measures. Coprococcus and Dialister were depleted in people the authors classed as depressed, also after the authors corrected for antidepressant use. The gut bacteria's potential to make a dopamine breakdown product (3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetic acid) went with better mental quality of life.

3123.content: In a lab experiment in the Netherlands, 39 adults (mean age 35.7, 21 women) watched a frightening film next to a small humanoid robot (Aldebaran Nao, steered from a control room) that spoke soothing words; 20 randomly assigned participants also got a touch of the robot's hand on the shoulder with the words, 19 did not. The film raised arousal, but the robot's touch changed none of the measures: heart rate and its variability, skin conductance, cortisol, breathing rate and reported stress, dislike of the film, how the robot was seen, and money given to charity at the robot's request.

3124.content: Abstract only. In this paper, which reports the positional cloning of the obese (ob) gene in the mouse (Mus musculus) and its human homologue, the authors state that mutation of ob in mice results in profound obesity and type II diabetes, a syndrome that resembles morbid obesity in humans. They propose that the ob gene product works as part of a signalling pathway from fat tissue that regulates the size of the body's fat store.

3125.content: Abstract only. In 24-hour dietary recalls from 40,937 US adults (over 19 years) across nine waves of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, ultra-processed food rose from 53.5% to 57.0% of daily calories between 2001-2002 and 2017-2018, after adjusting for changes in the population, and rose in every subgroup except Hispanic adults. Minimally processed food fell from 32.7% to 27.4% of calories over the same years, in every subgroup.

3126.content: In one-day 24-hour dietary recalls from 9,317 people aged 1 year and over in the 2009-2010 US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, ultra-processed foods supplied 57.9% of energy intake and 89.7% of the energy from added sugars. Ultra-processed foods held 21.1% of their calories as added sugar, against 2.4% in processed foods and 3.7% in unprocessed or minimally processed foods and culinary ingredients together. Added sugar rose from 7.5% of energy in the fifth of people eating the least ultra-processed food to 19.5% in the fifth eating the most.

3127.content: From national time-use surveys converted to energy cost (MET hours a week, adults), Ng and Popkin estimate that total physical activity from work, home tasks, travel and active leisure fell in the US from 235 MET hours a week in 1965 to 160 in 2009, and in the UK from 216 in 1961 to 173 in 2005 (20% lower). The losses came from work, home and travel; active leisure rose only slightly and did not make up for them, while sedentary leisure time grew.

In China, from the China Health and Nutrition Surveys (1991 to 2009), adults' total physical activity from work, home tasks, travel and active leisure fell from about 399 to 213 MET hours a week, mostly through less movement at work and at home and in travel, as people moved out of farming into factory and service work. Of the five countries studied (US, UK, Brazil, China, India), China and Brazil showed the steepest declines; India showed the least.

3128.content: In a double-blind trial at Emory University, 60 medically stable outpatients diagnosed with major depression that had not responded to antidepressants were randomised to three infusions of the TNF-alpha blocker infliximab (5 mg/kg, n = 30) or placebo (n = 30) over 12 weeks. Scores on the 17-item Hamilton depression scale fell no more with infliximab than with placebo overall. Baseline C-reactive protein, a blood marker of inflammation, changed the result: above 5 mg/L infliximab did better than placebo (3.1 points more improvement, standardised effect +0.41; response 62% against 33%, 8 of 13 against 3 of 9, p = 0.19), and at 5 mg/L or below placebo did better (standardised effect 0.82 in favour of placebo; response 41% against 57%).

In the same trial, among patients with C-reactive protein above 5 mg/L, the symptoms that improved more with infliximab than with placebo were loss of pleasure and drive, slowed movement, low mood, worry and suicidal thoughts. Higher baseline C-reactive protein went with a weaker response to placebo (placebo non-responders 7.8 mg/L against responders 3.1 mg/L, p = 0.12, not significant).

3129.content: Using police reports of family violence from over 750 US city and county police agencies (National Incident-Based Reporting System, 1995 to 2006) matched to Sunday regular-season games of six NFL teams, and holding the bookmakers' pre-game point spread and the local TV audience constant, the authors find that upset losses (defeats when the home team was predicted to win by 4 or more points) lead to about a 10% rise in at-home violence by men against their wives and girlfriends. Losses in games expected to be close had small and non-significant effects, and upset wins had little effect.

In the same data, the rise in violence after an upset loss was concentrated in the hours around the end of the game, and was larger when the game mattered more: about 20% after an upset loss to a traditional rival against 8% for other teams (p = 0.01 for the difference), and 15% after an upset loss in a frustrating game (many sacks, turnovers or penalty yards) against 7% otherwise.

3130.content: Abstract only. In two experiments on the illusory truth effect (repeated statements are judged more true than new ones), repetition raised the rated truth of false statements even when participants knew the correct answer, as shown both by normed estimates of what people know and by each participant's own answers on a knowledge check after the experiment. Modelling in the second experiment indicated that participants sometimes rely on the ease of processing a repeated statement even when the relevant knowledge is available to them.

3131.content: Abstract only. In 92 pregnant women, studied by a team at the University of Wroclaw, Poland, who answered the Disgust Scale-Revised in each trimester, total disgust and core disgust were highest in the first trimester, when the authors say maternal immune suppression is also highest, and fell over pregnancy in women carrying daughters. Women carrying sons kept relatively high disgust through the first and second trimesters.

3132.content: In 94 pregnant women in Prague who answered the Czech Disgust Scale-Revised in each trimester and after birth, a replication of the earlier longitudinal study did not find disgust highest in the first trimester: overall disgust and animal-reminder disgust (wounds, blood, death) were lowest in the first trimester and higher in the second trimester and after birth, while core and contamination disgust did not change significantly. Results on fetal sex were mixed.

In the same study, women who reported recent health problems in the first trimester scored higher on core disgust at that time (22 women, mean 29.1, against 25.1 for the 70 without; F = 6.40, p = 0.013) and on contamination disgust, a pattern the authors read as disgust rising when protection against infection is more needed.

3133.content: Across up to 98 world regions (mostly countries), an index of historical pathogen load correlated with four published survey measures of individualism and collectivism: regions with more pathogens scored as more collectivist and less individualist (absolute r 0.63 to 0.73 for historical pathogen load, all p < 0.001; for example r = -0.69 with Hofstede's individualism across 68 regions). Pathogen load still carried unique weight when GDP per head and the Gini index were entered with it, and the pattern held with 6 or 10 broad world regions as the unit.

3134.content: In a nonclinical sample of 120 naturally cycling women, salivary progesterone correlated with how strongly the women reported emotions, thoughts and behaviours of disease avoidance, as the authors' compensatory behavioral prophylaxis hypothesis expected.

3135.content: Reanalysing public goods games in which 240 subjects were randomly regrouped with strangers each round, under strict anonymity, the authors found that each money unit a group member contributed was followed by the focal subject contributing 0.19 more units in the next round with new partners (0.18 in the version with punishment), 0.07 more two rounds later from a person two steps away whom the subject never saw (0.05 with punishment), and 0.06 more from three steps away in the punishment version. By their estimate one extra unit given in the first round was tripled across the group over the experiment.

3136.content: From 11th-century trade records and a simple game model, Greif argued that the Maghribi traders could employ overseas agents despite the risk of being cheated, through a coalition of traders that shared information about agents and so let a reputation mechanism govern the relationships.

3137.content: Rereading the evidence offered for the Maghribi traders' coalition, Edwards and Ogilvie found that not one cited example shows the coalition existed; the traders used the formal legal system to enforce agency agreements and combined reputation-based sanctions with courts, much as medieval European merchants did.

3138.content: In an experiment where participants could choose between a group with a sanctioning institution and a sanction-free group, the sanctioning group was avoided at first, yet over the rounds the entire population moved into it and cooperated strongly, while the sanction-free group emptied completely.

3139.content: Across up to 122 countries and three measures of in-group preference (strength of family ties, collectivism, in-group favoritism), the effectiveness of government institutions correlated with less favoring of in-group members, and the association held after controlling for pathogen stress and world region, in checks on reverse causality over 13 years, and in an instrumental variable analysis. In countries where government services are less likely to meet basic needs, people invested more in family and in-group members.

When world region was controlled, none of the associations between the three main in-group preference measures and non-zoonotic pathogen stress stayed significant; with government effectiveness in the model, pathogen stress went with only two of three main measures and two of five alternative ones.

3140.content: In 375 heterosexual women not using hormonal contraception, tested in up to three blocks of five weekly sessions (337 completed five or more), within-woman changes in salivary progesterone, estradiol, testosterone and cortisol did not track changes in pathogen disgust on the Three Domain Disgust Scale (progesterone estimate 0.32, p = .46). Sexual and moral disgust did not track the hormones either, and the between-women correlation of progesterone and pathogen disgust at the first session was also null.

3141.content: In economic game experiments that tested their costly-signalling model, people who paid to punish selfishness toward someone else were trusted more, and behaved in a more trustworthy way, than people who did not punish. When a more informative signal was available (the chance to help directly), people punished less and punishment became a weaker signal of trustworthiness, while costly helping stayed a strong and much used signal.

3142.content: In one experiment, memory for the source of names (whether a name had been linked to cheating, trustworthy or irrelevant behaviour) was better for names linked to cheating, while plain recognition of whether a name had been seen before did not differ by behaviour. The authors note this pattern repeats their earlier results with faces and read it as a general bias to remember the source of information about cheating, not a face-specific cheater-detection module.

3143.content: In two studies, participants who had recently been ill paid more attention to disfigured faces (Study 1) and avoided disfigured individuals more (Study 2) than participants who had not recently been ill; the authors read this as the biological immune system switching on the behavioral immune system.

3144.content: A preregistered direct replication of Miller and Maner's Study 1, with identical task and code, tested 402 participants at universities in Michigan, Glasgow and Amsterdam (151 recently ill, 251 not), more than four times the original 96. Recently ill participants showed no greater attentional bias toward disfigured faces, and an equivalence test rejected an effect as large as the one the original design could detect (dz = -0.14, 90% CI -0.31 to -0.04, against a bound of 0.35). Illness recency also did not go with germ aversion, pathogen disgust or disgust ratings of infection images.

3145.content: A review of disease avoidance and stigma reports a study (Park, Faulkner and Schaller 2003) in which people with physical disabilities were more often associated with disease than people without, and this association was stronger among people more sensitive to disgust or more concerned about catching disease. The review also reports that healthy people describe disgust at visible physical abnormalities.

3146.content: Patient R.M., with bilateral damage to medial orbitofrontal cortex and the anterior temporal poles that disconnected both amygdalae, solved 70% of precaution problems on the Wason selection task and 38.9% of matched social-contract (cheater-detection) problems, a 31-point gap against a 1.2-point mean gap in 37 control subjects; two other patients with overlapping but different damage showed no such gap. His family reported he does not notice when someone takes advantage of him.

3147.content: In 11,501 adults surveyed in 30 nations, people in nations with higher historical parasite stress endorsed traditional norms more (national means correlated r = 0.70 with parasite stress) and scored no higher on social dominance orientation (r = -0.06). Within nations, individual pathogen disgust sensitivity went with traditionalism (meta-analysed r = 0.10, 95% CI 0.07 to 0.12) and barely with social dominance orientation (r = 0.04).

In the same 30-nation survey, nations differed in average pathogen disgust sensitivity, but this variation was unrelated to national parasite stress (national correlation r = 0.18, multilevel t(26.18) = 1.12, P = 0.27): people living in more pathogen-dense countries were not more disgust-sensitive. Women scored consistently higher than men across nations (meta-analysed d = 0.41).

3148.content: Across three experiments, people who had acted in synchrony with others cooperated more in later group economic exercises, including ones that required personal sacrifice; positive emotions did not need to arise for the effect to appear, and the authors read it as synchrony strengthening attachment to the group.

3149.content: In his own account of the 2013 field study in Mauritius, Xygalatas reports that Tamil Hindu devotees and attendees donated significantly more money to charity after the high-intensity Thaipusam kavadi ritual (body piercing, hours of carrying a heavy kavadi, 242 steps up to the temple) than after a low-intensity ritual at the same temple, that merely attending the kavadi was enough to raise giving, and that the more pain participants had experienced, the more generous they were toward the community.

3150.content: In annual US telephone surveys of 18,986 night-time caregivers of infants under 7 months (about 1,000 a year), 11% reported that the infant usually shared a bed; the share rose from 6.0% in 1993 to 13.5% in 2010. Among White families the rise stopped after 2000, while among Black and Hispanic families it continued through 2010; in 2010, 39.6% of Black mothers reported usual bed-sharing, and Black infants were 3.5 times as likely as White infants to usually bed-share (adjusted odds ratio).

Thirty-six percent of caregivers in the same survey had talked to a doctor about bed-sharing. Compared with those who had not, caregivers who reported a doctor with a negative attitude toward bed-sharing were less likely to bed-share (adjusted odds ratio 0.66), while those who reported a neutral doctor were more likely to (adjusted odds ratio 1.4).

3151.content: In two online samples (554 Mechanical Turk adults on romantic relationships; 747 Prolific adults on romantic relationships and friendships), people with stronger destiny beliefs about relationships (a relationship is meant to be or not) felt more positive about ghosting, ending a relationship by cutting off all contact, intended to use it more, and were more likely to have used it before; people with stronger growth beliefs showed the opposite pattern for acceptability and intentions.

3152.content: In a qualitative study of 99 emerging adults about ghosting, the majority reported having taken part in it both as the one who ghosted and as the one ghosted; the authors describe five themes for why initiators chose ghosting, three for how they decided, and three for how the ghosted person realised it had happened.

3153.content: Using WHO 2008 country data on how many adults do not meet activity recommendations and pooled relative risks from prospective cohort studies, Lee and colleagues estimate that physical inactivity accounts for 6 percent of the worldwide burden of coronary heart disease (3.2 percent in South-east Asia to 7.8 percent in the Eastern Mediterranean region), 7 percent of type 2 diabetes, 10 percent of breast cancer and 10 percent of colon cancer, and for 9 percent of premature mortality, more than 5.3 of the 57 million deaths worldwide in 2008.

In the same analysis, removing physical inactivity would raise the life expectancy of the world's population by an estimated 0.68 years (0.41 years in South-east Asia to 0.95 in the Eastern Mediterranean region). The authors compare this with smoking and obesity and conclude that inactivity has an impact comparable to either.

3154.content: Abstract only. Maltby, Houran and McCutcheon gave the Celebrity Attitude Scale and a short Eysenck personality questionnaire to convenience samples of 317 students and 290 community respondents. They report that celebrity worship is not uncommon, and that their correlations fit the predicted pattern: the entertainment-social level went with extraversion, the intense-personal level with neuroticism, and the borderline-pathological level with the trait the questionnaire scores as psychoticism, as the authors label the three levels.

3155.content: Combining tax, survey and national accounts data to cover 100 percent of US national income, Piketty, Saez and Zucman find that the bottom half of adults saw its share of pretax national income fall from about 20 percent in 1980 to 12 percent in 2014, while the top 1 percent's share rose from about 12 to 20 percent. In 1980 the top 1 percent earned on average 27 times as much as the bottom half before tax; in 2014, 81 times.

In the same accounts, average pretax income of the bottom half of US adults stayed at about 16,000 dollars a year (2014 dollars) from 1980 to 2014 while average national income per adult grew 60 percent to 64,500 dollars. After taxes and transfers, working-age adults in the bottom half still saw close to zero growth over the period; the authors find that transfers went mostly to the elderly and the middle class.

3156.content: Abstract only. In a placebo-controlled crossover study, 40 healthy volunteers given intranasal oxytocin or placebo viewed faces with different expressions while receiving gentle human touch or machine touch on the skin. Smiling faces made the touch that came with them feel more pleasant and frowning faces made it feel less pleasant, the latter more so for human touch than machine touch. Oxytocin did not change how pleasant the touch felt. Pupils widened more to human touch than to equally intense machine touch, most of all with a smiling face.

Abstract only. In the same experiment, after intranasal oxytocin, gentle human touch (compared with machine touch) sharpened how participants judged the faces: frowning faces were rated less friendly and attractive and smiling faces more friendly and attractive.

3157.content: Abstract only. In latent profile analyses of three non-clinical samples (14,006, 483 and 672 people, recruited from general websites and a pornography site), three profiles came out in every sample: low-frequency use without problems (68 to 73 percent), high-frequency use without problems (19 to 29 percent) and high-frequency use with problems as scored on a problematic-use scale (3 to 8 percent). People with high-frequency use and no problems outnumbered those with problematic high-frequency use 3 to 6 times. The two high-frequency groups differed in reported hypersexuality, depressive symptoms, boredom proneness, self-esteem, uncomfortable feelings about pornography and basic psychological needs.

3158.content: Abstract only. Across six studies, the Three Domains of Disgust Scale split into the same three factors, pathogen, sexual and moral disgust: by principal components in 206 people (with good reliability, including retest over 12 weeks) and by confirmatory factor analysis in 406 more. The pathogen and sexual subscales tracked other measures of disgust and contamination and only weakly tracked negative mood. The moral subscale did less well: in 70 people it showed no consistent link with moral attitudes, and in 178 people answers to the moral items were stronger when the response option was anger than when it was disgust.

3159.content: In the preregistered International Sex Survey (82,243 people in 42 countries on five continents, 26 languages, mean age 32.4), 3.2 percent of participants scored as at risk of problematic pornography use on the long Problematic Pornography Consumption Scale; across the three measures the authors tested, the at-risk share ran from 3.2 to 16.6 percent depending on the measure. Men reported the highest levels, shares differed between countries, and there were no differences by sexual orientation. Only 4 to 10 percent of those at risk had ever sought treatment; another 21 to 37 percent wanted to but did not, for reasons such as cost.

3160.content: From OECD data, the mean age of women at first birth rose by about one year per decade across OECD countries from the 1970s, and in Europe and Japan by about four years, from 25 in 1970 to 29 in 2008; the United States changed least (1.5 years). The authors write that European women have never had their first births so late, with many countries near an average of 30.

In a PRISMA-guided review of the demographic, social science and medical literature, the authors name as the central reasons for later first births the rise of effective contraception, women's rising education and paid work, value change, gender equity, changes in partnerships, housing conditions, economic uncertainty and the absence of supportive family policies. They report that some social policies can counter postponement.

The review reports Leridon's (2008) estimates that the share of women who are sterile rises from 1 percent at 25 to 5 percent at 35, 17 percent at 40 and up to 55 percent at 45; under natural conditions 75 percent of women trying to conceive at 30 have a conception ending in a live birth within a year, 66 percent at 35 and 44 percent at 40.

3161.content: Reviewing a decade of US research, Raley and Sweeney report that nearly half of US marriages are expected to end in divorce or separation, that the annual divorce rate fell from its 1980 peak of 22.8 per 1,000 married women to 16.7 in 2016, and that divorce among Americans aged 50 and over doubled between 1990 and 2010. Divorce by age 46 runs from about 21 percent of men and 32 percent of women with a bachelor's degree to 44 percent of men and 52 percent of women without a high school diploma.

In the same review, 7.5 percent of US children under 18 (5.6 million) lived with a married or cohabiting stepparent in 2009, against 7.0 percent in 1991; about 1.7 percent lived with a stepsibling and 10.8 percent with a half-sibling. Remarriage rates have declined, but the share of marriages that are remarriages is rising, and the review reports that step-relationships are generally less close than biological ones, with wide variation.

3162.content: In an online survey of 328 Dutch-speaking adults who had used a dating app (63 percent women, 86 percent heterosexual, mean age 31.7), recruited through newspaper and magazine outlets, 279 (85 percent) said they had been ghosted on an app, cut off without explanation, and 173 (63 percent) said they had ghosted someone themselves.

In the same survey, 94 of the people who described being ghosted (44 percent, as the authors give it) reported long-term effects on their mental health, mostly lowered self-esteem (89 people), distrust of others (20) and, for 3, depression and panic attacks as they reported them. Ghosting was rated more painful the more often it had happened, the longer the contact had lasted, when the pair had met face to face and when it came unexpectedly (the model explained 48.6 percent of the variance).

3163.content: In four samples, quota samples of US adults (1,321) and Danish adults (2,005) matched to the population by YouGov, a lab study of 42 Danish students with a physiological measure, and 1,076 white Americans on MTurk, people more sensitive to contamination disgust opposed immigration more. The link held after education, income, ideology and personality were controlled, was about as large as that of education, and also appeared with an unobtrusive physiological response to disgusting images. A meta-analysis of the 16 earlier articles on the link found them underpowered and showing signs of publication bias.

In a randomised experiment in the MTurk sample (1,037 people), all read a story of a hospital orderly cleaning up vomit; half then read that he carefully washed his hands. The hand-washing cue cut the link between disgust sensitivity and opposition to immigration by 47 percent. In the Danish sample, people high in contamination disgust disapproved more of close contact with immigrants and approved more of immigrants choosing to keep apart, which the authors read as avoidance rather than a wish to harm.

3164.content: Abstract only. 94 participants were randomly assigned to have disgust, sadness or a neutral state induced, and then took an implicit association test pairing animals with an arbitrary outgroup made by a minimal-groups procedure. All groups showed some dehumanizing bias, but the disgusted participants most strongly associated the outgroup with animals (and the ingroup with humanity); the sad and neutral groups did not differ.

3165.content: Abstract only. In a prospective study of a representative birth cohort, Caspi and colleagues reported that people carrying one or two short copies of the serotonin transporter promoter variant (5-HTT) had more depressive symptoms, more diagnosed depression and more suicidality after stressful life events than people with two long copies. Later preregistered tests in far larger samples did not repeat this interaction.

3166.content: Abstract only. In an fMRI study, 10 participants viewed 48 photographs of social groups (and 12 viewed objects), each picture standing for one cell of the warmth by competence grid of the stereotype content model. The medial prefrontal cortex, needed for social cognition, responded to every social group except the groups seen as both cold and incompetent, such as addicts and homeless people; these instead drew insula and amygdala activity, a pattern the authors read as disgust.

3167.content: Abstract only. In focus groups (25 people) and interviews (26), Hayes, Carr and Wohn asked why people use one-click cues such as Likes and Favorites and how they read them when they receive them. They report that such clicks do more than keep a channel open, and may say as much about the relationship between sender and receiver as about the content clicked.

3168.content: Abstract only. Sensitivity to interpersonal disgust (for example not wanting to wear clean used clothes or sit on a seat still warm from a stranger) went with more negative attitudes toward immigrants, foreigners and socially deviant groups, even with concern about catching disease controlled. In a path model the link to attitudes toward immigrants ran indirectly, through social dominance orientation, right-wing authoritarianism and seeing the out-group as less human.

3169.content: Abstract only. In three studies, disgust, and not anger, sadness or fear, went with harsher moral judgment of acts that violate purity and more approval of acts that uphold it, and not with judgments about justice or harm and care. Study 1 measured felt disgust, Study 2 induced disgust against induced sadness, and Study 3 measured trait disgust. Across studies, people of lower socioeconomic status moralized purity more.

3170.content: Among 181 US adults from an online panel drawn mainly from the four 2004 swing states, scores on the 8-item short Disgust Sensitivity Scale went with rating oneself as more politically conservative (standardised beta 0.22, about 5% of the variance), and the link held with religious affiliation in the model (beta 0.23). A pilot with 82 University of California Irvine undergraduates found the same correlation (r = .29). In Study 2, among 84 Cornell undergraduates who took the full 32-item scale, disgust sensitivity went with placing oneself further to the right (beta 0.27) and with more conservative answers on gay marriage (beta 0.35), abortion (beta 0.36) and, unexpectedly, tax cuts (beta 0.39), and with none of the other seven issues (affirmative action, the Iraq war, unions, the death penalty and others), though every sign pointed the same way.

3171.content: In a US online sample of 1,971 adults who took brief implicit association tests, the gap between Democrats and Republicans in automatic liking for their own party (Cohen's d 0.95) was larger than the gap between Black and white Americans in automatic racial preference (d 0.61). The authors read this as partisan animosity being at least as automatic as racial animosity.

In an experiment with 1,021 US adults asked to pick one of two graduating high school seniors for a scholarship, about 80% of Democrats and Republicans chose the candidate of their own party, and academic qualifications did not change this: a partisan's chance of picking the other party's candidate never rose above 0.3, even when that candidate had the better grades. In the parallel race task, only African American participants favoured their own race (73.1%), and white participants slightly favoured the African American candidate (55.8%).

3172.content: In anonymous online experiments with Amazon Mechanical Turk workers (8,440 people across the outrage studies), people reported more outrage at another person's selfishness when they had no chance to show their own trustworthiness by sharing with a third party, and mediation analyses suggest that the chance to share lowered outrage through reputation concerns. In costly punishment experiments (6,076 people) they punished more when sharing was not possible. The authors read this as reputation concerns shaping outrage even when nobody is watching, through a habit of acting as if reputation were at stake.

3173.content: In a PET study with [11C]raclopride, 16 people the authors diagnosed as pathological gamblers and 15 healthy controls played the Iowa Gambling Task. Those labelled pathological gamblers who lost money showed significantly more dopamine release in the left ventral striatum than the controls; when either group won money, dopamine release did not differ. The authors suggest this may underlie chasing losses.

3174.content: Across four studies (online samples of 201, 819 and 347 adults recruited mainly through Amazon Mechanical Turk, and 1,252 adults in the United States and Canada reporting real moral events by smartphone over three days), anger rose and disgust fell when a moral violation hit the person themself rather than someone else. In the scenario studies, anger went with wanting high-cost direct aggression (hitting, insulting, yelling at the wrongdoer) and disgust did not, while disgust went with wanting low-cost indirect aggression (excluding the wrongdoer, spreading bad information about them) and anger did not. The results held with trait aggression and trait disgust controlled.

3175.content: Students in the United States and Japan read descriptions of moral violations and matched each to one of six facial expressions or to a word (contempt, anger, disgust, or their translations). The results generally matched the authors' proposed mapping: anger to violations of individual rights (autonomy), contempt to violations of communal codes including hierarchy (community), and disgust to violations of purity and sanctity (divinity). Facial expressions Americans actually made while reading the descriptions gave the same picture.

3176.content: In four small experiments (127 Stanford students near a bin sprayed with a fart spray, 43 University of Virginia students in a dirty room, 69 and 133 University of Plymouth students who recalled a disgusting event or watched a disgusting film), induced disgust made moral judgments harsher than in control groups. In Experiments 2 to 4 the effect held only for people high in private body consciousness (attention to their own bodily sensations), and in the dirty-room experiment the manipulation did not raise self-rated disgust.

3177.content: In two large studies (1,412 people in total), inducing disgust did not make moral judgments harsher, and neither sensitivity to bodily states nor the accessibility of mood changed that. The authors conclude the studies do not support large effects of induced disgust or of these two moderators.

3178.content: In two studies, meaning in life statistically mediated the link between religiousness and life satisfaction (Study 1A) and between religiousness and self-esteem and optimism (Study 1B). In an experience-sampling study (Study 2), meaning in life also mediated the link between daily religious behaviours and well-being on the same days.

3179.content: A meta-analysis of 24 studies found that people with a stronger behavioural immune system, measured as disgust sensitivity, fear of contamination or perceived vulnerability to disease, scored higher on social conservatism (right-wing authoritarianism, social dominance orientation, religious fundamentalism, ethnocentrism, collectivism and political conservatism). Summary correlations ranged from 0.24 to 0.31 across models; a trim-and-fill correction for missing studies lowered the corrected estimate from 0.31 to 0.25. Brief self-placement measures of political conservatism (one item in one study, four similar items in the other) gave the weakest links (0.03 and 0.06 in two studies), which the authors put down to those items mixing social and economic views.

3180.content: In two dictator-game experiments with Hokkaido University students in Japan (84 and 142 people), participants were sorted into trivial minimal groups and gave money to an anonymous recipient who did not know the giver's group. With a plain desktop, they gave no more to their own group's members than to the other group's. With a painting of eyes on the screen, they did: in Experiment 1, 64.3% chose an equal split for an in-group recipient against 42.9% for an out-group recipient, and in Experiment 2 the eyes raised giving to in-group members only. The authors read this as favouritism toward one's own group running on expected reputation and indirect return from that group, the bounded generalized reciprocity model.

3181.content: A systematic review of 69 national adult gambling prevalence surveys from 30 countries (2000 to 2015; 46 in Europe, 10 in Asia, 5 in Oceania, 4 in Africa, 3 in North America, 1 in South America) found past-year rates of problem gambling, as scored on screens such as the SOGS, PGSI and DSM-IV criteria, from 0.12% to 5.8% worldwide; by continent, 2% to 5% in North America, 0.5% to 5.8% in Asia, 0.4% to 0.7% in Oceania and 0.1% to 3.4% in Europe. The authors say direct comparison is hard, as the surveys used different instruments, cut-offs and time frames. In most European surveys, problem gambling scores were higher among men, single or divorced people, younger people, people with less education, ethnic minorities or people born abroad, and the unemployed or those on low incomes.

In the national surveys reviewed, the most common forms of gambling were lotteries, scratch cards, sports betting and gambling machines, but the forms most played by those scoring as problem gamblers were slot machines and internet gambling games. The authors link this to games with high event frequency and a short interval between stake and payout, and call for policies on the availability of such machines.

3182.content: A narrative review of the literature from 1994 to 2013 reports that representative surveys gave prevalence estimates of compulsive buying, as defined by the authors' cited criteria (a preoccupation with buying, frequent buying episodes or overpowering urges to buy felt as irresistible and senseless), of 6% to 7%, that younger people score as more prone, and that European data suggest compulsive buying rose in the adult population over the previous 20 years.

The same review reports no evidence that medication works for compulsive buying, while group cognitive behavioural therapy has been shown to be effective. Patients seeking treatment for compulsive buying are reported to carry other labels often (anxiety and depressive mood disorders, compulsive hoarding, binge eating disorder).

3183.content: On one US online dating site (eight months, June 2002 to February 2003; about 52,857 active heterosexual users with full profiles), pairs who exchanged messages shared traits more often than random pairing would give, for every trait examined. The strongest were life-course traits: marital status was the same 64% more often than chance and wanting children 54% more often, and the number of children 39% more often; physical build, smoking, self-rated looks, education, religion, race and drinking followed. Race was shared in 81.2% of pairs, only 14% above the 71.1% chance level, since 83.7% of users were white.

On the same site, 29,687 users sent 236,930 messages, and 78.2% of the 110,722 conversations were a single message that got no reply. Men started 73.3% of conversations between a man and a woman, and their first messages were answered less often than women's (20.6% against 25.1%). The number of ties per person followed a power-law spread, with many users having few contacts and a few having many.

3184.content: In two fMRI experiments with nine participants each, people judged 60 dilemmas. Dilemmas where harm is done up close and personally (such as pushing a man off a footbridge to save five) raised activity in the medial frontal gyrus, posterior cingulate and angular gyrus, areas other studies tie to emotion, and lowered activity in working-memory areas, compared with impersonal moral dilemmas (such as turning a trolley) and non-moral ones. In the personal dilemmas, people who judged the harmful act appropriate took longer to answer, which the authors read as emotion interfering with that judgment.

3185.content: In a first study, 137 Facebook users described in their own words how they used Facebook and what they enjoyed; their phrases were coded into 46 items that 241 users rated in a second study. Factor analysis gave the uses and gratifications of social connection, shared identities, content, social investigation, social network surfing and status updating (the abstract says seven and names six). Different users' demographics, visit patterns and privacy settings went with different uses.

3186.content: In an online survey of 177 adults recruited on Amazon Mechanical Turk (night-shift workers and people who said they had a sleep condition were left out), Kroese and colleagues measured bedtime procrastination, going to bed later than intended while nothing outside the person prevents going earlier, with a new 9-item scale. Higher scores went with lower self-regulation and with more insufficient sleep as they reported it, fewer hours of sleep and more daytime fatigue, over and above demographics and self-regulation; the models explained 27.1% of the variance in hours of sleep, 27.8% in fatigue and 40.9% in felt insufficient sleep. Almost 30% of the sample reported sleeping 6 hours or less on week nights.

3187.content: Abstract only. From surveys and de-identified, aggregated Facebook behaviour data, Scissors and colleagues report that people care more about who Likes their posts than how many Likes they get, and want that feedback most from close friends, romantic partners and family members other than their parents. Most people did not feel strongly that getting enough Likes matters; people with lower self-esteem and higher self-monitoring were more likely to think Likes important and to feel bad when they did not get enough.

3188.content: Abstract only. Sixty-nine online daters identified the deceptions in their own dating profiles and were photographed in the lab; independent judges rated their physical attractiveness. The less attractive the daters were rated, the more likely they were to enhance their profile photographs and to lie about height, weight and age. Attractiveness was unrelated to deception about profile items not tied to appearance, such as income and occupation, which the authors read as limited and strategic deception.

3189.content: In a survey of 1,117 people recruited offline in Sydney, Australia, and online through newsgroups and web links, participants rated 15 acts done without their partner on a 5-point scale from not infidelity to extreme infidelity. Sexual intercourse was rated highest (mean 4.74), then cybersex and hot chat with the same person regularly (4.10 and 3.94) and with strangers (3.22 to 3.89); viewing pornographic pictures, emails, videos or magazines was rated low (1.96 to 1.98), below strip clubs (2.23). A factor analysis grouped the acts into sexual infidelity (online and offline sexual acts together), emotional infidelity and pornography, so online acts did not form a category of their own.

3190.content: Using the friendship networks of 72.2 million US Facebook users aged 25 to 44 (21 billion friendships, used as a stand-in for real-world friendships), Chetty and colleagues found strong homophily by socioeconomic status: each percentile of a person's own rank went with 0.44 percentile in the mean rank of their friends. Below-median-status people had 30.2% fewer above-median-status friends than they would have if friendships formed regardless of status; in the least connected tenth of counties the shortfall was about 42%.

Across US counties, economic connectedness, twice the share of above-median-status friends among below-median-status people, was correlated 0.65 with the adult income rank of children who grew up in low-income families, while measures of network cohesiveness and civic engagement were not strongly related. Across ZIP codes the correlation was 0.69, and going from the 10th to the 90th percentile ZIP code in connectedness went with an 11-percentile higher adult income rank for low-income children.

3191.content: In a nationally representative, probability-based online survey of 1,677 US young people aged 8 to 18 in 2019, 8- to 12-year-olds used on average 4 hours 44 minutes of entertainment screen media a day and teens 7 hours 22 minutes, not counting screens used for school or homework. Among teens, 62% used more than four hours a day and 29% more than eight hours.

3192.content: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 41 studies (38 cross-sectional, 3 cohort; 41,871 children and young people, 55% female, studies from 2011 to 2017) found that a median 23.3% scored above the authors' cut-offs for problematic smartphone use on the self-report scales used. Those above the cut-offs had higher odds of reporting depression symptoms (OR 3.17, pooled from four studies with dichotomous data), anxiety, higher perceived stress (OR 1.86) and poorer sleep quality (OR 2.60) on self-report scales.

3193.content: Using the How Couples Meet and Stay Together surveys of US couples (2009 and 2017), and controlling for the diversity of local geographies, Thomas found that couples who met online were more often interracial, interreligious and of different college degree status, but more similar in age. They were no more and no less likely to cross party lines. The author's March 2018 manuscript gives sizes: on average a 6% greater probability of being interracial than couples who met offline, with over 1.5 times the odds.

Thomas estimated the population effect as small: only a small part of the recent change in couple diversity can be put down to couples meeting online. The author's March 2018 manuscript works one case: if the 28 percent of couples formed since 2009 who met online had met offline instead, about 1.7 percent fewer of all couples would be interracial.

3194.content: In a counterbalanced within-subject experiment, 25 healthy adults were tested after a normal night of sleep and after a night of total sleep deprivation. After sleep deprivation they called a heat stimulus painful at a lower temperature (mean pain threshold 42.47 against 43.89 degrees C). In fMRI, pain reactivity rose in primary somatosensory cortex and fell in the nucleus accumbens, thalamus and insula, and the rise in somatosensory reactivity went with the size of the threshold drop across people (r = 0.55). Ratings of the hottest stimuli did not change.

In a separate online study, 60 of 236 adults surveyed on Amazon Mechanical Turk (those who reported pain and had a US IP address) kept sleep diaries for two nights while sleeping as they chose; those whose sleep efficiency fell from one night to the next reported a larger rise in pain the next day than those whose sleep efficiency rose.

3195.content: 164 healthy adults aged 18 to 55 wore wrist actigraphs and kept sleep diaries for 7 days, then were quarantined and given rhinovirus by nasal drops and watched for 5 days. Of the 164, 124 (75.6%) were infected and 48 (29.3%) developed a biologically verified cold. Shorter actigraph-measured sleep went with more clinical colds: against those sleeping more than 7 hours, those sleeping under 5 hours had 4.50 times the odds (95% CI 1.08 to 18.69) and those sleeping 5 to 6 hours 4.24 times (1.08 to 16.71); 6 to 7 hours carried no clear extra risk (OR 1.66). The link held after adjusting for prior antibodies, demographics, season, body mass, psychological variables and health practices. Sleep fragmentation and diary-reported sleep were not related.

3196.content: Abstract only. 15 healthy volunteers slept in a sleep laboratory after an adaptation night on a reference night and on a night preceded by half an hour of cognitive tasks without an emotional component, in counterbalanced order. After the tasks, polysomnographic sleep onset latency was significantly longer, more high-frequency activity was recorded in the first and second deep-sleep periods, and heart rate and proximal temperature differed during and after sleep onset.

3197.content: Abstract only. Pooling data from three laboratory studies of men and women who reached orgasm by masturbation or by penile-vaginal intercourse, and adjusting for prolactin changes in a non-sexual control condition, Brody and Krüger report that the rise in prolactin after intercourse was 400% greater than after masturbation, in both sexes. They read the post-orgasm prolactin rise as an index of sexual satiety.
